On the independent Sea-Undistort dataset, sampler-aware fine-tuning improved restoration fidelity, reaching 19.469 +/- 0.332 dB PSNR and 0.554 +/- 0.005 SSIM under combined water-surface distortions, although perceptual trade-offs remained. Additional experiments on real UAV imagery examined feature preservation and segmentation behavior. These findings demonstrate the potential of semi-synthetic training and conditional diffusion for shallow-water image restoration while highlighting the importance of evaluating both reconstruction fidelity and downstream remote-sensing utility.

items.title_en: 3D Gaussian Splatting within Self-Learned Neural View-Dependent Color Fields
items.abstract_en: 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) has become a vital tool in novel view synthesis. 3D Gaussian functions with attributes like color, opacity, and scale are stacked together to explicitly model a radiance field. However, discrete 3D Gaussians usually produce poor depth with few geometry details but lots of floaters, which hinders the effective modeling of smooth radiance fields. To address this issue, we propose to learn a radiance field within a continuous view-dependent color field parameterized by neural networks. With continuous constraints in color, the bias on low-frequency signals of neural networks can highly encourage the geometry modeling to contribute to high-frequency color variations on images, getting rid of solely relying on the color attribute itself. Moreover, we impose a constraint to improve the Lipschitz continuity of the neural color field, making large changes of each Gaussian's color also match with large changes of its position in terms of a ratio. To this end, we additionally introduce novel self-learning strategies to improve the learning of the neural view-dependent color field without any external knowledge or priors, aiming for better generalization on unseen scenes. Our numerical and visual comparisons on widely used benchmarks justify our idea and show better ability of high fidelity geometry recovery in 3DGS. Project page: https://github.com/yangyixi21/Neural-Color-Fields-3DGS.

items.title_en: Multimodal Prompt Learning with Dual-Granularity Contrastive Alignment for Preoperative Prediction of Lung Adenocarcinoma Invasiveness Using 3D CT
items.title_zh: 基于双粒度对比对齐的多模态提示学习用于3D CT肺腺癌侵袭性术前预测
items.abstract_en: Accurate preoperative prediction of lung adenocarcinoma invasiveness is important for surgical planning and individualized treatment. However, overlapping CT appearances make it challenging to distinguish invasive adenocarcinoma (IAD) from Pre-IAD lesions. We propose a multimodal prompt-learning framework with dual-granularity image-text alignment for 3D CT-based IAD classification. A 3D ResNet-CBAM encoder extracts global and spatial visual features. A frozen RadBERT backbone is adapted with separate learnable prompts for report-level and keyword-level text encoding. These prompts are initialized using semantic representations derived from real-world clinical reports. Global contrastive alignment connects whole-volume CT representations with reports generated from clinician-annotated radiological attributes to provide overall semantic supervision. A multiple instance learning-based local alignment module associates spatial CT features with vascular-focused radiological keywords, to capture local imaging characteristics potentially associated with tumor invasion. The framework jointly optimizes classification and alignment objectives, while inference requires only CT images. Experiments included 1,593 pathologically confirmed nodules. On the test set, the proposed method achieved an accuracy of 87.92%, F1-score of 87.78%, and AUC of 0.9499. Its AUC significantly exceeded that of the image-only Res-CBAM baseline with the same visual backbone (0.9297; DeLong test, p = 0.0078). Ablation analyses supported the complementary contributions of global and local alignment and the benefit of report-based prompt initialization. Qualitative visualizations showed activation within nodules and adjacent vascular structures. These findings suggest that dual-granularity radiological supervision can enhance CT-based invasiveness prediction while preserving a CT-only inference workflow.

items.title_en: Ray-SCR: Generalizing Scene Coordinate Regression Across Camera Models
items.abstract_en: Among visual localization strategies, scene coordinate regression (SCR) has emerged as an attractive approach for its compactness, accuracy, and speed. Despite these advantages, SCR models generalize poorly across substantially different camera models, such as omnidirectional or strongly rectified imagery. This limitation arises because, changes in field of view, lens distortion, or rectification-induced resampling can make the same scene content appear differently depending on its pixel position, degrading localization accuracy. To cope with this limitation, we introduce Ray-SCR, a lightweight extension to existing SCR architectures that conditions local visual features on their calibrated viewing rays and refines neighboring ray-conditioned features with a shallow local Transformer. We further formulate supervision directly in ray space and use sparse SfM points as metric anchors that link observations across views and camera models. Taken together, these components enable a single scene representation built from a panoramic mapping sequence to accurately localize query images captured with very different cameras, including pinhole, fisheye, and omnidirectional cameras. We evaluate Ray-SCR across multiple SCR architectures and on datasets with pinhole, fisheye, and omnidirectional cameras. The proposed ray conditioning substantially improves generalization across cameras and leads to state-of-the-art localization performance in these challenging cross-camera settings. The project page is available at https://jaeminch0.github.io/ray-scr-generalizing-scene-coordinate-regression-across-camera-models/.

items.title_en: MIRA: Reinforcing Multimodal Reasoning via Deceptive Contextual Augmentation
items.abstract_en: While Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards (RLVR) has significantly advanced multimodal reasoning, existing frameworks suffer from a critical "perception-reasoning gap." Due to an over-reliance on seemingly relevant visual tokens, even minor perceptual perturbations can propagate through the reasoning process, leading to compounding hallucinations. To address this issue, we propose MIRA, a training framework that improves robustness to erroneous visual contexts while enhancing logical reasoning ability. By injecting filtered, deceptive visual contexts during training, we construct challenging "hard traps" that stress-test the model's robustness to misleading information. Furthermore, we introduce a group-wise reflection-triggering mechanism that enables the model to autonomously detect and rectify inconsistencies between visual cues and logical constraints, which is ultimately internalized as an intrinsic policy behavior. Importantly, MIRA does not rely on human annotations. Experimental results across multiple reasoning and perception benchmarks show that MIRA yields an average 7% improvement on in-domain benchmarks, with consistent improvements on vision-centric benchmarks. These findings highlight that active error recovery is essential for robust multimodal reasoning. Comprehensive ablation studies and analyses further provide insights into why MIRA is effective.

items.title_en: VL-Dedup: Graded Multimodal Entity Resolution for Image-Text Data Deduplication
items.abstract_en: Image-text corpora contain copies of one image, captions that describe one image in different ways, captions reused for different images, and captions that do not match their images. Each case calls for a different curation action. Deduplication and multimodal entity resolution (ER) only decide whether records are the same, and they are evaluated on labeled pairs. Yet pair scores do not tell which records end up in the same cluster or which useful captions get deleted. We therefore formulate image-text deduplication as graded multimodal ER, which decides visual identity, caption handling, and mismatches for each pair, and we evaluate it at three levels: pairs, clusters, and the retained set. Our method, VL-Dedup, groups records of the same visual entity into clusters and caps the size of each cluster. Within each cluster, a vision-language model (VLM) and CLIPScore decide which captions to keep and which to flag. We also build VL-DedupBench, with 50,000 COCO and SOP records and 66,788 labeled pairs. On it, a classifier that selects no false edge among the labeled pairs still joins millions of record pairs from different entities. Spending VLM calls on the pairs inside clusters, rather than on pairs with uncertain scores, gives better caption decisions from the same model. Even when almost all clusters are correct, keeping one record per cluster loses facts in many deletions, while the deletions of VL-Dedup lose much less information.

items.title_en: Cross-Layer Refinement and Frequency-aware Fusion Network for Multi-Source Remote Sensing Image Classification
items.abstract_en: Multi-source remote sensing image classification benefits from complementary spectral and structural information. However, identifying discriminative cross-modal features remains challenging. This letter proposes a Cross-Layer Refinement and Frequency-aware Fusion Network (CRFNet) within a lightweight dual-branch architecture. Specifically, a Cross-Layer Refinement Attention (CLRA) module propagates selected attention relationships across successive layers and employs top relation selection to progressively strengthen discriminative spatial dependencies while suppressing irrelevant responses. Furthermore, a Frequency-aware Complementary Fusion (FCF) module combines frequency-wise interactions with cross-modal channel attention in the Fourier domain. The resulting representations are then converted into spatial-domain gates to selectively modulate complementary features. Experiments on the Houston 2013 and Augsburg datasets demonstrate that the proposed CRFNet consistently outperforms several state-of-the-art methods. The codes are publicly available at https://github.com/oucailab/CRFNet

items.title_en: Shared-Pattern Collaborative Network for Multi-Source Remote Sensing Data Classification
items.title_zh: 用于多源遥感数据分类的共享模式协同网络
items.abstract_en: Multi-source remote sensing data classification has received growing attention recently. However, existing methods still struggle to jointly model long-range contextual dependencies and shared spatial patterns across heterogeneous modalities. To address this issue, we propose a Shared-Pattern Collaborative Network (SPCNet) for HSI and SAR/LiDAR joint classification. To enhance cross-modal collaborative learning, Shared-Pattern Collaborative Block (SPCB) is designed by introducing a shared large-kernel operator and a dynamic convolution branch, enabling the network to capture common spatial structures and content-adaptive local features. Furthermore, Region-Adaptive Modality Allocator (RAMA) is developed to assign spatially varying modality weights for reliable feature fusion. Experiments on Houston2013, Augsburg, and Houston2018 datasets demonstrate that SPCNet achieves superior classification performance over several state-of-the-art methods. The code will be made publicly available at https://github.com/oucailab/SPCNet

items.title_en: PlanContext: Benchmarking In-Context Driving Decision-Making
items.abstract_en: Real-world driving requires context-aware decision-making. Existing end-to-end driving benchmarks primarily assess trajectory quality through safety, compliance, comfort, and driving progress, leaving context-dependent decision-making insufficiently characterized. To fill this gap, we present PlanContext, a benchmark for evaluating in-context driving decision-making. PlanContext constructs paired evaluations by varying high-level driving intentions while keeping the observed scene fixed, enabling a natural and controllable assessment of context-dependent decision-making. We further define six representative driving contexts and jointly evaluate contextual decision correctness, road compliance, and dynamic safety with class-balanced metrics. Experiments on 9,561 scene-condition instances from NAVSIM and 23 public end-to-end driving models show that high conventional driving-quality scores do not consistently correspond to strong route-level in-context driving decision-making. Further analysis shows that model behavior varies with decision timing, road structure, and traffic interaction depending on the decision required by the current context. Our results highlight in-context driving decision-making as an important complementary dimension for evaluating end-to-end driving systems.

items.title_en: MuCHMDPoser: Multiview RGB-Camera Full-Body Pose Tracking for Virtual Reality
items.abstract_en: Accurate full-body tracking in Virtual Reality (VR) is heavily underconstrained when relying solely on consumer-grade sparse sensors, such as Head-Mounted Displays (HMDs) and handheld controllers. Indeed, the self-avatar full-body pose must be inferred based on the 3 available upper-body joints tracked by these devices. This leads to significant tracking error, especially in lower-body pose. To overcome this issue, we propose to extend the tracking setup with external multiview RGB cameras. We show that integrating RGB-based pose estimation this framework is able to significantly decrease lower-body tracking errors, even under common artifacts in RGB-based estimates. Additionally, we evaluate a only-once HMD-camera calibration procedure that does not require any physical markers. We finally propose an implementation of the overall framework, achieving an end-to-end animation at 60 FPS on a Nvidia RTX3080 GPU. Codes are available at https://github.com/antmaio/MuCHMDPoser.

items.title_en: VideoEditor-MoE: Scaling Complex Video Editing with Mixture of Experts
items.abstract_en: Complex video editing requires understanding complex instructions while jointly fulfilling multiple editing requests. Meeting these demands through dense model scaling substantially increases computational cost. We introduce VideoEditor-MoE, the first open-source mixture-of-experts framework for video editing. Beyond sparse MLP-MoE layers, MoE-Attention expands attention capacity through routed key--value experts while preserving global interactions among video tokens. Initialized from a 5B video editing model, VideoEditor-MoE scales to 14B and 56B parameters, with approximately 8B parameters activated per token in both variants. Comparisons with existing methods and two complementary baselines, Explicit-MoE and MLP-MoE, assess its benefits over explicit expert guidance and MLP-only expert architectures. Further analyses demonstrate that all experts remain active and reveal that learned routing responds more strongly to sample content and diffusion noise levels than to human-defined editing categories. Spatial analysis further indicates sensitivity to object-level semantic features. We also identify decoupled weight decay as a strategy for stabilizing expert scaling.

items.title_en: Bayesian Sequential Optimal Experimental Design for Single-Pixel Imaging using Reinforcement Learning
items.abstract_en: Adaptive compressed sensing (CS) aims to select the most informative measurements sequentially, which is crucial for many modern imaging systems. This task can be formulated as a Bayesian sequential optimal experimental design (sOED) problem, where each new acquisition is chosen to maximally reduce uncertainty about the unknown image given prior information and subsequent data provided by acquisitions. However, in single-pixel imaging (SPI), the large design space consists of all possible binary illumination patterns. Directly optimizing the Bayesian sOED objective over this space using conventional methods is generally challenging. In this work, we reformulate sOED for SPI as a reinforcement learning (RL) problem. In RL, an agent learns a policy through repeated experimental trials to maximize a reward, here given as the expected information gain, the most complete measure of uncertainty reduction in Bayesian OED. This avoids the need to directly optimize complex information-theoretic objectives during a measurement to obtain the next design. Instead, the result is a learned policy function that directly maps the current posterior belief about the image to the next optimal binary measurement pattern, in a computationally efficient way. Using a simple yet representative SPI imaging scenario, this work evaluates the scalability of the learned policy under two different policy parameterizations. Furthermore, we investigate how performance deteriorates when only approximate posterior information is available or the measurements are impaired by noise, and propose several strategies to introduce additional design constraints motivated by biomedical applications. The numerical experiments demonstrate that the proposed Bayesian sOED-RL framework remains robust and can be extended to more complex, large-scale SPI scenarios.

items.title_en: GPU-Native Real-Time Textured Mesh Reconstruction with Seam-Aware Multi-View Radiometric Correction
items.abstract_en: We present a GPU-native volumetric-video system for real-time reconstruction of graphics-compatible textured triangle meshes from multiple RGB-D sensors. Existing TSDF systems accelerate fusion and mesh extraction, but extending them to per-frame textured meshing adds CPU mesh processing, CPU-side texturing work, or extra CPU-GPU transfers between stages. After input staging, our method keeps the reconstruction and texturing stages (TSDF fusion, Marching Cubes, connected-component noise removal, view-based texture mapping, inpainting, and radiometric seam correction) resident on the GPU; no intermediate mesh or image data returns to the host between these stages. A fixed-size-array representation of mesh topology gives constant-time neighbor access on the GPU and makes the downstream mesh-level operations data-parallel. Because we texture each face from a single camera, exposure seams that vary smoothly across each image remain; we estimate a per-camera low-frequency gain field and bake it into the atlas on the GPU. On the CMU Panoptic dataset, our method is faster than the baselines at every tested voxel resolution and number of sensors, achieves peak speedups of more than an order of magnitude over CUDA-accelerated nvblox and CPU-based Open3D, and approaches an offline textured-meshing baseline in perceptual re-rendering quality.

items.title_en: A phase decoder for reconstructing missing muscle activity
items.title_zh: 一种用于重建缺失肌肉活动的相位解码器
items.abstract_en: Upper-limb assistive devices are commonly controlled with electromyographic (EMG) signals, but nerve injury, muscle loss, or practical limits on electrode placement can leave only a few usable signals, which constrains the decoding of intended movements. Here, we introduce a decoder that reconstructs missing muscle activations from sparse EMGs using a two-stage real-time approach: (1) estimating ongoing movement phase from available signals, and (2) retrieving corresponding muscle activations from a library of pre-recorded muscle activity templates. In proof-of-concept tests, neurologically intact participants (N=4) performed object-transfer tasks under simulated denervation conditions. The decoder accurately estimated movement phase (median root-mean-square error [RMSE] <0.17 of movement duration) and reconstructed missing muscle activations (RMSE 0.08-0.34; correlation up to 0.97) within ~2 ms, in a previously unseen participant. The results indicate that template based reconstruction could leverage sparse EMG for low latency control of assistive technology.
items.abstract_zh: 上肢辅助装置通常由肌电（EMG）信号控制，但神经损伤、肌肉缺失或电极放置的实际限制可能只留下少数可用信号，从而制约意图运动的解码。本文提出一种解码器，采用两阶段实时方法从稀疏EMG重建缺失的肌肉激活：（1）由可用信号估计当前运动相位；（2）从预先录制的肌肉活动模板库中检索相应的肌肉激活。在概念验证测试中，4名神经功能完好的参与者在模拟去神经支配条件下完成物体转移任务。解码器能准确估计运动相位（中位均方根误差<0.17个运动时长），并在约2 ms内重建缺失的肌肉激活（RMSE 0.08–0.34，相关性最高0.97），且可推广到此前未见过的参与者。结果表明，基于模板的重建可利用稀疏EMG实现辅助技术的低延迟控制。
items.highlight_zh: 用运动相位加模板库，从稀疏EMG在约2 ms内重建缺失肌肉激活
items.digest_zh: 1）研究什么问题：肌电控制的假肢和辅助装置在临床上常遇到可用信号太少的问题——神经损伤、肌肉切除或电极贴不下，只剩两三个通道，传统解码器难以还原使用者想做的动作。2）用了什么方法：作者没有直接“预测”缺失通道，而是把连续控制拆成两步。第一步，用现有少量EMG估计当前动作进行到周期的哪个“相位”；第二步，按这个相位去一张事先录好的肌肉活动模板库里查表，取回该时刻各肌肉应有的激活水平，从而补全缺失通道。3）得到什么结果：4名神经完好被试在人为屏蔽部分通道（模拟去神经）的条件下做物体转移任务。相位估计的中位均方根误差小于整个动作时长的0.17；重建的缺失肌肉激活与真实值误差在0.08–0.34之间，相关系数最高达0.97；整个计算约2 ms完成；并且对一位未参与模板录制的新被试同样有效。4）为何重要：这套思路把“预测”换成了“检索”，计算量极小、延迟极低，适合嵌入式实时控制；对残存信号极少的患者提供了一条务实路径。局限也很清楚：只是小样本概念验证，动作类型有限，模板库需要为每个人单独采集，病理状态下的相位估计仍待检验。

items.title_en: State-dependent emergence of coupling between oscillatory and aperiodic neural activity
items.title_zh: 振荡与非周期神经活动之间耦合的状态依赖性涌现
items.abstract_en: Neural oscillations and aperiodic activity are two quintessential mesoscopic-level features arising from shared circuits, yet what governs their relationship remains unclear. Here we show that coupling between oscillatory frequency and aperiodic exponent is sporadic and state-dependent. Bias-reduced analyses of 3,245 intracranial contacts from 61 awake subjects showed significant coupling in only <13% of contacts per band. A connectome-constrained dynamical model predicted that neither changes of input to local circuit nor removal of long-range connections modulated the coupling; whereas stronger local inhibitory feedback drove covariation between oscillatory frequency and aperiodic exponent. The model predictions were supported by three independent experiments: transcranial stimulation shifted each component independently and focal ablation of remote cortical tissues did not change coupling; whereas coupling emerged during seizures that altered local excitatory-inhibitory balance. These results suggest that the relation between periodic and aperiodic neural activity is neither intrinsically independent nor coupled, but determined by local circuit states.
items.abstract_zh: 神经振荡与非周期活动是共享环路产生的两种典型介观特征，但什么决定了它们之间的关系仍不清楚。本文表明，振荡频率与非周期指数之间的耦合是偶发且依赖状态的。对61名清醒被试的3245个颅内触点做偏差校正分析显示，每个频段仅不到13%的触点存在显著耦合。一个受连接组约束的动力学模型预测：改变对局部环路的输入或移除长程连接都不调节耦合，而更强的局部抑制性反馈会驱动振荡频率与非周期指数的共变。三项独立实验支持了模型预测：经颅刺激分别独立改变两个成分，远端皮层组织的局灶消融不改变耦合；而在改变局部兴奋-抑制平衡的癫痫发作期间，耦合出现了。这些结果提示，周期性与非周期神经活动的关系既非内禀独立、也非固有耦合，而是由局部环路状态决定。
items.highlight_zh: 振荡与非周期活动的耦合罕见，由局部抑制性环路状态决定
items.digest_zh: 1）研究什么问题：脑电或颅内记录里既有节律性振荡（如α波），也有不呈节律的1/f样“非周期”成分。两者都来自同一批神经环路，但学界长期不清楚它们是否耦合、由什么决定。这直接影响一个常见做法：用非周期指数去校正振荡功率是否合理。2）用了什么方法：作者分析了61名清醒被试共3245个颅内触点的信号，用偏差校正的谱参数化方法分别估计振荡频率和非周期指数，统计显著耦合的比例；再用受连接组约束的动力学模型提出机制假设；最后用三类实验验证。3）得到什么结果：耦合其实很罕见，每个频段只有不到13%的触点显著。模型显示，改变外部输入或切断长程连接都不影响耦合，只有增强局部抑制性反馈才会让两个成分一起变化。实验验证一致：经颅刺激对两个成分各自独立起作用，远端皮层局灶消融不改变耦合，而癫痫发作（局部兴奋-抑制平衡被打破）时耦合才出现。4）为何重要：这说明周期与非周期的关系不是脑的固定属性，而是局部环路状态的一种读出，有望作为兴奋-抑制平衡的指标；也提醒研究者不要默认二者耦合。局限是数据主要来自需颅内监测的癫痫患者，存在选择偏倚。

items.title_en: Pubertal timing is a critical dimension of adolescent brain vulnerability
items.title_zh: 青春期时序是青少年大脑脆弱性的关键维度
items.abstract_en: Adolescence is a period of rapid brain development, during which biological maturational timing varies substantially between individuals. This variability may drive specific developmental vulnerabilities to adverse experiences with long-term consequences, warranting early identification of at-risk individuals. We utilized ultrasonic bone age measurements to track pubertal maturity, classifying participants by adolescent biological maturity relative to chronological age (accelerated, average, decelerated). Brain hierarchy was quantified as the irreversibility of brain signals in resting state electroencephalography, providing a brain-based method to detect vulnerability patterns. The COVID-19 pandemic presented a unique opportunity to also assess alterations in brain hierarchy following external disruption. We mapped maturity-defined trajectories and rates of hierarchical organization, and their post-pandemic deviation from expected development, capturing two distinct vulnerability forms. First, early maturing adolescents showed persistent reduction in brain hierarchy. Second, those undergoing their fastest phase of development - specifically, decelerated adolescents - showed the strongest disruption in brain hierarchy following the pandemic. These findings suggest that pubertal timing is a critical dimension of individual variation in adolescent brain development and vulnerability. They also emphasize the need for objective maturity measurements to tailor support to individual pubertal timelines, particularly given the secular trend toward earlier puberty and ongoing global ecological crises.
items.abstract_zh: 青春期是大脑快速发育的时期，个体间的生物学成熟时序差异很大。这种差异可能造成对不良经历的特异性发育脆弱性并带来长期后果，因此需要早期识别高风险个体。我们利用超声骨龄测量追踪青春期成熟度，按相对于实际年龄的生物学成熟度（加速、平均、减速）对被试分类。以静息态脑电信号的不可逆性量化“大脑层级”，提供一种基于大脑的脆弱性检测方法。COVID-19大流行则提供了考察外部干扰后大脑层级改变的机会。我们刻画了成熟度所定义的层级组织轨迹与速率，以及疫情后偏离预期发育的程度，捕捉到两种不同的脆弱性形式：早熟青少年的大脑层级持续降低；而处于发育最快阶段的青少年——特别是减速组——疫情后大脑层级受扰最严重。这些发现表明，青春期时序是青少年大脑发育与脆弱性个体差异的关键维度，也强调需要客观的成熟度测量，以便按个体青春期时间线提供支持，尤其考虑到青春期提前的长期趋势与持续的全球生态危机。
items.highlight_zh: 青春期成熟早晚决定大脑层级轨迹与疫情下的脆弱程度
items.digest_zh: 1）研究什么问题：青少年期大脑快速重塑，但每个孩子“生物学上成熟”的时间早晚差别很大。同样一次外部冲击（如疫情），对早熟和晚熟的孩子可能伤害不同。问题是缺乏客观的成熟度标尺，也缺乏能识别脆弱个体的脑指标。2）用了什么方法：作者用超声骨龄测量客观刻画青春期成熟度，把被试按“生物学成熟度相对实际年龄”分为加速、平均、减速三组。再用静息态脑电信号的不可逆性（时间序列在时间反演下有多不对称）量化“大脑层级”组织程度，追踪各组发育轨迹与速率。COVID-19大流行被当作一次天然扰动，用来观察疫情后大脑层级偏离预期轨迹的程度。3）得到什么结果：识别出两种脆弱形式。一是早熟（加速）青少年，其大脑层级持续偏低；二是正处在发育最快阶段的青少年，特别是减速组，在疫情后大脑层级受到的扰乱最严重。4）为何重要：它把“什么时候发育”提到了和“发育到什么程度”同等重要的位置，说明青春期时序是理解个体差异与脆弱性的一个关键维度。方法上，骨龄这类客观测量加上脑电标记，有望在群体层面提前筛出高风险个体，并按各自的时间线给予支持——在全球青春期普遍提前、生态危机频发的背景下尤有意义。局限是脑电层级只是间接指标，疫情属于不可控的自然实验，因果推断仍需谨慎。

items.title_en: Paraquat Inhalation Produces Male-Biased Dopaminergic Neuron Loss and Motor Deficits in Mice: Relevance to Parkinsons Disease
items.title_zh: 百草枯吸入导致小鼠雄性偏向性多巴胺能神经元丢失和运动缺陷：与帕金森病的相关性
items.abstract_en: Long-term exposure to paraquat (PQ), a widely used herbicide, has been linked to increased risk of Parkinsons Disease (PD) in agricultural workers and rural communities in the United States (US), findings further supported by experimental animal studies. Although banned in many countries across the globe, PQ remains widely used in the US. Inhalation of PQ has been known to induce systemic organ failure at acute concentrations. However, prolonged low-dose inhalation from agricultural spraying and pesticide drift has not been readily evaluated for its potential to contribute to neurodegenerative diseases in vivo. Instead, many experimental studies have relied on systemic routes of exposure, which do not effectively replicate the most common route of exposure to PQ in the environment. In the current study, Parkinsonian features were examined in mice that had been exposed via whole-body inhalation to PQ aerosol for either 40 or 60 days. Levels of PQ in brain were highest in olfactory bulb, followed by frontal cortex and then brainstem in both sexes. After 60 days of exposure, male-specific impairments in locomotor activity were observed, in addition to reductions in striatal dopamine, in substantia nigra tyrosine hydroxylase (TH) expression and number of TH+ dopaminergic neurons, the latter being considered the primary basis of PD, along with increased olfactory bulb -synuclein levels. As such, these studies confirm the dopaminergic neurotoxicity of inhaled PQ. These findings raise significant concerns as to the contribution of PQ exposures to the continued increase in the incidence of PD in the US.

items.title_en: Imipramine binds to amyloid-β and extends the survival of Alzheimer's disease patients
items.title_zh: 丙咪嗪与淀粉样蛋白β结合并延长阿尔茨海默病患者的生存期
items.abstract_en: Background Apolipoprotein E (apoE) plays numerous roles in the pathogenic pathway to Alzheimer's disease (AD). We previously performed a high-throughput screen and identified the antidepressant imipramine as an inhibitor of the interaction between apoE and amyloid-{beta} (A{beta}). We also found that imipramine use to treat depression in AD patients was associated with better Mini-Mental State Exam (MMSE) scores. Here we studied the mechanisms by which imipramine inhibits the AD pathogenic pathway and investigated its effect on mortality in AD patients. Methods Nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy was used to characterize the interaction between imipramine and A{beta} monomers. Human induced pluripotent stem cell (hiPSC)-derived AD cerebral organoids (COs) and transgenic AD rats treated with imipramine underwent neuropathological evaluation, while rat learning and memory were assessed in the Morris Water Maze. AD patient mortality in the National Alzheimer's Coordinating Center's database was analyzed by Kaplan-Meier and Cox proportional hazards models. Results Imipramine inhibits the apoE-A{beta} interaction by binding directly to A{beta} monomers. Imipramine reduces A{beta} accumulation and neuronal cell loss in AD COs. Imipramine-treated female AD rats had enhanced reference memory and increased hippocampal cellularity and cholinergic neurotransmission. AD patients prescribed imipramine had reduced all-cause mortality over 10 years relative to those prescribed other tricyclic antidepressants (TCA), non-TCA antidepressants, or no antidepressants. Conclusions The findings support the conclusions that: a) the mechanism by which apoE confers risk for AD is by catalyzing the polymerization of A{beta} into neurotoxic species, b) targeting apoE is a promising, underappreciated strategy for the prevention of AD, c) imipramine should be used more frequently to treat depression in AD clinical practice, and d) imipramine should be evaluated in prospective trials, particularly in APOE4 carriers, as a potential method to improve cognition and reduce mortality in AD.

items.title_en: NeuralFieldManifold: Uncovering the Manifold Geometry of Local Field Potentials
items.title_zh: NeuralFieldManifold：揭示局部场电位的流形几何
items.abstract_en: Manifold geometry has become a powerful framework for understanding how the brain organizes high-dimensional neural activity into compact, interpretable structure. To date, however, most theoretical and methodological advances in neural manifold analysis have focused on spiking activity, leaving unresolved a fundamental question: What are the geometric principles governing the dynamics of local field potentials (LFPs); population level signals reflecting integrated subthreshold and suprathreshold neural activity that are broadly integral to clinical and brain-computer interface settings. Here, we establish, analytically and empirically, that the lag-embedded dynamics of LFP signals lie on a low-dimensional K-torus, where K directly relates to sustained oscillatory modes present in the signal. Modeling LFPs as bounded autoregressive processes, we show that each oscillatory component contributes an independent circular degree of freedom, while aperiodic 1/f structure and noise contribute only geometric thickness around the manifold without altering its topology. To apply this theory to real nonstationary recordings, we introduce DeepLagField, a physics-informed network that jointly estimates time-varying AR structure and effective model order, with formal guarantees that local toroidal geometry is preserved despite non-stationary nature of neuronal processes. Persistent homology analysis on real recordings reveals topological signatures consistent with the predicted toroidal Betti numbers in primate V1 LFP, rodent hippocampal LFP, and mouse cortical EEG, with varying degrees of agreement across recordings and temporal windows. Crucially, decoding analyses across three distinct neural datasets demonstrate that these geometric structures are not merely descriptive but capture behaviorally relevant information rivaling conventional spectral features. Together, these findings establish a theoretically grounded and empirically validated geometric framework for neural field analysis, extending the manifold perspective beyond spiking activity and offering a complementary language to spectral analysis for understanding and translating population dynamics across neural modalities.

items.title_en: Hmox1/CO regulates retina regeneration via modulation of Wnt/β-catenin signalling and induction of vaspb in zebrafish
items.title_zh: Hmox1/CO通过调控Wnt/β-catenin信号传导和诱导斑马鱼vaspb来调节视网膜再生
items.abstract_en: Muller glia (MG) in the zebrafish retina retain a latent stem cell capacity that is absent in mammals, yet the injury responsive signals that drive this reprogramming remain incompletely defined. Here, we identify heme oxygenase-1 (Hmox1), the stress-inducible, rate-limiting enzyme of heme catabolism, as a previously unrecognized regulator of this process. Following injury, hmox1a is selectively and rapidly induced among the heme oxygenase gene family, localizing to photoreceptors with expression peaking during the MG proliferation window. Pharmacological inhibition and morpholino mediated knockdown of Hmox1 dysregulate the acute inflammatory response, impair Muller glia-derived progenitor cell (MGPC) proliferation, and produce lasting deficits in retinal lamination, establishing Hmox1 as a potentially non-redundant, early-acting node required for structural recovery. Exogenous delivery of carbon monoxide (CO), a bioactive Hmox1 metabolite, partially rescues each of these phenotypes, functionally implicating CO as a key downstream effector. Mechanistically, Hmox1/CO signalling stabilizes {beta}-catenin likely via transcriptional repression of the Wnt antagonist dkk1b. This stabilized {beta}-catenin is enriched at a predicted Tcf7l2 site in the promoter of vaspb, which encodes an actin binding protein and is newly identified here as an injury-induced Wnt target gene. Bioinformatic and functional analyses further implicate Nfe2l2a (Nrf2) as a candidate intermediary bridging Hmox1/CO to Wnt regulation, with putative antioxidant response elements identified within the dkk1b locus. Together, these findings outline a putative Hmox1[->]CO[->]Nrf2[->]dkk1b[->]{beta}-catenin[->]vaspb relay coupling redox biology to Wnt-dependent glial reprogramming. Notably, HO-1 is similarly induced in stressed mammalian retina, yet Wnt/{beta}-catenin activation fails to sustain regeneration, positioning the Hmox1/CO axis as a candidate target for future investigation in mammalian retina regeneration.

items.title_en: Brain-wide representations of olfactory behavior in C. elegans
items.title_zh: 秀丽隐杆线虫嗅觉行为的全脑表征
items.abstract_en: Olfactory navigation emerges from dynamic interactions between sensory input, brain activity state and the animal's own movements. In C. elegans, a compact nervous system enables brain-wide imaging in behaving animals exposed to controlled olfactory environments, with an undulatory locomotion that reduces navigation to transitions among forward runs, reversals, and turns. Here, we used tracking microscopy to record and compare brain-wide neural activity in crawling worms navigating spatial odor gradients or isotropic environments, and in immobilized worms responding to temporal odor pulses. Across conditions, we identified strongly correlated brain-wide activity patterns spanning olfactory sensory neurons, interneurons, and premotor interneurons. Comparisons between navigation in odor gradients and exploration in isotropic environments revealed a compact functional circuit linking olfactory sensory neurons, interneurons, and premotor neurons. Comparisons between different odors distinguished sensory activity relationships associated with odor identity from a shared sensorimotor circuit for navigational movement. Comparisons between crawling and immobilized animals revealed profound differences in motor-state transitions and brain-wide correlation structure, further demonstrating the dependence of sensory representations and motor decision-making on behavioral context. Our findings reveal a functional organization linking olfactory sensory activity to navigational movement and show how this organization depends on behavioral state and environmental context.

items.title_en: Graph neural network approach for inferring neuronal connectivity
items.title_zh: 用于推断神经元连接性的图神经网络方法
items.abstract_en: Understanding the connectivity of neuronal networks is essential for understanding brain function. Current anatomical mapping techniques, such as serial section microscopy and viral tracing, are resource-intensive and cannot capture the efficacy of connectivity. A complementary approach is to infer effective connectivity from single-neuron-resolution population activity. We developed a graph neural network (GNN)-based tool, CircuitGNN, that accurately infers neural effective connectivity from population activity. CircuitGNN accurately inferred the connectivity of several small circuits and detected both the strengthening and weakening of connections, such as those that occur during learning. CircuitGNN outperformed other methods when applied to simulated population activity generated by an invertebrate central pattern-generating circuit and a cortical microcircuit. CircuitGNN was evaluated on networks of varying size, recording duration, and proportion of hidden neurons. Although performance improved with longer recordings, CircuitGNN achieved high precision with recordings as short as 4 min, scaled to large circuits of up to ~750 neurons, and remained robust when 20% or 40% of neurons were hidden. These results establish CircuitGNN as an accurate and robust technique for inferring neural connectivity from activity.

items.title_en: Noise-referenced multi-shell diffusion-weighted imaging for regional cerebrospinal fluid thermometry
items.title_zh: 用于区域脑脊液测温的噪声参考多壳扩散加权成像
items.abstract_en: We developed a multi-shell diffusion-weighted imaging approach for separate ventricular and subarachnoid cerebrospinal fluid thermometry. The approach uses measured image noise to assess agreement among temperature estimates. In 12 participants, temperature was estimated from four non-zero diffusion weightings. For each voxel, disagreement between these estimates was compared with that expected from image noise, accounting for their shared reference image. Voxels meeting this consistency criterion were retained for regional analysis. Mean diffusion-derived temperature ({+/-} SD) was 38.4 {+/-} 0.4 {degrees}C in the lateral ventricles and 36.0 {+/-} 1.1 {degrees}C in the subarachnoid space. Ventricular estimates were consistently higher than subarachnoid estimates across all participants, with a mean difference of 2.4 {+/-} 1.2 {degrees}C (95% confidence interval 1.6 -3.1 {degrees}C). This difference persisted under alternative noise models and temperature estimators. Subarachnoid estimates increased with retained voxel count; in a post hoc analysis of the six participants with the largest retained counts, ventricular estimates remained higher by 1.6 {+/-} 0.7 {degrees}C. Absolute temperature accuracy and the physiological origin of the regional difference require independent validation. This approach provides an internal consistency check for CSF thermometry and supports separate assessment of ventricular and subarachnoid temperatures.

items.title_en: Adipocyte Kindlin-2 Coordinates an E-cadherin/β-catenin/IGFBP2 Endocrine Axis to Regulate Skin Regeneration and Diabetic Wound Healing
items.title_zh: 脂肪细胞Kindlin-2协调E-cadherin/β-catenin/IGFBP2内分泌轴调控皮肤再生与糖尿病伤口愈合
items.abstract_en: Skin wound healing is a complex, multicellular process essential for maintaining tissue integrity and homeostasis. Despite advances in biomaterial and cell-based therapies, the mechanisms by which adipose tissue regulates skin regeneration remain incompletely understood. Here, we identify adipocyte Kindlin-2 as a critical regulator of cutaneous wound repair. Adipocyte-specific deletion of Kindlin-2 markedly accelerates wound closure in mice by enhancing fibroblast proliferation, angiogenesis, and suppressing inflammation. Transplantation of visceral white adipose tissue (vWAT) from Kindlin-2-deficient mice similarly promotes wound healing, indicating an endocrine contribution of vWAT to skin regeneration. Mechanistically, loss of Kindlin-2 promotes E-cadherin proteolysis, resulting in increased release of a 33-kDa C-terminal fragment (CTF2) that activates {beta}-catenin signaling and induces transcriptional upregulation and secretion of insulin-like growth factor binding protein 2 (IGFBP2). Elevated circulating IGFBP2, in turn, stimulates integrin signaling in target cells to enhance wound repair. Pharmacological inhibition of {beta}-catenin signaling abrogated the healing advantage conferred by Kindlin-2 deficiency. Conversely, local delivery of IGFBP2 via lentiviral significantly accelerates wound closure in both wild-type C57BL/6 and diabetic ob/ob mice. Collectively, these findings uncover a previously unrecognized adipose-skin endocrine axis governed by Kindlin-2 and IGFBP2 that orchestrates tissue regeneration. Targeting this Kindlin-2/E-cadherin/{beta}-catenin/IGFBP2 pathway offers a promising therapeutic strategy for enhancing wound healing, particularly in chronic and diabetic wounds.

items.title_en: The pupal stage shapes life-history trade-offs across metamorphosis
items.title_zh: 蛹期塑造跨变态的生活史权衡
items.abstract_en: Dealing with ecological stressors during development often comes at the expense of later-life performance. Although such trade-offs are well studied as two-stage systems such as larva-adult trade-offs, they are rarely examined across multiple developmental stages, limiting our understanding of how ecological effects are integrated throughout complex life cycles. We addressed this gap using a multistage experimental framework in Aedes aegypti, where we exposed individuals to predation risk during the larval stage, the pupal stage, both stages, or neither, and quantified developmental, physiological, and adult fitness traits. Contrary to expectations, predation risk across successive stages did not produce cumulative fitness costs, and traits varied in their responses. Both males and females emerged faster when exposed to risk, with lighter bodies, but males paid an additional cost of reduced starvation resistance when the pupal stage was exposed. Surprisingly, despite their lower body mass, females showed enhanced reproductive performance when both stages were exposed to risk. Overall, responses were stage- and sex-specific, with exposure during the non-feeding pupal stage imposing greater life-history costs than larval exposure alone. Measurements across the larva-pupa-adult continuum further revealed that traits such as body mass and energy reserves respond differently before and after metamorphosis, highlighting the role of the pupa in mediating trade-offs. Our findings identify the pupal stage as a critical mediator of life-history trade-offs and demonstrate the value of a multistage framework for understanding the role of each stage in life-history evolution.

items.title_en: Cell-lineage selection interacts with development and life history to shape the rates and identity of heritable mutations
items.title_zh: 细胞谱系选择与发育和生活史相互作用，塑造可遗传突变的速率与类型
items.abstract_en: Mutation rates determine the supply of heritable variation and are central to evolutionary theory, yet they are usually treated as properties of molecular mutational processes. We hypothesised that mutation rates are also shaped by selection among cell lineages within organisms and that the strength of this process depends on developmental and life-history traits. To test the extent of this idea, we combined mathematical modelling with experiments in Drosophila melanogaster and treated mutation rates as emergent properties of interactions among molecular mutagenesis, development, life history, and cell-lineage selection. The model predicts that even modest effects of mutations on cellular fitness can substantially alter the probability that mutations are transmitted, and that these effects depend strongly on developmental architecture, germline dynamics, and time to reproduction. In Drosophila, we experimentally demonstrate biased transmission of a mutation affecting cellular proliferation and show that this bias changes over the reproductive lifespan of the individual. Extending the model genome-wide reveals that the cellular distribution of fitness effects and its interaction with developmental parameters influence both the estimated mutation rate and the composition of transmitted mutations, producing transmission biases that favour mutations with particular cellular fitness effects. These results suggest that developmental and life-history parameters determine how cellular fitness effects translate into transmission bias; therefore, estimates of heritable mutational input can vary from species to species even under constant molecular mutagenesis. By filtering mutations before they enter populations, developmental and life-history evolution can modify both the rate and the nature of heritable variation and thereby influence evolutionary trajectories.

items.title_en: Association between trajectories of breastfeeding duration and infant health: Prospective cohort study
items.title_zh: 母乳喂养持续时间轨迹与婴儿健康的关联：前瞻性队列研究
items.abstract_en: Background: Breastfeeding is a modifiable pathway contributing to infant health. Objectives: To estimate trajectories of breastfeeding and the association between trajectories of breastfeeding and infant health. Methods: We conducted a prospective longitudinal cohort study (2014-2020, Canada) with 3217 cohabitating English-literate mother-father-infant triads with internet or telephone access. Women with major psychiatric conditions or suicidality were excluded. Data were collected online at baseline ( 90th percentile). We estimated trajectories of breastfeeding using latent class growth analysis. Associations were estimated using adjusted linear mixed models. Results: Most included mothers (n=2548) were of Canadian birth (2078/2548, 82%) and graduated from university (1920/2548, 75%); few reported unemployment (222/2548, 9%) or prenatal depression (240/2548, 9%). We identified two trajectories of breastfeeding: Constant Breastfeeding (1522/2548, 60%) and Decreasing Breastfeeding (1026/2548, 40%). No statistically significant differences were observed between classes for either the risk of challenging behaviors (RR -0.006 95% CI -0.028 to 0.016) or the risk of emergent visits (RR -0.015 95% CI -0.053 to 0.023). Conclusions: In this study, discontinued breastfeeding was not associated with infant health. Future studies should focus on 6-month exclusive breastfeeding, a modifiable therapeutic infant feeding target.

items.title_en: Maternal ADHD and exclusive breastfeeding: A prospective community-based cohort study
items.title_zh: 母亲ADHD与纯母乳喂养：一项前瞻性社区队列研究
items.abstract_en: Importance: Maternal attention-deficit disorder with or without hyperactivity (ADHD) is an established risk factor for adverse perinatal outcomes that remains understudied to breastfeeding. Objective: To estimate the effect of maternal ADHD on 6-month exclusive breastfeeding. Design: A prospective longitudinal community-based cohort study. Setting: Canada, 2014-2020. Participants: We included 3217 English-literate mother-father dyads with internet or telephone access, comprising women with singleton birth within 3 weeks postpartum (study baseline) and were cohabiting with the biological father. Women with major psychiatric conditions or suicidality were excluded. All participants provided informed consent at recruitment. Data were collected online through self-report questionnaires. Exposure: Maternal ADHD was measured at baseline using the Adult ADHD Self-Report Scale (sum of scores [≥]14). Main Outcomes and Measures: We defined 6-month exclusive breastfeeding based on maternal reported infant feeding, assessed at 3 and 6 months. Maternal childhood adversity (Adverse Childhood Experiences International Questionnaire, ACE-IQ; sum score) was included as a confounder. The average treatment effect on the treated (ATT) was estimated using linear probability models. We calculated 95% percentile bootstrap CI. Missing data were handled using multiple imputation by chained equations with 10 iterations. Results: Complete-case analyses included 2071/3217 mother-father dyads, most of which were Canadian-born (79%). Childhood adversity, mental health conditions, and substance use were higher among mothers who screened positive for ADHD (4%) than among those who did not: the median number of ACE was 5 IQR 4-6; 38% self-reported prenatal depression, 13% smoked cigarettes and 19% drank alcohol during pregnancy; 11% of infants used the neonatal intensive care unit. Notably, though 90% of mothers with ADHD intended to breastfeed exclusively only 28% breastfed exclusively for 6 months. Among families with maternal ADHD, the effect of maternal ADHD on 6-month exclusive breastfeeding was ATT -0.105, 95% CI -0.209 to -0.003 in the model adjusted for maternal ACE and paternal ADHD. With multiple imputation: ATT -0.109, 95% CI -0.213 to -0.004. Conclusions and Relevance: Mothers with ADHD intend to breastfeed their infants exclusively, but additional challenges shorten the duration of exclusive breastfeeding, indicating a need for interventions tailored to neurodevelopmental differences.

items.title_en: Polydrug use and recreational motives are associated with lower posttraumatic symptoms in survivors of a mass trauma event
items.title_zh: 多药使用和娱乐性动机与大规模创伤事件幸存者较低创伤后症状相关
items.abstract_en: Objective: Drug use after trauma is common, but polydrug use patterns, motives, and associations with subsequent symptoms are poorly understood. We examined these associations among mass-casualty terror attack survivors, 72% of whom used drugs immediately before trauma exposure. Methods: Survivors of the October 7, 2023 Nova Festival attack reported use of six drug types (alcohol, cannabis, ketamine, stimulants, MDMA, psychedelics) and motives (avoidance, emotional regulation, self-medication, sleep, recreation) longitudinally at three timepoints (TP): 1-6 months (N=772), 8-12 months (N=453), and 17-24 months (N=302) post-attack. Separate latent class analyses of TP2 data characterized drug use, motives, and their combination. Linear regression and mixed-effects models examined associations between class membership and PTSD Checklist for DSM-5 (PCL-5) scores, adjusting for age, sex, time since trauma, and TP1 PCL-5 scores. Results: At TP2, 70% reported polydrug use, 17% used one drug, and 13% reported no use. The high drug-load class (mean 4.6 drug types) had lower PCL-5 scores than the low drug-load class (mean 1.5 drug types); this difference was evident among participants using [≥]4 drug types and persisted through TP3. The self-medication-motive class had higher PCL-5 scores than the recreational-motive class. In joint analyses, recreational-motive users at both low and high drug loads had lower PCL-5 scores than participants reporting self-medication motives and primarily cannabis use. Conclusions: Polydrug use was common among the mass-trauma survivors in our study. Self-medication motives were associated with higher PTSD symptom severity than recreational motives. Unexpectedly, higher polydrug use was associated with lower PTSD symptom scores.

items.title_en: ACCURACY OF COMPRESSED SENSING ACCELERATED 3D-FLAIR IN THE DIAGNOSTIC WORK-UP OF MULTIPLE SCLEROSIS AT 1.5 T
items.title_zh: 压缩感知加速3D-FLAIR在1.5 T多发性硬化诊断检查中的准确性
items.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: 3D-FLAIR is central to MR-based diagnosis and monitoring of MS, but long acquisition times remain a limitation. OBJECTIVES: This single-center prospective non-inferiority study evaluated whether compressed sensing (CS) - accelerated 3D-FLAIR at 1.5T provides lesion detection comparable to optimized Generalized Autocalibrating Partially Parallel Acquisition (GRAPPA) - accelerated 3D-FLAIR. Optimized CS- and GRAPPA-accelerated 3D-FLAIR sequences were incorporated into MRI examinations in patients with known or suspected MS. The primary endpoint was manual lesion count by two blinded readers using a 10% non-inferiority margin. Secondary endpoints included image quality, SNR, CNR, and automated lesion count and volumetry. RESULTS: Sixty-eight patients were included (mean age, 40.1+/-13.3 years; 61.8% women). CS-accelerated 3D-FLAIR reduced acquisition time by 31.8% compared with GRAPPA (4:00 vs 5:52 minutes). Non-inferiority for manual lesion count was demonstrated for both readers (reader A, p < .0001; reader B, p = .005). Interrater agreement was excellent for CS (ICC = 0.921; 95% CI, 0.837-0.957) and very good for GRAPPA (ICC = 0.851; 95% CI, 0.769-0.906). Subjective image quality was high for both techniques. GRAPPA showed higher objective signal-to-noise-ratio (SNR) and contrast-to-noise-ratio (CNR), whereas automated lesion counts and volumes were higher for CS. CONCLUSION: CS-accelerated 3D-FLAIR provided non-inferior lesion detection with substantial scan-time reduction.

items.title_en: PROSPECTIVE COMPARISON OF OPTIMIZED COMPRESSED SENSING AND GRAPPA-ACCELERATED 3D-TOF-MRA FOR EVALUATION OF UNTREATED INTRACRANIAL ANEURYSMS AT 1.5 T: A NON-INFERIORITY STUDY
items.title_zh: 优化压缩感知与GRAPPA加速3D-TOF-MRA用于评估1.5 T未治疗颅内动脉瘤的前瞻性比较：一项非劣效性研究
items.abstract_en: RATIONALE AND OBJECTIVES 3D-TOF-MRA is a standard non-invasive method for detecting and monitoring intracranial aneurysms, but long scan times remain a limitation. Compressed sensing (CS) acceleration for intracranial aneurysm evaluation has mainly been studied at 3T. This prospective single-center non-inferiority study compared CS-accelerated 3D-TOF at 1.5T with GRAPPA-accelerated 3D-TOF-MRA for evaluating untreated intracranial aneurysms. MATERIALS AND METHODS Sample size was determined via a preliminary retrospective study. 25 patients with 32 untreated aneurysms underwent both CS- (factor 7, 3:04 min) and GRAPPA-accelerated (factor 2, 5:00 min) 3D-TOF, yielding a 38.7% scan-time reduction. Two blinded neuroradiologists assessed overall image quality (primary endpoint) and artifacts, subjective CNR, aneurysm delineation and diameters (secondary endpoints). Non-inferiority was tested via one-sided t-test (prespecified 10% margin); interrater agreement used ICC. RESULTS CS demonstrated non-inferiority to GRAPPA for overall image quality in both readers (p <= .023), though interrater agreement was low (ICC 0.241-0.262), reflecting subjective variability. Secondary exploratory analyses showed heterogeneous preferences. ROI-based CNR was lower for CS (median 169.6; IQR, 91.0-226. vs. 278.2; 181.0-366.2). Aneurysm diameter measurements showed excellent interrater agreement for both techniques (CS ICC, 0.899-0.980; GRAPPA ICC, 0.877-0.973; all p < .001). CONCLUSION CS-accelerated 3D-TOF at 1.5T met non-inferiority criteria vs. GRAPPA-TOF for overall image quality, reducing scan time by 38.7% while preserving aneurysm measurement reliability. However, reduced CNR and reader-preference variability important trade-offs.

items.title_en: Fibromuscular Dysplasia in Acute Type A Aortic Dissection: A Common yet Underrecognized Vascular Phenotype in Women
items.abstract_en: Objectives: Fibromuscular dysplasia (FMD) is a non inflammatory, non atherosclerotic arterial disease characterized by multifocal arterial beading that predominantly affects women. Although FMD commonly involves the renal and carotid arteries, its relationship with acute type A aortic dissection (ATAAD) remains poorly understood. We investigated the proportion of patients with FMD among patients with ATAAD, focusing on sex based differences. Materials and Methods: Patients aged below 70 years with ATAAD and ECG triggered aortic CT angiography (CTA) were consecutively included in this retrospective single-center study. FMD was defined as multifocal arterial beading (string-of-beads appearance) in at least one vascular territory, according to international consensus criteria. The highest-quality CTA examination was evaluated by an experienced cardiovascular radiologist. All suspected FMD cases were independently reviewed by a second experienced cardiovascular radiologist, with the final diagnosis established by consensus. Proportions were reported with 95% confidence intervals and compared between sexes . Results: Of 214 patients screened, 200 were included (138 men and 62 women). FMD was confirmed in 18/200 patients (9%; 95% CI, 6 till 14%), none of whom had a prior FMD diagnosis. FMD was more frequent in women (12/62, 19%; 95% CI, 11 till 31%) than men (6/138, 4%; 95% CI, 2 till 9%; P<0.001). FMD predominantly involved the renal arteries. Additional carotid CTA was available in 49/200 patients (25%) and in 7/18 patients with FMD (39%); three of these seven patients had carotid FMD. Conclusion: FMD was observed in a substantial proportion of patients presenting with ATAAD, particularly women. These findings suggest that FMD is an underrecognized vascular phenotype in patients with ATAAD.

items.title_en: Screening for rheumatoid arthritis-associated interstitial lung disease using lung ultrasound: a systematic review and quality appraisal of recent studies
items.abstract_en: Interstitial lung diseases (ILD) associated with systemic autoimmune disease can have a strong negative impact on patient outcomes. The diagnostic gold standard is high-resolution computer tomography (HRCT). Numerous studies have proven lung ultrasound's (LUS) utility in ILD, as well as other lung pathologies. Recently, there has been more focus on ILD in rheumatoid arthritis (RA), a previously overlooked complication, and screening methods. The purpose of this systematic review was to summarize the recent knowledge regarding LUS compared to HRCT in screening ILD in RA patients. We reviewed relevant literature from the last 10 years and selected 10 articles. Results show that LUS is effective compared to HRCT as a screening tool. Several diagnostic and severity scores have been elaborated and tested. Further focus should be on LUS in long-term follow-up and standardization of protocols.

items.title_en: Enhancing deep sleep with auditory stimulation to boost cognitive training responsiveness in people with Parkinson's disease and mild cognitive impairment: Rationale and design of the double-blind randomized controlled trial PD-CogT-Sleep
items.abstract_en: Background: Cognitive training (CogT) is an established non-pharmacological intervention for people with Parkinson's disease (PD) and mild cognitive impairment (PD-MCI). However, overall effects on cognitive outcomes are small to moderate and interindividually highly heterogeneous. Sleep -especially deep sleep- could be an important determinant of CogT responsiveness in PD, and may have beneficial effects on PD pathophysiology. Therefore, the enhancement of deep sleep by phase-targeted auditory stimulation (PTAS) could strengthen the effects of CogT on cognitive symptoms and counteract disease progression. Methods: PD-CogT-Sleep is a monocentric, partly decentralized, double-blind, randomized sham-controlled trial that combines two remotely delivered non-pharmacological interventions, to assess the additive effect of PTAS on digital CogT responsiveness in people with PD-MCI. The primary outcome is executive functions; Secondary and exploratory outcomes include further cognitive functions, participant-reported outcome measures, blood-based biomarkers, and high-density sleep electroencephalography markers. Outcomes are assessed at baseline, five weeks post-allocation and at 3-month follow-up. We aim to consecutively recruit N=50 participants, who will be randomized 1:1 to receive CogT+PTAS or CogT+Sham. Discussion: The PD-CogT-Sleep study integrates wearable and digital technologies to systematically combine a novel, non-invasive, sleep-enhancing intervention (PTAS) with established CogT to improve cognition and evaluate PTAS' disease-modifying potential through its effects on blood-based biomarkers in PD-MCI. The expected results will foster our understanding of the interplay of sleep, cognition, and neurodegeneration, and may guide further development of safe, feasible, scalable, patient-centered, technology-based non-pharmacological interventions counteracting cognitive decline in neurodegenerative diseases.

items.title_en: Quantitative deep motor phenotyping of 102 people with SCN2A, KCNQ2, CSNK2A1, CACNA1A or SCN8A-related disorders
items.abstract_en: Background and Objectives: Motor dysfunction is a major contributor to disability in pediatric-onset monogenic neurodevelopmental disorders (NDDs), yet systematic quantifications of motor phenotypes across development using validated clinical scales remain underdeveloped. Existing studies have classified motor phenotypes rather than quantified domain-specific severity, limiting their use as outcome measures in clinical trials. Here, we systematically quantify motor dysfunction using established clinical rating scales to explore their utility as motor endpoints. Methods: In this cross-sectional observational study, 102 individuals with NDDs (0.5-38 years) secondary to pathogenic or likely pathogenic variants in five genes (SCN2A, KCNQ2, CSNK2A1, CACNA1A, SCN8A) and 31 unaffected sibling controls underwent standardized motor assessments using the Scale for Assessment and Rating of Ataxia, Burke-Fahn-Marsden Dystonia Scale, and the Modified Ashworth Scale. Regional and functional categorization of parameters enabled differentiated interpretation. Gene-specific patterns were evaluated using z-score standardization across the pooled affected cohort, with gene-level averaging and nonparametric bootstrap-derived 95% confidence intervals. Results: Dysfunction was present in individuals with NDDs across speech (90%), coordination (87%), dystonia (83.3%), gross motor (82.4%) and spasticity (42.2%), with minimal impairment in controls (0-12.9%). We observed substantial heterogeneity across motor domains and subdomains; ataxic dysarthria had the highest score distribution (median 0.83 [IQR, 0.17-1.0]), whereas spasticity showed near-floor scores. Individuals with SCN2A variants demonstrated higher mean z-scores across multiple subdomains than other genes, with more consistent deviations observed in coordination and speech domains (Coordination: mean z = 0.29, 95% CI 0.03-0.54; Speech: mean z = 0.3, 95% CI 0.03-0.57), whereas domain-specific or less pronounced patterns were observed in other genes. The ataxia and dystonia scales demonstrated low floor and ceiling effects. Discussion: Using three clinical scales across a broad developmental and functional range, our study moves motor phenotyping in monogenic NDDs from categorical description toward quantitative, domain-resolved severity assessment. Exploratory analysis indicates marked heterogeneity in severity profiles across genes, most notably in SCN2A, suggesting potential selective motor vulnerability. These findings provide evidence for the feasibility of motor phenotyping and provide preliminary, cross-sectional benchmark severity distributions. Subsequent longitudinal validation and validation in larger, longitudinal, and variant-stratified cohorts will enable natural history studies and future therapeutic trials alongside seizure outcomes.

items.title_en: Variant Classification of a Non-Protein Coding Gene: ACMG/AMP Specifications for RMRP from the Clinical Genome Resource Severe Combined Immunodeficiency Disease Variant Curation Expert Panel
items.abstract_en: Purpose: This study, conducted by the Clinical Genome Resource Severe Combined Immunodeficiency Disease Variant Curation Expert Panel (ClinGen SCID-VCEP), aimed to adapt the American College of Medical Genetics and Genomics/Association for Molecular Pathology (ACMG/AMP) framework for germline variant interpretation in RMRP. Unlike the protein-coding genes for which the framework was primarily developed, RMRP encodes a non-protein-coding RNA. Biallelic pathogenic variants in RMRP cause cartilage-hair hypoplasia, which can include severe combined immunodeficiency disease and other immune abnormalities. Methods: An RMRP-focused SCID-VCEP subgroup reviewed all 28 ACMG/AMP evidence criteria using population databases, published clinical and experimental data, computational predictions, and expert consensus. Each criterion was retained, modified, or designated as not applicable based on RMRP biology and disease mechanisms. The resulting specifications were pilot tested using 27 variants selected from ClinVar and research laboratory data. Results: Fifteen ACMG/AMP criteria were determined to be applicable to RMRP, while 13 were considered not applicable. Several criteria were modified to evaluate nucleotide-level effects on transcriptional regulation, critical promoter regions, and RNA secondary structure. The specifications also incorporated RMRP-specific recommendations for population frequency, functional evidence, variant phase, segregation, and phenotype. Application of the specifications classified 6 variants as pathogenic, 10 as likely pathogenic, 7 as variants of uncertain significance, and 4 as benign. Previously pathogenic or likely pathogenic variants remained within the pathogenic spectrum, and all previously benign variants remained benign. Variants with conflicting ClinVar interpretations were resolved as either likely pathogenic or uncertain. PM1, PM3, and PP4 were the primary criteria supporting pathogenic classifications. Conclusion: The SCID-VCEP specifications provide a standardized approach to the classification of germline RMRP variants in cartilage-hair hypoplasia and demonstrate how the ACMG/AMP framework can be adapted for a disease-associated non-protein-coding RNA gene. These specifications support the development of variant interpretation frameworks for other clinically relevant non-protein-coding genes.

items.title_en: Effects of Pantoprazole Based on Dialysis Status: A Protocol and Statistical Analysis Plan for a Secondary Analysis of the REVISE Trial
items.abstract_en: Background A recent international randomized trial found that the proton pump inhibitor (PPI) pantoprazole significantly reduced the risk of clinically important upper gastrointestinal (GI) bleeding among invasively ventilated patients in the intensive care unit (ICU), with no effect on mortality. Pantoprazole may be of particularly high utility among patients at high-risk of bleeding, such as those receiving renal replacement therapy (RRT) prior to ICU admission. However, given the complex mechanisms by which renal insufficiency may increase bleeding risk, as well as the possible association between PPI use and adverse kidney outcomes, investigating whether kidney failure treated with RRT at baseline modifies the treatment effect of PPIs is clinically relevant. Methods We have planned a post hoc secondary analysis of the Re-evaluating the Inhibition of Stress Erosions (REVISE) Trial (NCT03374800). The primary objective if this study is to evaluate whether any RRT on study day 1 (e.g., maintenance RRT in the outpatient setting, or RRT initiated in the hospital [intermittent hemodialysis, continuous renal replacement therapy, sustained low efficiency dialysis, or peritoneal dialysis]) modifies the treatment effect of pantoprazole on clinically important upper GI bleeding and 90-day mortality. The secondary objective is to evaluate whether maintenance RRT (intermittent hemodialysis or peritoneal dialysis) in an outpatient setting before the index hospital admission modifies the effect of pantoprazole on clinically important upper GI bleeding and 90-day mortality. Secondary outcomes for both analyses are patient important upper GI bleeding, ICU and hospital mortality. We will perform Cox proportional-hazard analyses, including the RRT exposure of interest, randomized group, and their interaction for each outcome, reporting results as hazards ratios with 95% confidence intervals, and p-values for the interaction term. Conclusion Results of this study will inform critical care practice, particularly for the care of patients at risk of stress-related GI ulceration in the ICU who have received RRT.

items.title_en: Automatic Generation of Novel Highly-Functional Molecular Sequences
items.title_zh: 自动生成新型高功能分子序列
items.abstract_en: While multiple methods now exist to generate functional sequence variants from existing annotated examples, it is unclear how well such methods can be used to generate sequences that exceed the functionality of those contained in the example set. Using two complete fitness landscapes, we quantify how effectively generative tools can search sequence space and find rare, novel, highly functional sequences, focusing on variational auto-encoders and information-theoretic methods. We find that an information-theoretic method that does not require training and runs significantly faster than standard Machine-Learning/Artificial Intelligence (ML/AI) methods also is significantly more effective in finding rare highly-functional sequences. We discuss the application of this novel method to discover rare polypeptides with anti-bacterial properties that are specific to bacterial, but not eukaryotic, cell membranes.
items.abstract_zh: 目前已有多種方法可以从已有标注样本生成功能序列变体，但这些方法能否生成功能超过样本集内序列的新序列，仍不清楚。我们利用两个完整的适应度景观，定量评估生成式工具在序列空间中搜索并找到稀有、新颖、高功能序列的效果，重点考察变分自编码器与信息论方法。我们发现，一种无需训练、运行速度远快于标准机器学习/人工智能（ML/AI）方法的信息论方法，在寻找稀有高功能序列方面也显著更有效。我们还讨论了如何用这一新方法发现具有抗菌特性、且特异作用于细菌细胞膜而非真核细胞膜的稀有���肽。
items.highlight_zh: 无需训练的信息论方法比VAE更快更有效地找出稀有高功能序列
items.digest_zh: 1）研究什么问题：现在有不少生成模型可以从已有标注样本出发，造出“像样”的蛋白或核酸序列。但真正有用的问题是：它们能不能造出功能比训练集中最好的序列还强的新序列？这一点此前缺乏严格检验。2）用了什么方法：作者借助两个已知的“完整适应度景观”——即任意序列的功能值都能被精确计算甚至穷举的数据集——把序列搜索变成一个可严格打分的任务。然后比较变分自编码器（VAE）与一类信息论方法，看谁能在巨大的序列空间中更高效地找到稀有但高功能的序列。3）得到什么结果：一种不需要训练、运行速度显著快于标准ML/AI方法的信息论方法，在找到稀有高功能序列上也显著更有效。也就是说，在这类任务上，“训练一个生成模型去模仿数据分布”未必是最优策略。4）为何重要：序列空间极其庞大而功能实验昂贵，搜索策略的效率直接决定能否发现有用的分子。作者进一步提出把该方法用于发现只攻击细菌膜、不伤真核细胞膜的抗菌多肽，这对应对耐药菌有潜在价值。局限是只在两个适应度景观上做了验证，能否推广到其他蛋白家族与更复杂的功能，还需要更多实验检验。

items.title_en: In-depth data movement characterization of DNA read mapping algorithms
items.abstract_en: Read mapping algorithms represent a critical bottleneck in genomic analysis pipelines due to the resources required; a problem that is becoming more pronounced as sequencing technologies advance and datasets expand. We present an extensive workload characterization of leading read mapping algorithms across diverse sequencing technologies to identify hardware acceleration and optimization opportunities. We analyzed the following implementations: MashMap, wfmash, and Minimap2 for whole-genome alignment (WGA); NGMLR, Minimap2, and LRA for long reads; and Bowtie2, BWA-MEM, StrobeAlign, and minibwa for short reads. We used the Intel VTune Profiler for detailed memory analysis to identify memory- bound functions, cache usage patterns, and data transfer bottlenecks. We further analyzed a selected subset of alignment tools using the DAMOV-SIM simulator to obtain a more granular view of data movement characteristics for two different cache structures. Based on our results, Minimap2 emerges as the fastest alignment tool for long read scenarios, but falls behind in whole-genome alignment due to poor multithreading. Across all three categories, some programs (e.g., LRA, BWA-MEM) are highly memory-bound. More in-depth analysis via DAMOV-SIM revealed that some memory-bound tools, in particular, do not fully utilize the multi-level cache hierarchy in modern multi-core CPU architectures. Our results show that while some tools require algorithmic redesign for performance gains, some others can benefit from running on PIM architectures.

items.title_en: RangeFinder: Predicting Ligand Property Ranges from Protein Pockets
items.title_zh: RangeFinder：从蛋白质口袋预测配体性质范围
items.abstract_en: Identifying ligands for a protein target requires searching a vast chemical space for a comparatively small set of compatible molecules. Existing machine learning approaches primarily address this problem by generating candidate ligands or scoring individual protein-ligand pairs, but provide limited information about the broader chemical space compatible with a binding pocket. We introduce RangeFinder, an SE(3)-equivariant transformer pocket-level model, trained and evaluated on BioLiP2 data, that predicts ranges over nine physicochemical ligand properties directly from pocket structure, chemistry, and evolutionary context. Using an intersection-over-union objective and evaluation metric (range-IoU), RangeFinder achieves a range-IoU of $0.464 \pm 0.002$, outperforming all deployable baselines while requiring only $12.2$ ms per pocket. We also quantify our method's ability to reduce the ligand search space while retaining compatible binders; in this regard, RangeFinder achieves a Reduction-Recall F-Score of $0.543 \pm 0.011$ --- once again outperforming all deployable baselines. Ablation experiments indicate that RangeFinder's performance depends more strongly on the density and quality of ligand supervision than on any individual input modality or specialized training strategy. Together, these results position RangeFinder as an inexpensive and effective molecular filtering prior, with demonstrated potential in narrowing the ligand search space of target pockets before docking, generation, or synthesis. The code for this project can be found at: https://github.com/alannadels/RangeFinder.

items.title_en: From FAIR to AI-FAIR Metadata-First Infrastructure for AI-Enabled Science
items.abstract_en: Artificial intelligence (AI) technologies and their capabilities have advanced rapidly over the past few years, leading to widespread interest and adoption in the biological and ecological sciences. However, the data infrastructure and computational resources that provide the foundation for AI workflows in ecology and biodiversity science remain fragmented. Moreover, the flow of value remains largely unidirectional: data move from collectors, through repositories and aggregators into models, and finally to research products or management actions. The derived value, such as corrected taxonomies, annotations, quality flags, and insights, rarely returns to source communities. We propose an extension of the original FAIR principles to address the needs of AI-ready infrastructure: the AI-FAIR metadata criteria, which place AI-enabled science in the context of a bidirectional Question-Data-Model triangle. This framework is designed to facilitate large-scale content-based analysis across diverse collections and ensure that the scientists generating the data benefit from the AI-enabled advances built on their data. Alongside these criteria, we introduce an agentic evaluation workflow that both rates existing datasets on the AI-FAIR and traditional FAIR criteria and provides actionable feedback where critical metadata is missing or incomplete. This modular dataset evaluation tool, paired with a domain-appropriate checklist, translates these principles into a reusable assessment of machine-learning readiness, AI-readiness for specified tasks, traceability, and ethical and CARE-aligned stewardship. Through this approach we aim to create a community-informed system to close the model data loop, so that AI also enriches data to further enable scientific discovery.

items.title_en: Intrinsic network dynamics catalyze switching in functional connectivity states of the brain
items.abstract_en: Dynamic functional connectivity (dFC) reflects ongoing reconfiguration of large-scale brain networks, but the temporal organization and network processes underlying spontaneous state transitions remain poorly understood. We developed functional connectivity state switching (FCSS), a phase-coherence-based framework that tracks multiscale changes in dominant whole-brain connectivity configurations. In Human Connectome Project fMRI, FCSS was strongly evoked by cognitive state and condition switches, and distinct transition dynamics differentially predicted working-memory performance. During rest, spontaneous FCSS was characterized by progressive changes in network segregation, integration, and cross-network communication as connectivity approached a switching event. Critically, event-related analysis time-locked to spontaneous FCSS revealed opposing pre-switch dynamics: salience-network contribution increased while default-mode-network contribution decreased, suggesting coordinated engagement and disengagement of these networks before switching. This reciprocal reweighting may provide a network-level mechanism for spontaneous FC reconfiguration. Together, these findings identify both global reorganization and network-specific processes underlying spontaneous and task-evoked brain-state transitions in the human brain.

items.title_en: Coupling cellular trajectories and RNA kinetics on continuous expression manifolds with ManifoldVelo
items.abstract_en: Jointly recovering pseudotime and RNA velocity from static single-cell transcriptomes requires reconciling global trajectory structure with local expression changes, particularly in complex cycles and branching differentiation. Here we introduce ManifoldVelo, a topology-conditioned framework that jointly learns cellular coordinates, continuous RNA trajectories and regulatory kinetics. Derivatives of unspliced and spliced RNA trajectories are matched to transcription-splicing-degradation dynamics, including between observed cells, allowing expression reconstruction, cellular ordering and kinetic estimation to inform one another. ManifoldVelo recovers pseudotime across all evaluated single-cell trajectory types, including cyclic, multibranch and smooth non-branching trajectories. ManifoldVelo achieves the best pseudotime recovery among compared methods in multipeak cyclic simulations and the highest directional agreement for spliced RNA velocity in both multipeak cyclic and branching simulations. Real-data analyses support phase prediction across experimental plates and differentiation trajectories consistent with pancreatic developmental stages and marker expression. Its central advantage is the joint recovery of temporal position and local dynamics across distinct trajectory structures within a reusable dynamic reference. New cells are assigned pseudotime and velocity predictions from spliced RNA alone, without refitting the reference model. ManifoldVelo provides a foundation for dynamic cell atlases that transfer learned temporal and kinetic information to new samples.

items.title_en: Quantum channel tomography: optimal bounds in the near-boundary regime
items.title_zh: 量子信道层析：近边界区域的最优界
items.abstract_en: Quantum channel tomography (also known as quantum process tomography) is a fundamental task in quantum information and quantum computing, aiming to learn the full description of an unknown quantum channel from black-box queries. For channels with input dimension $d_1$, output dimension $d_2$, and Kraus rank at most $r$, [CGO+26] identifies the dilation rate $τ=rd_2/d_1\geq 1$ as a key parameter governing a Heisenberg-to-classical transition in query complexity. While the optimal bounds in the boundary regime ($τ=1$) and the away-from-boundary regime ($τ\geq 1+Ω(1)$) are now known, the precise behavior in the near-boundary regime ($1<τ<1+o(1)$) has remained unresolved. In this paper, we close this gap, thereby fully settling the query complexity of quantum channel tomography. Specifically, we show that the query complexity is - $Ω(rd_1d_2/\varepsilon^2)$ for diamond norm error $\varepsilon$, matching the upper bound by [MB26, CGO+26], - $Θ(d_1^2/\varepsilon+\min\{(τ-1)d_1^2,(τ-1)^2d_1^2d_2^2\}/\varepsilon^2)$ for Choi trace norm error $\varepsilon$.
