Our results reveal two qualitatively different forms of the Heisenberg-to-classical transition. For diamond norm tomography, the Heisenberg scaling disappears suddenly as soon as $τ$ leaves the boundary regime. In contrast, Choi trace norm tomography exhibits a gradual transition from Heisenberg to classical scaling as $τ$ moves from the boundary regime to the away-from-boundary regime.
items.abstract_zh: 量子信道层析旨在从黑箱查询中学习未知量子信道的完整描述。对输入维数 d1、输出维数 d2、Kraus 秩至多 r 的信道，膨胀率 τ=rd2/d1 控制查询复杂度由海森堡型向经典型的转变。边界区（τ=1）与远离边界区（τ≥1+Ω(1)）的最优界已知，近边界区（1<τ<1+o(1)）则悬而未决。本文填补该空白，彻底确定其查询复杂度：diamond 范数误差 ε 下为 Ω(rd1d2/ε²)，与已有上界匹配；Choi 迹范数误差 ε 下为 Θ(d1²/ε+min{(τ-1)d1²,(τ-1)²d1²d2²}/ε²)。结果表明两者转变形态不同：前者离开边界区即骤然失去海森堡标度，后者则渐进过渡。
items.highlight_zh: 补全近边界区，彻底定出量子信道层析查询复杂度
items.digest_zh: ①研究了什么问题：量子信道层析要完全刻画一个未知量子信道，需要多少次查询？此前已知答案取决于“膨胀率”τ=rd2/d1（r 为 Kraus 秩，d1、d2 为输入输出维数），并存在从海森堡标度到经典标度的转变，但 τ 略大于 1 的“近边界区”一直是空白。②方法：作者给出新的下界构造，与已有上界结合得到紧确的查询复杂度——diamond 范数下为 Ω(rd1d2/ε²)，Choi 迹范数下为 Θ(d1²/ε+min{(τ-1)d1²,(τ-1)²d1²d2²}/ε²)。③结果：两种误差度量下的转变形态截然不同：diamond 范数层析一旦 τ 离开 1，海森堡标度立刻消失；Choi 迹范数层析则随 τ 增大平滑过渡。④为何重要：至此量子信道层析的查询复杂度被完全确定，也说明“用哪种误差度量”会实质改变问题的难度图景，对量子基准测试与设备表征有直接指导意义。

items.title_en: Mutual information to all orders from modular flow: a replica-free approach
items.title_zh: 用模流给出任意阶互信息：一种免复制方法
items.abstract_en: We derive an all-orders long-distance expansion of vacuum mutual information between two disjoint balls in generic $d$-dimensional CFTs. The derivation uses a novel radial sewing expansion of the joint vacuum density matrix, together with a modular response formula for relative entropy and the geometric modular flow of a single ball, without analytic continuation in replica number. The expansion coefficients are modular integrals of modular-flowed vacuum correlators. Our formula provides a systematic treatment of arbitrary multi-point sectors, and recovers known results on two-point sector derived from replica methods. The full two-point sector resums into a modular integral of the thermal partition function on $S^{d-1}$, with an effective temperature depending on ball configuration and modular time. We compute the expansion explicitly in CFTs. In two-dimensional Ising CFT, using analytic reductions and multidimensional numerical integration, we obtain the first ten radial orders in the long-distance expansion, which involve sphere correlators with up to twenty spin insertions. The truncated expansion agrees well with lattice data at finite separation, and approximately satisfies crossing symmetry. Analytic calculations also reproduce known expansion coefficients for 2d free compact boson at self-dual radius and its current sector, as well as for free scalars in higher dimensions.
items.abstract_zh: 本文对一般 d 维共形场论中两个不相交球的真空互信息，给出全阶长距离展开。方法上采用联合真空密度矩阵的径向缝合展开，结合相对熵的模响应公式与单个球的几何模流，无需对复制数作解析延拓；展开系数为模流演化后真空关联函数的模积分。该框架可系统处理任意多点扇区，并重现复制方法得到的二点扇区结果。完整二点扇区被重求和为 S^{d-1} 上热配分函数的模积分。作者在二维 Ising CFT 中数值得到前十个径向阶，与格点数据吻合且近似满足交叉对称性。
items.highlight_zh: 免复制技巧，给出真空互信息的全阶长距离展开
items.digest_zh: ①问题：在共形场论（CFT）中，两个不相交球形区域的真空纠缠（互信息）随距离如何展开？传统做法靠“复制技巧”，需要对复制数 n 做解析延拓，处理高阶（多点）贡献时很吃力。②方法：作者绕开复制，改用两条工具——联合真空密度矩阵的径向“缝合”展开，以及相对熵的模响应公式加单个球的几何模流。展开系数写成模流演化后真空关联函数的模积分，天然能容纳任意多点扇区。③结果：完整二点扇区被重求和为 S^{d-1} 上热配分函数的模积分，有效温度依赖球的位形与模时间；在二维 Ising CFT 中借助解析化简与数值积分算出前十个径向阶（涉及多达 20 个自旋插入），与格点数据吻合，并近似满足交叉对称性；还重现了自对偶半径自由紧致玻色子及高维自由标量的已知系数。④意义：给出不依赖解析延拓的系统框架，把互信息的长距离展开推进到任意阶，为检验 CFT 与全息纠缠熵提供可计算的新工具。

items.title_en: Lee-Yang theorems for $q$-deformed oscillators and doubly-scaled SYK
items.title_zh: q-变形振子与双标度 SYK 的 Lee-Yang 定理
items.abstract_en: We show that the vacuum partition function of the $q$-deformed oscillator \[ L_q(z):= \langle0|e^{zT_q}|0\rangle, \qquad T_q := \mathsf{a}_q + \mathsf{a}_q^* \] satisfies the Lee-Yang property, i.e., all zeros of $L_q$ lie on the imaginary line for all $q\in[-1, 1)$, proving the conjectures of Okuyama'23. Using the connection between $q$-deformed oscillators and the Sachdev-Ye-Kitaev (SYK) Hamiltonian in the doubly-scaled regime, we show that the annealed SYK partition function satisfies the Lee-Yang property in the thermodynamic limit, that is, all of its Fisher zeros are on the imaginary axis. As a result, we show that the quenched SYK partition function admits a zero-free strip of constant width with high probability, rigorously complementing the large$-k$ replica calculations of Zlokapa and Kiani'26. We show the imaginary-rootedness of $L_q$ by expressing $\varphi_q(z):= L_q(\mathbf{i} z)$ as a locally uniform limit of ``$q$-deformed'' matching polynomials and then showing that those $q$-deformed polynomials are real-rooted. This establishes that $\varphi_q$ is real-rooted, and in fact belongs to the \emph{Laguerre-Pólya} class. The real-rootedness of the $q$-deformed polynomials yields novel log-concavity relations on the \emph{$q$-deformed matching moments} \[M_\ell(q):= \sum_{π\in\mathcal{P}_2(2\ell)}q^{\operatorname{cr}(π)}.\] We show the real-rootedness of the $q$-deformed polynomials by using the Touchard--Riordan formula to derive a partial differential equation relating their $q$-derivatives to their $z$-derivatives, and then analyzing the resulting motion of their roots.
items.abstract_zh: 本文证明 q-变形振子的真空配分函数 L_q(z)=⟨0|e^{zT_q}|0⟩（T_q=a_q+a_q^*）满足 Lee-Yang 性质：对所有 q∈[-1,1)，L_q 的零点全部落在虚轴上，从而证明了 Okuyama 2023 的猜想。借助 q-变形振子与双标度区 SYK 哈密顿量的联系，作者证明退火 SYK 配分函数在热力学极限下满足 Lee-Yang 性质，即所有 Fisher 零点位于虚轴；进而证明淬火 SYK 配分函数以高概率存在宽度恒定的无零点带，严格补充了此前的大 k 复制计算。证明思路是把 φ_q(z)=L_q(iz) 表示为 q-变形匹配多项式的局部一致极限并证明后者实根，从而 φ_q 实根且属于 Laguerre-Pólya 类，并由此得到 q-变形匹配矩的新对数凹性关系。
items.highlight_zh: 证明 q-变形振子零点全在虚轴，并推广到双标度 SYK
items.digest_zh: ①问题：Lee-Yang 定理说配分函数零点落在某些临界线上，从而导出相变的普适性质。Okuyama 此前猜想 q-变形振子的真空配分函数 L_q(z) 的零点全在虚轴上，并把这一猜想与双标度 SYK 模型联系起来，但一直缺乏严格证明。②方法：作者把 φ_q(z)=L_q(iz) 写成“q-变形”匹配多项式的局部一致极限：先用 Touchard–Riordan 公式导出联系 q-导数与 z-导数的偏微分方程，再分析根的演化，证明这些变形多项式只有实根，从而 φ_q 实根并属于 Laguerre–Pólya 类。③结果：猜想被证实——所有 q∈[-1,1) 时 L_q 的零点都在虚轴上；由此推出退火 SYK 配分函数在热力学极限下的 Fisher 零点全在虚轴，淬火情形以高概率存在宽度恒定的无零点带，严格补上了大 k 复制计算。副产品是 q-变形匹配矩的新对数凹性关系。④意义：把组合数学的多项式实根性、q-变形代数与 SYK 黑洞物理联系起来，为有限 q 下的 SYK 提供严格工具。

items.title_en: Inhomogeneous Synthetic Fluxes in Optical Lattices
items.title_zh: 光晶格中的非均匀合成通量
items.abstract_en: Synthetic gauge fields in optical lattices are usually engineered to realize a uniform magnetic flux. Here, we propose a scheme to generate spatially inhomogeneous fluxes and demonstrate how such fluxes reshape the single-particle spectrum. Within Wannier--Stark-assisted tunneling, onsite modulation produces a plaquette flux that depends on the orientation of the static tilt, whereas laser-assisted tunneling (LAT) does not. Using LAT, two coherent Raman processes with different momentum transfers imprint a dimerized Peierls phase that alternates the flux between neighboring plaquettes of a square lattice while keeping the mean flux fixed. A bond-selective Raman phase extends the scheme to the kagome lattice, where a parameter $ξ$ redistributes the flux between triangles and hexagons at fixed flux per unit cell. The Hofstadter--Rammal spectrum of the bipartite square lattice retains chiral symmetry for all $ξ$, whereas the kagome lattice lacks this symmetry, and its flux periodicity and reflection symmetries survive only at special values of $ξ$. As $ξ$ is reduced, the anomalous Landau levels of the kagome singular flat band are compressed toward the flat-band energy and evolve into a degenerate zero-energy manifold at $ξ=0$ with compactly localized states. The dynamical structure factor, accessible through Bragg scattering, resolves this evolution as a Rydberg-like series of peaks whose spectral span tracks the width of the anomalous-level tower and vanishes as $ξ\to0$. We discuss the frequency resolution and temperature required for its observation.

items.title_en: Spacetime Emergence in the Memory of a Learning Agent
items.title_zh: 学习智能体记忆中的时空涌现
items.abstract_en: We show that the causal structure of spacetime can emerge within the memory of a learning agent performing a quantum information task. We train a model-based reinforcement-learning agent to maximize the quantum mutual information between localized quantum probes interacting with a quantum field in Minkowski spacetime, without directly providing it with information regarding the spacetime metric or causal structure. In learning to accomplish this task, the reinforcement-learning agent constructs an internal predictive model whose planner develops the characteristic null structure of spacetime, allowing us to reconstruct the causal structure of the Minkowski metric with high accuracy. Within this task, spacetime geometry is obtained from an agent's successful predictions and actions, providing a first step toward showing that spacetime concepts emerge from operational quantum experience.
items.abstract_zh: 本文表明，时空的因果结构可以在执行量子信息任务的学习智能体的记忆中涌现。作者训练一个基于模型的强化学习智能体，使其最大化局域量子探针与闵可夫斯基时空中量子场相互作用产生的量子互信息，且不向其提供任何关于时空度规或因果结构的信息。在学习过程中，智能体构建出内部预测模型，其规划器发展出时空特有的零结构，从而能以高精度重建闵可夫斯基度规的因果结构。在该任务中，时空几何源自智能体成功的预测与行动，是“时空概念从操作性量子经验中涌现”的第一步。
items.highlight_zh: 强化学习智能体在记忆中自发重建时空因果结构
items.digest_zh: ①问题：时空的几何与因果结构，能否从一个只做操作性任务的智能体内部“长出来”？这是量子引力与量子信息交叉的一个概念性问题。②方法：作者搭建一个基于模型的强化学习智能体，让它操控与闵可夫斯基时空中量子场相互作用的局域量子探针，并最大化探针之间的量子互信息。整个训练过程不告诉它度规、光锥或任何因果信息，只给任务奖励。③结果：为了把任务做好，智能体内部预测模型的规划器自发形成了时空特有的“零结构”；用这套内部表示反推，能以很高精度重建闵可夫斯基度规的因果结构。④意义：这说明时空几何可以从智能体成功的预测与行动中被“读取”出来，是“时空概念源于操作性量子经验”这一纲领的首个具体演示，也为用量子信息任务反推几何提供了可操作的研究范式。

items.title_en: Temperature-Independent Logarithmic Current Slope in Interdiffusion-Broadened Silicon pn Junction toward Low-Power Thermometry
items.title_zh: 面向低功耗测温的互扩散展宽硅pn结中温度无关的对数电流斜率
items.abstract_en: With the development of cryogenic technologies such as quantum computing, there is an increasing need for low-power cryogenic thermometers that minimize self-heating. Here, we report an anomalous temperature-independent logarithmic current slope, $d(\ln J)/dV$, in heavily doped silicon p$^{+}$n$^{+}$ junctions with significant dopant interdiffusion and highlight the advantages of our device as a low-power, cryogenic thermometer. Electrical characterizations from 2 to 420 K reveal that, at low forward bias, $d(\ln J)/dV$ remains nearly constant, which yields a voltage-temperature responsivity that is nearly independent of bias current. The observed transport cannot be fully understood with conventional diffusion or direct band-to-band tunneling. Instead, the results suggest the contribution of trap-assisted tunneling. These results establish interdiffusion-broadened silicon p$^{+}$n$^{+}$ junctions as a route to low-power temperature sensors while providing insight into carrier transport in heavily doped semiconductor junctions.

items.title_en: Single-pass stochastic cooling for electron microscopy
items.title_zh: 用于电子显微镜的单程随机冷却
items.abstract_en: Scientific applications of free electrons, such as in electron microscopes and particle accelerators, are limited by the brightness of available electron sources. Accelerators can use phase space cooling to surpass these source limitations, whereas electron microscopes can only rely on particle filtering to increase beam coherence at the cost of reduced brightness. We show that strong electron-light coupling in nanophotonic structures makes it possible to achieve single-pass stochastic cooling inside an electron microscope for a lossless improvement of longitudinal emittance. This approach is laser-free and compatible with normal CW operation of electron microscopes. We derive a fully quantum mechanical model of stochastic cooling valid in the strong coupling regime, finding an analytic asymptotic formula for the optimal cooled energy spread $σ_{E_f}\simeq0.88(\hbarω)^{2/3}σ_{E_0}^{1/3}$, with $\hbar ω$ the cooling photon energy and $σ_{E_0}$ the initial energy spread. Numerical simulations confirm that the energy spread reduction is reflected in an increase in the purity of the electron's quantum state and a reduction of the longitudinal phase space area. Our work paves a path towards even brighter beams for electron microscopy, promising higher image quality, enhanced spectral resolution, and a route to reaching fundamental quantum limits on electron beam phase space area.

items.title_en: Quantum Private Information Retrieval on Forests
items.title_zh: 森林上的量子私有信息检索
items.abstract_en: We consider the problem of graph private information retrieval (PIR) in the quantum setting. We focus on a specific type of graphs, namely the forest graphs. A forest graph is a union of disjoint trees. We consider the quantum setting where all the servers share an entangled state. Each server is allowed to send only one qudit per retrieval round. We design a scheme for the forest graphs that achieves the rate of $\frac{3}{N}$. The scheme uses a GHZ state as the initial entangled state between the servers prior to the scheme initiation. We compare our scheme with the only work done in the literature that considered the quantum setting of graph PIR. We show that our scheme is more efficient in this setting. We derive the quantum capacity for the case of $G=3K_2$, which is equal to $4/6$. $G=3K_2$ is a special case of the forest graph. We design a scheme that is specialized for this graph, achieving a rate equal to $4/6$ and provide the corresponding matching upper bound, establishing it as the capacity.

items.title_en: Unifying entanglement and nonclassicality via the Narcowich-Wigner spectrum
items.title_zh: 通过Narcowich-Wigner谱统一纠缠与非经典性
items.abstract_en: Entanglement and nonclassicality are two fundamental features of quantum mechanics which serve as resources in quantum information processing tasks and are tightly connected by two-mode mixing. In this work, we show that the connection between entanglement and nonclassicality extends well beyond the two-mode mixing setting by considering the case of arbitrary multimode Gaussian evolutions. Using the Narcowich-Wigner spectrum as our main technical tool to quantify single-mode phase-space nonclassicality, we derive sufficient conditions for a single-mode state to generate NPT entanglement after a multimode Gaussian unitary evolution, which both tighten and generalize existing criteria. As an application, we obtain simple single-mode protocols for quantitatively testing the entanglement structure of multimode quantum states over arbitrary bipartitions. Our results identify the Narcowich-Wigner spectrum as a powerful tool for investigating fundamental properties of bosonic quantum states.

items.title_en: Quantum tomography on Schwartz space
items.title_zh: Schwartz空间上的量子层析
items.abstract_en: In this work we show that standard results in quantum tomography, which are typically proven in the context of Hilbert spaces, can analogously be established in the theory of Schwartz spaces. In particular, we will see that quantum states are equivalently characterized by their Wigner function, the characteristic of their Wigner function, and the probability distributions for a family of linear combinations of position and momentum. Physically, the latter can be understood as the evolution of its probability distribution in position over time under, for example, free or harmonic evolution. The result is obtained with techniques that are more accessible to a physicist audience, and shows that, at least for tomography results, the full structure of Hilbert spaces is not necessary.

items.title_en: Polariton tweezers
items.title_zh: 极化激元镊子
items.abstract_en: The non-invasive, deterministic manipulation of charge carriers remains a fundamental challenge in solid-state quantum technologies. Here, we demonstrate the concept of dynamic polariton tweezers capable of trapping and transporting electrons across a two-dimensional electron system via the long-range electrostatic potential of dipolar (d-) exciton-polaritons. By driving a semiconductor microcavity with a specifically engineered, non-collinear three-beam optical pump with TE-polarization, we synthesize a macroscopic polariton lattice with hexagonal symmetry. The spatially periodic field of this d-polariton condensate acts as a reconfigurable trapping landscape for the electrons. We show that introducing targeted frequency detunings between the continuous-wave pumps strictly breaks the spatiotemporal symmetry of the system, converting the stationary macroscopic interference pattern into a dynamically moving conveyor belt. By precisely customizing these frequency detunings, the entire lattice - along with the electrostatically trapped electrons - can be rigidly driven in any arbitrary in-plane direction. This precise phase-matching mechanism bypasses the need for a net kinetic momentum transfer, establishing a robust, optically controlled platform for the long-range routing of charged particles and topological defects in driven-dissipative quantum fluids.

items.title_en: Cage-enforced i-wave altermagnetism in boron-carbon clathrates
items.title_zh: 硼碳笼合物中由笼状结构强制的i波交变磁性
items.abstract_en: The spin splitting of an altermagnet arises from a rotation that relates its two magnetic sublattices. In known cases it is fixed by the crystal structure. Here we show that guest-host frameworks separate the two roles. In the boron-carbon clathrates $M$B$_3$C$_3$ the ordered cage removes the translation between the two guest sites and enforces cubic $i$-wave altermagnetism, with six symmetry-enforced nodal planes, for any magnetic guest in the compensated state; strain retunes the class to $d$- or $g$-wave. We demonstrate the platform with GdB$_3$C$_3$: its compensated antiferromagnetic ground state is a narrow-gap semiconductor with spin splitting of 0.19 eV at the conduction-band edge, and its weakly pinned Néel vector switches the helicity-resolved optical response on and off according to the magnetic point group. Thermodynamic stability at high pressure and dynamical stability at ambient pressure indicate that it can be made by the route established for this family.

items.title_en: On the Failure Probability of Quantum Leftover Hashing with Bad Seeds
items.title_zh: 论不良种子下量子剩余哈希的失败概率
items.abstract_en: We study hashing against quantum adversaries, as used in cryptographic applications, and provide bounds on the probability of failure in practical settings where seeds might be reused and might be non-ideal. Randomness extraction and privacy amplification are key components of quantum cryptographic protocols, such as quantum randomness generation or key distribution, that allow the compression of partially secure raw data into shorter output with high security. To ensure the security of any cryptographic construction that integrates them, it is desirable to establish composable security. This can be done by using methods based on universal hashing and leveraging the general leftover hash lemma, which allows extraction of near-uniform random numbers from an imperfect entropy source by sampling from an almost two-universal family of hash functions using a seed. This approach is taken in many practical implementations, commonly using Toeplitz hashing. The lemma provides an upper bound $\varepsilon$ on the distance of the output to uniform randomness, which holds on average over the choice of seeds. It makes no claim that any particular seed yields near-uniform random numbers. This poses a problem for practical applications where a seed is sampled once and reused for many rounds (blockwise hashing). Here, we study the subset of \textit{bad} seeds yielding far-from-uniform outputs. We show that randomness extraction against quantum side information is guaranteed to produce $δ$-close-to-uniform random numbers except with failure probability $\left(\frac{\varepsilon}δ\right)^2$. This result is generalised to blockwise hashing providing a guarantee of the security of $k$ rounds except with failure probability $\big(\frac{(2k-1)\varepsilon}δ\big)^2$. Moreover, we extend the general leftover hash lemma to blockwise hashing and relax the assumption of almost two-universality.

items.title_en: Exceptional Points and Optimized Encoding in Qubit Stabilizer Codes
items.title_zh: 量子比特稳定子码中的奇异点与优化编码
items.abstract_en: Continuous blind stabilizer measurements turn stabilizer codes into a Liouvillian spectral problem in which Hamiltonian terms compete with dissipative error channels. We show that this competition generically enables Liouvillian exceptional points, whose occurrence at weak error rates is constrained by the code distance. Exceptional points are detrimental in this regime of error correction as they maximize the decay rate of encoded coherences. We then optimize the encoding of the logical qubit using the eigenmodes of the Lindblad operator. This phase-optimized encoding cancels the linear short-time decay of logical qubit coherences. We apply this encoding to the [[5,1,3]] code and demonstrate that it outperforms naive encoding methods near the exceptional point, improves the fidelity of a logical $π$ rotation and remains effective in the presence of additional weak error channels.

items.title_en: Surface charges and quantum reflection of hydrogen-isotope beams at grazing incidence
items.title_zh: 掠入射下氢同位素束的表面电荷与量子反射
items.abstract_en: Experiments with cryogenic beams of hydrogen isotopes (hydrogen (H), deuterium (D), and tritium (T)) can be used to study quantum reflection from solid dielectric mirrors. Most dielectric surfaces carry trapped electric charges whose field polarizes the incident atom. We study theoretically how such charges, distributed randomly, in clusters, with compensation over a finite length, or in order, change specular reflection and diffuse scattering of H, D, and T at grazing incidence on typical dielectric mirrors (SiO$_2$/Si and MgF$_2$), for longitudinal velocities of 100--300~m/s and normal velocities of 3--100~cm/s which might become available soon in grazing incidence experiments. Starting from the exact coupled-channel equations, we show that the specular wave feels only the laterally averaged polarization potential, which is fixed by the structure factor of the charges and, for uncorrelated charges, is an inverse-square tail $-C_2/z^2$. The exact solution replaces the linear threshold law $1-\Rr\propto\vperp$ by the fractional power $\vperp^{2ν}$, $ν=(1/4-ζ)^{1/2}$, with the coupling $ζ\propto C_2$; for weak coupling, this appears as a logarithmic velocity dependence, and for $ζ>1/4$, the reflection coefficient oscillates log-periodically. At the surface charge density of $10^{12}$ cm$^{-2}$, absorption increases by up to 26\% for SiO$_2$/Si and by a factor of two to three for MgF$_2$; the effect increases with atomic mass, saturates for compensated charges, and is accompanied by diffuse scattering below $10^{-3}$ of charge-induced loss. We also formulate the condition of complete absorption at the solid surface.

items.title_en: Aberration stabilized light bullets in normal dispersion injected Kerr resonators
items.title_zh: 正常色散注入式克尔谐振腔中像差稳定的光弹
items.abstract_en: We investigate three-dimensional light bullets (LBs) in an optically injected, vertically emitting Kerr-Gires-Tournois interferometer operating in the normal dispersion regime. In the uniform field limit, the dynamics is governed by a generalized Lugiato-Lefever equation with third-order dispersion, paraxial diffraction, and fourth-order diffraction, stemming from lens and mirror aberrations close to the self-imaging condition. Using direct numerical simulations, we show that without aberration only transversely drifting, tilted multi-peak localized states (LSs) are stable in two dimensions, whereas no stable LBs exist in three dimensions. However, a small negative spherical aberration stabilizes a rich multistable family of two-dimensional LSs, including straight and tilted multi-peak LSs, oscillating states, and complex bound states, which persist even for negative paraxial diffraction. We identify an Andronov-Hopf bifurcation followed by a homoclinic transition toward tilted states, accompanied by hysteresis. Finally, we demonstrate that stable straight and tilted LBs exist in three dimensions in the presence of aberration, the latter forming a continuous family parametrized by the transverse tilt direction.

items.title_en: Lossless propagation bounds for long-range fermionic interactions
items.title_zh: 长程费米子相互作用的无损耗传播界
items.abstract_en: We prove propagation estimates for extensive fermionic many-body interactions with polynomial time growth, no loss of spatial decay, and an optimal threshold for the polynomial spatial exponent. More precisely, we construct local representatives of evolved fermionic many-body interactions on metric spaces with polynomial volume growth of order $d_{\mathrm{vol}}$ and suitable cell partitions. For the even Hamiltonian interaction $Φ_u$ and the even interaction $Ψ$ being evolved, we assume bounds, uniform in the site, on sums of term norms over finite supports $X$ containing a given site, with weights $e^{κ|X|}(1+\operatorname{diam}X)^a$ and $e^{κ|X|}(1+\operatorname{diam}X)^p$, respectively. Here $a>d_{\mathrm{vol}}$, $0\le p\le a$, $κ$ is sufficiently large, and the Hamiltonian bound is uniform in time. We construct local representatives whose interaction norms with weight $e^{c(1+|t-s|)^{-b}|X|}(1+\operatorname{diam}X)^p$ grow at most polynomially in $|t-s|$, for suitable $c,b>0$. In particular, $p=a$ is allowed: the Hamiltonian need not decay faster than the interaction being evolved. The threshold $a>d_{\mathrm{vol}}$ is optimal in general: uniform polynomial time bounds at $p=a$ fail for $0<a\le d_{\mathrm{vol}}$, even for smooth time-dependent two-site interactions. Polynomial time growth permits integration against filters with sufficiently many finite absolute moments, including those used in quasi-adiabatic constructions and quantum belief propagation. We derive consequences for filtered interactions and the dynamics they generate, providing dynamical estimates for perturbation theory with extensive perturbations, including gap stability, the principle that local perturbations perturb locally (LPPL), adiabatic theory, and response theory. All results also hold for quantum spin systems.

items.title_en: Efficient thermalization of one-dimensional noncommuting Hamiltonians via system-bath interactions with $Θ(n)$ ancilla qubits
items.title_zh: 通过具有$Θ(n)$个辅助量子比特的系统-浴相互作用实现一维非对易哈密顿量的高效热化
items.abstract_en: We prove rapid convergence of a system-bath interaction algorithm for preparing Gibbs states of one-dimensional noncommuting Hamiltonians at every fixed positive temperature. For a chain of $n$ qudits of local dimension $2^q$ with bounded nearest-neighbor interactions, the algorithm prepares the Gibbs state from any initial state to trace-norm error $0<\varepsilon\le1/2$ in expected total Hamiltonian evolution time $\widetilde{O}(n/\varepsilon)$. This improves the previously proved $\widetilde{O}(n^6/\varepsilon)$ bound for single-ancilla system-bath Gibbs samplers, up to logarithmic factors. The proposed algorithm couples $4^q-1$ resettable bath qubits to each site in parallel and randomizes the interaction time. Our analysis bounds both the one-round approximation error and the stationarity defect of an approximate stationary state in Gibbs-weighted $L^2$ norms, with only linear dependence on the system size. It also uses the dephasing induced by randomized evolution to control the extensive Lamb shift without treating it as a small perturbation of the dissipative dynamics.

items.title_en: Coherent 1-μm-Band Co-Transmission with C+L-Band Channels over 50-km Hollow-Core Fiber
items.title_zh: 50公里空芯光纤上1-μm波段与C+L波段信道的相干共传输
items.abstract_en: We experimentally demonstrate simultaneous coherent transmission across 1-$μ$m and C+L bands, carrying $54\times125$-GBaud PDM-16QAM C+L channels and $2\times15$-GBaud PDM-QPSK 1-$μ$m channels over 50 km, highlighting 1 $μ$m as a promising additional transmission window while avoiding gas-absorption constraints in C/L-band of HCFs.

items.title_en: Quartet state of the neutral nitrogen-vacancy center in diamond and optimized spin readout under near-infrared two-photon excitation
items.abstract_en: Photoionization of the excited nitrogen-vacancy center (NV-) in diamond leaves the neutral defect in a metastable quartet state of unknown energy. Using two-photon optically detected magnetic resonance with a tunable femtosecond laser, we resolve its onset in the spin contrast at 1.23 +/- 0.02 eV and, with the ground-state threshold from the same setup, place the quartet 0.54 +/- 0.04 eV above the neutral ground state. The threshold sets the optimum excitation for spin readout at 1060-1075 nm, in the near-infrared tissue window, with 26-37% higher shot-noise-limited sensitivity than at 1030-1040 nm.

items.title_en: Axion polarimetry with parametric readout: photon-number conversion and sensitivity limits
items.abstract_en: We propose a bias-assisted active photon-number conversion scheme for axion-induced polarization rotation in a four-port optical ring cavity with parametric readout. A calibrated real polarization rotation applied \emph{before} the final optical parametric oscillator (OPO) converts the otherwise quadratic response of the summed output photon number into a linear signal. We derive the resulting photon moments and the extracted-field covariance, retaining the four-port optical transfer, finite axion coherence and linewidth. Our principal phenomenological result is a prospective low-mass sensitivity window at $m_a=10^{-18}$--$10^{-16}\,\mathrm{eV}$, extending below the published exclusion bounds included in our comparison, notably the NuSTAR M82 limits. This is a conditional noise-equivalent projection, using the adopted $A/σ_A=1$ stochastic-power criterion and a parameterized technical-noise budget, not a confidence-level exclusion forecast. As a separate readout result, OPO-based total counting reduces the noise-equivalent coupling by approximately $5\%$ relative to matched selective attenuation in a favorable higher-frequency band; $5\%$ internal loss together with a $0.10$-rad pump-phase offset leaves a $3.5\%$ advantage in the stated example. A coherent input with only the final OPO retains this high-frequency benefit, whereas optimized coherent polarimetry remains more sensitive in the baseline. Our results identify both the operating principle of active number conversion and the stability requirements for a future implementation.

items.title_en: Agentic Pipelines for Mapping Topological Codes to Quantum Hardware
items.abstract_en: Mapping a prescribed many-body Hamiltonian to a particular quantum hardware is generally an approximate process, resulting in both intended and unwanted quantum dynamics. We introduce an AI-agent-assisted workflow that uses Lean to establish whether an effective device Hamiltonian retains the intended low-energy subspace of the target many-body Hamiltonian. We demonstrate this approach with topological quantum error correction (QEC), providing, to our knowledge, the first Lean-verified pipeline connecting a code space to low-energy states of a device model. Starting from qubits and parity checks, the pipeline constructs the ideal Hamiltonian whose lowest energy states form the intended code space, and determines the excitation gap that protects that code space. It then tests if the device retains the required number of isolated low-energy states and quantifies how closely their subspace matches the intended code space. We compare three bounds on unwanted energy shifts obtained by: summing the interaction strengths, grouping the anticommuting Pauli interactions, and diagonalizing the Hamiltonian. Pauli grouping yields a bound that is tighter than the conventional sum and closer to the diagonalization result, avoiding overly conservative compensation requirements. The workflow also identifies the strongest unwanted interactions and the qubits they affect, providing specific targets for improving device couplings and controls. We demonstrate our framework using an eight-qubit toric-code array on a superconducting device, where the same driven device generates both the required four-qubit interactions as well as unwanted dynamics. An AI agent identifies viable device parameters within a prescribed leakage budget, and Lean verifies four isolated low-energy states close to the ideal code space. Our workflow supports predictive hardware engineering for analog implementations of QEC codes.

items.title_en: Stabilizer Learning under Global Depolarizing Noise with Polynomial Copies and $2^t$ Time
items.abstract_en: We study learning the stabilizer structure of an unknown pure $n$-qubit state observed through global depolarizing noise of unknown strength, with a fixed promised upper bound below one, using destructive two-copy Bell measurements. Let $0\le t\le n$ bound the stabilizer nullity, let $\varepsilon>0$ be the accuracy, and let $0<δ<1$ be the failure tolerance. With probability at least $1-δ$, a learner must return a commuting unsigned Pauli group containing every stabilizer of the pure state; averaging conjugation by that group must decrease the purity of the observed noisy state by at most $\varepsilon$. Tang and Steckmann gave such a learner with polynomially many copies and $2^t$ times polynomial time when the noise strength is below a threshold of at most about $0.16$, which tends to zero as $t/n\to1$. They asked whether other algorithms with these resources can exceed this threshold. We answer this question affirmatively for every fixed bound on global depolarizing noise below one and every $0\le t\le n$, including states with only one promised independent stabilizer. Our learner uses polynomially many copies and $2^t$ times polynomial classical running time. All resource bounds hold on every execution. Their polynomial factors depend on $n,1/\varepsilon,\log(1/δ)$, with degrees and constants depending on the fixed noise promise.

items.title_en: Inline inter-core phase control in multi-core fiber with a commercial polarization controller
items.abstract_en: Inter-core phase control is a prerequisite for interferometry in multi-core fiber (MCF), but no compact inline element for this purpose is presently available, and existing approaches require fanout to single-mode fiber or free-space optics. We show that a commercial inline polarization controller, a low-loss and widely available component, can be operated as an inline inter-core phase shifter. Two-core interferometry on a jacketed four-core patchcord gives a reversible inter-core phase of $0.95 \pm 0.02$~rad from a single device, with an operating-point-independent lower bound of $0.38$~rad, driven through repeated load-unload cycles at a rate set by the actuator. A diametrically compressed disk model is used to predict the operating condition: with the input polarization aligned to a principal stress axis the device imparts a relative phase between cores without rotating the polarization state of either, which we verify by polarimetry on all four cores. The response is polarization dependent, falling to less than $0.58$~rad for the orthogonal input. The result is a practical, inline route to inter-core phase control and stabilization in all-MCF interferometers, requiring neither fanout to single-mode fiber nor free-space optics.

items.title_en: Geometric Phase and Spinor Beam Dynamics of Paraxial Beams
items.abstract_en: We show that treating a paraxially propagating electric field as a spinor provides a natural way to include geometric phase in beam propagation models. Importantly, by exploiting differences in the way geometric phase and dynamical phase accrue during propagation, we show that spatial variations in the former can have surprising and rather remarkable consequences for beam dynamics. As an example, we design a beam with a centroid that is predicted to follow a curved path through free space, a prediction we subsequently validate in experiment. The model presented herein does not contradict existing propagation models, but rather shows how to leverage the extra degree of freedom afforded by the spinor angle to make new predictions.

items.title_en: Qyantram: A Transparent and Verifiable Quantum Computing Platform
items.abstract_en: Most quantum circuit platforms focus on idealized circuit assembly and simulation, hiding hardware compilation, error identification, and variational model training behind black-box operations. QYANTRAM addresses this gap through an open platform comprising four subsystems, built around evidence-backed results and independent verification. Its staged compilation pipeline makes every transformation traceable, while the router publishes rejected SWAP candidates and their scores for transparent decision-making. Verification exploits inactive qubits remaining in the |0> state, reducing complexity from 2^N to 2^k for k active qubits. This mathematically exact reduction enables full pre-compilation verification on 127- and 156-qubit layouts, achieving approximately 10,000x speed-ups with execution times below one millisecond. The error identification engine exhaustively evaluates all Pauli error patterns without sampling, matching closed-form predictions within 2.8e-17. Its machine-learning engine achieves numerical agreement within 2.0e-15 of qiskit.quantum_info while training 25-50 times faster. The router introduces approximately 1.27x more SWAP gates than Qiskit's SABRE due to its omission of optimization, trading routing efficiency for complete decision transparency and traceability.

items.title_en: Dynamics of Fock states in traveling pulses
items.abstract_en: The quantum state of a traveling light pulse can qualitatively change the excitation dynamics of a two-level atom. We investigate this dependence for coherent and Fock input states using a virtual-cavity formulation with matched input and output temporal profiles. Analytical treatment of the master equation and numerical simulations show that coherent pulses produce damped Rabi oscillations, whereas Fock pulses can exhibit a partial recovery of the oscillation amplitude in the trailing part of the pulse. We examine how coupling to an auxiliary temporal mode and radiative loss shape this recovery. We also establish a connection with stimulated Raman adiabatic passage through an exact many-photon dark state and derive the associated adiabaticity condition. The observed recovery occurs away from ideal dark-state following. These results distinguish transient recovery in traveling-pulse scattering from conventional cavity collapse and revival, and clarify the scope of an adiabatic-transfer interpretation.

items.title_en: Spin SYK-dot chains: entanglement bound and resource estimates towards a quantum advantage
items.abstract_en: Ground states of Sachdev-Ye-Kitaev (SYK)-type models are volume-law entangled, which makes them costly both for tensor networks and for quantum hardware simulations. Thus, it remains unclear where quantum hardware could outperform classical simulation of such models. In this work, we study a spin SYK-dot chain, in which q dense SYK dots of p qubits are joined by single ZZ bonds of strength K. The entanglement across any cut is then bounded by floor(p/2) ln 2 plus the inter-dot entanglement, and the two-qubit depth of one Trotter step is set by p alone. A resource estimate shows that a quantum advantage for the ground state could appear only for dots of about 15 to 21 qubits or more. There, a single Trotter step already requires two-qubit error rates of order 10^{-6}, beyond the reach of noisy intermediate-scale quantum (NISQ) hardware. We test the assumptions of this estimate with an imaginary-time matrix product state (MPS) that applies each dot as one block. It agrees with exact diagonalisation at (p, q) = (6, 2). At (5, 2), a variational circuit with the same dot-plus-link layout comes within 3.6% of the exact energy, and noisy simulations show that its fidelity decays as assumed in the resource estimate. At (8, 5), i.e., N = 40 qubits, the energy converges at bond dimension chi = 768, far below the exact value 2^20, and the inter-dot entanglement stays small and is set mainly by K. Out-of-time-order correlators across the links decay on a time scale that shrinks rapidly with |K|. Thus, the dot size p and the inter-dot coupling K together set the entanglement of the chain, and with it where a quantum advantage could appear.

items.title_en: Universality and Emergent Classicality in Krylov Space
items.abstract_en: Krylov complexity grows linearly at late times for many systems. In this regime, we give a general spectral formula for the leading growth coefficients of Krylov complexity and its higher moments, without requiring detailed knowledge of the Lanczos coefficients. For states with a narrow energy distribution compared to the bandwidth, dynamics in the Krylov basis resembles motion along a classical trajectory. We demonstrate our results for the critical XY chain and double-scaled SYK. For the latter, we compute the leading late-time behavior of the chord-number moments through one-loop order.

items.title_en: Taming a macroscopic free mass through continuous quantum measurement
items.abstract_en: The free particle is the most elementary dynamical system in quantum mechanics. Despite remarkable progress in quantum control of increasingly massive solid-state mechanical oscillators, the analogous control of the free-particle counterpart has remained elusive. Dissipation and environmental noise have prevented such control in the inherently low-frequency domain of free-particle dynamics---a regime of growing importance for quantum sensing and tests of fundamental physics. Here we realize a suspended 1-milligram rotor operating in the free-particle regime with exceptional environmental isolation. Combining this isolation with a low-noise measurement architecture, we directly resolve thermal fluctuations in the motion associated with a damping rate of only 7~nHz. Through continuous quantum measurement of the rotor, we localize its otherwise unconfined motion, obtaining conditional states with entropic temperatures as low as 140~nK as a quantitative measure of control in the free-particle regime. This is two orders of magnitude below temperatures previously achieved in tabletop optomechanical experiments. We demonstrate immediate utilities of the new operating regime, setting new constraints on modifications of quantum mechanics and benchmarking inferred entanglement-to-decoherence rate ratios nearly two orders of magnitude beyond the state of the art for tests of gravity at the quantum-classical interface.

items.title_en: Correlated Catalysis Removes the Strong Converse for Entanglement Distillation
items.abstract_en: Entanglement distillation converts noisy shared quantum states into maximally entangled pairs using local operations and classical communication. The distillable entanglement $E_D$ determines the maximum asymptotic rate at which this process can be performed reliably. For several classes of quantum states, distillation above this rate obeys a strong converse: the fidelity with the target state vanishes asymptotically. Here we show that correlated catalysis removes the strong converse for every distillable bipartite state. Specifically, at any target rate $R>E_D$, the optimal asymptotic fidelity is given by $E_D/R$. Thus, although catalysis does not increase the maximum reliable distillation rate, it allows nonvanishing fidelity at every finite rate. Remarkably, this advantage persists even when the catalyst is returned exactly at every finite blocklength and the correlations between the output and catalyst vanish asymptotically. We further characterize the catalyst size required to sustain nonvanishing fidelity above the reliable distillation rate.

items.title_en: Writing with Near-Field: towards Atomic Resolution in Material Processing
items.title_zh: 近场书写：迈向材料加工中的原子分辨率
items.abstract_en: Direct laser writing with ultra-short pulses is the most flexible route to two- and three-dimensional (2D/3D) material modification, yet its resolution is judged against the optical diffraction limit. This review argues the opposite: the finest, most reproducible modifications come not from shortening the wavelength but from localising the absorber. Through the threshold effect and a transient epsilon-near-zero (ENZ) state - the dielectric-to-metal (Die-Met) state of the excited solid - the deposited energy is confined to a dipole-like nano-seed whose near-field intensity falls as r^-6 (ideal point dipole). The localisation is thus set by the seed size, not the focal wavelength, and the final feature is shaped by the material response: post-pulse heat flow, cavitation and quenching. We show that polarisation controls the anisotropy of deposition: the quasi-static near-field and interface boundary conditions select the writing direction and the modification orientation, down to a single defect. We survey energy-deposition mechanisms from 100 nm to the single-nanometer scale and link them to working engineering: stitch-free large-area patterning and record aspect-ratio (10^3-10^4) dicing and wafering of transparent crystals. Finally, we conjecture guided volumetric deposition, in which laser-inscribed lossy nano-seeds act as antennas that let cavity microwaves anneal the modified nano-volumes from within, as a 2.45 GHz oven heats food through water-dipole absorption. Throughout, atomic resolution is used in a quantum-confined sense and denotes a direction of travel: 10-20 nm features are demonstrated, while deterministic single-defect and single-bond modification remain goals. The thesis is that ultrafast direct write beats diffraction-limited intuition because the material itself forms a transient nanoscale absorber whose near-field and boundary conditions govern energy deposition.

items.title_en: Exact fermionic matrix elements from the Bethe-ansatz solution of the Richardson-Gaudin model
items.abstract_en: We introduce an effective Hamiltonian description of mesoscopic superconducting systems based on the Bethe-ansatz solution of the Richardson--Gaudin model. Our central result is a compact determinant formula for the matrix elements of fermionic creation and annihilation operators, expressed entirely in terms of eigenvalue-based variables. This formula allows single-electron tunneling terms to be represented directly in the eigenbasis of the Richardson--Gaudin model, extending the eigenvalue-based framework beyond overlaps and previously known form factors. As a benchmark, we apply the method to a superconducting Anderson impurity model comprising a quantum dot coupled to an ultrasmall superconducting grain. The resulting low-energy description, formulated naturally in the canonical ensemble, captures even-odd effects, subgap excitations, and quantum-dot physics. The same framework gives access to observables not previously computed for such grain-dot systems in the canonical ensemble, such as the fixed-particle-number optical conductivity and flux-tunable spectra.

items.title_en: Belief Propagation-Informed Tesseract Decoding of Quantum LDPC Codes
items.abstract_en: In quantum error correction, the decoder must estimate the errors from the measurement data accurately and fast enough to avoid a backlog. Search-based decoders such as Tesseract achieve high accuracy by finding a minimum-weight set of error events with an A* search, but their search effort grows rapidly with the physical error rate and the code size. To reduce this search effort while maintaining a logical error rate close to that of Tesseract, we propose a belief propagation (BP)-guided modification of the Tesseract decoder for quantum low-density parity-check (LDPC) codes. Damped sum-product BP is applied to the triggered detectors before the Tesseract search. If the detectors triggered by the BP hard decision match the triggered detectors, this hard decision is accepted directly, and the Tesseract search is skipped. Otherwise, the BP marginal probability estimates, weighted by a trust coefficient, modify the search priority, while the path cost keeps the channel-prior weights so that the decoding objective is unchanged. The framework also supports BP-based initialization, in which selected BP decisions form the starting point of a residual search whose signed-cost objective allows incorrect initial decisions to be removed. A node-exploration limit bounds this residual search; if the limit is reached, the decoder falls back to the BP-guided search on the original triggered detector set. The method is evaluated on the [[72,12,6]], [[90,8,10]], and [[144,12,12]] bivariate bicycle codes under circuit-level noise. With BP-based initialization and a global trust coefficient, the number of Tesseract search nodes expanded is reduced by up to more than two orders of magnitude at low physical error rates, while the logical error rate remains close to that of Tesseract.

items.title_en: Many-Body Correlations in Phase-Space Microscopes
items.abstract_en: The recently proposed "phase-space microscope" (PSM) extends quantum gas microscopes by allowing joint, single-shot measurements of position and momentum. We show that the $n$-body correlation functions constructed from such phase-space snapshots determine, in principle, all $n$-body observables of a many-body quantum state. This establishes phase-space imaging as a complete probe of strongly correlated matter, beyond what snapshots of position and momentum can provide---a limitation that goes back to a famous question posed by Pauli. Even without the full reconstruction of the density matrices, the PSM provides valuable insight into the quantum states. We demonstrate this power through several applications: witnessing entanglement hidden from both position and momentum, including between spatially separated collective degrees of freedom; resolving pairing structure across the BEC-BCS crossover, including the phase of the pair wavefunction and the reconstruction of its two-body Wigner function; probing inhomogeneous systems and preformed pairs without long-range order, relevant to the pseudogap phase; extracting the interaction energy in a magnetic field; and measurements of the local Chern marker. Furthermore, we discuss phase imprinting in the matter-wave Fourier plane as an alternative method for probing time-reversal-symmetry-broken phases such as chiral $p$-wave superconductors. Together, these results establish the PSM as a versatile new tool for exploring fundamental features of quantum many-body phases in strongly correlated quantum matter.

items.title_en: On physical origin of Berry connection of free relativistic electrons
items.abstract_en: No consensus has been reached on the appropriate operators for the spin and orbital angular momentum of free relativistic electrons. But there is a tendency to believe the existence of a spin-orbit coupling through the Berry connection. Here we show that this is not the case. Because the positive-energy solution of the Dirac equation is associated with the state of the electron, it is reasonable to postulate that only when projected onto the positive-energy subspace can observable operators on the Hilbert space of the Dirac equation represent physical quantities of the electron. On this basis, we find, after mapping the projected operators onto an irreducible representation, that the Berry connection describes the position of a quantum reference point with respect to the laboratory reference frame, relative to which the position of the electron is canonical. The orbital angular momentum of the quantum reference point about the origin of the laboratory reference frame is expressed in terms of the Berry connection. It combines with the canonical orbital angular momentum of the electron about the quantum reference point to give the orbital angular momentum of the electron about the origin of the laboratory reference frame.

items.title_en: Second-order mean force Gibbs state of fermionic open systems
items.abstract_en: Thermodynamics typically assumes that a system in contact with a thermal reservoir relaxes to the Gibbs state, or to the grand canonical Gibbs state when it also exchanges particles. However, this only holds when the coupling is very weak. Beyond this, the expected equilibrium state is the mean force Gibbs (MFG) state, obtained by tracing the reservoir out of the thermal state of the combined system. Despite its relevance, general analytic results for the MFG state have so far been obtained almost exclusively for bosonic reservoirs. Here we derive the grand canonical MFG state to second order in the coupling for a generic fermionic system coupled to a thermal reservoir at arbitrary chemical potential, using the concept of the mode reduced state in order for the fermionic MFG state to be well defined. The correction to the bare Gibbs state separates into particle and hole channels weighted by the empty and occupied reservoir states, related through the Kubo-Martin-Schwinger condition. We apply the result to the resonant level model, two modes coupled to a shared reservoir, and the single impurity Anderson model. For the two modes, the reservoir mediates coherence between modes that do not interact directly, something the bare Gibbs state cannot capture. We verify our results against numerically exact calculations, including real-time dynamics for the interacting model, and find agreement between the static prediction and the dynamical relaxation.

items.title_en: Brillouin comb line amplifiers for optical atomic clocks
items.title_zh: 用于光学原子钟的布里渊梳线放大器
items.abstract_en: Optical atomic clocks outperform the microwave clocks at the heart of current timing and navigation infrastructure by orders-of-magnitude, and recent progress in on-chip integration provides the opportunity to widely deploy them. Conventionally, a narrow linewidth laser interrogates the atomic transition, and an optical frequency comb divides its stabilised frequency (hundreds of terahertz) down to a microwave that is electronically countable. The laser(s) impose a significant size, weight, power and cost penalty, which is a current barrier to low-cost, scalable, fully on-chip optical clocks. Here, we position the frequency comb as the central engine of the clock by using Brillouin-amplified comb lines for atomic spectroscopy, which eliminates the need for stable clock lasers. Amplified comb lines reach an ultra-low frequency noise floor of $6\,\mathrm{Hz^2/Hz}$ at $30\,\mathrm{kHz}$ offset, an order-of-magnitude below a high-end commercial fibre laser. We realize a clock based on the $\mathrm{5S}_{1/2}\rightarrow\mathrm{5D}_{5/2}$ transition in $^{87}\mathrm{Rb}$ with competitive fractional frequency stability of $2\times10^{-13}$ at $τ= 1\,\mathrm{s}$, averaging to $9\times10^{-15}$ at $τ= 1000\,\mathrm{s}$. Lastly, we demonstrate a photonic chip-integrated Brillouin amplifier with a record 62.9 dB gain and up to 40 dB transferred noise suppression when pumped with a simple, low-cost diode laser. This opens a new route to compact optical clocks and enables use of atomic transitions lacking low-noise lasers by broadening a comb to the required wavelength and amplifying single lines.

items.title_en: Nonreciprocal generation of Bell states via cooperative dissipation in a qubit-magnon system
items.abstract_en: Directionally generating and controlling quantum states is critical in chiral quantum technologies. Here, we propose a scheme for the nonreciprocal generation of Bell states via cooperative dissipation in a qubit-magnon system, consisting of a superconducting transmon qubit and a yttrium iron garnet sphere subject to a bias magnetic field. The cooperative dissipation between them is induced by coupling both to a common transmission-line waveguide. Due to this cooperative dissipation, the system possesses a dark eigenstate within the single-excitation subspace. Under appropriate parameter conditions, the dark eigenstate reduces to a specific Bell state. With the assistance of a drive pulse, the system can be prepared in this Bell state (i.e., the dark eigenstate). In particular, we find that the dark eigenstate corresponds to different Bell states under positive ($+\mathbf{B}_0$) and negative ($-\mathbf{B}_0$) bias fields. Consequently, nonreciprocal Bell-state generation is achieved: $+\mathbf{B}_0$ yields one Bell state, while $-\mathbf{B}_0$ yields the other. Moreover, we define a fidelity-based nonreciprocal rate to quantify this nonreciprocity. Our work establishes cooperative dissipation as a versatile resource for nonreciprocal entangled-state generation, opening a promising route toward chiral quantum technologies.

items.title_en: Shot-to-shot statistical fluctuations during beam self-cleaning in multimode fibers
items.abstract_en: Beam self-cleaning in multimode optical fibers has recently been interpreted within a thermodynamic framework, in which nonlinear propagation drives the optical field towards a statistical equilibrium state. While this interpretation has been supported by measurements of modal populations and entropy, the role of shot-to-shot spatial fluctuations of the output beam has so far remained unexplored. Here, we experimentally show that the transverse output beam profile becomes progressively more reproducible from shot to shot as beam self-cleaning develops. This behavior is consistent with the thermodynamic expectation that relative fluctuations become increasingly small as the system approaches equilibrium.

items.title_en: Needle-beam generation from SPDC photons using inverse-designed flat optics
items.abstract_en: We experimentally demonstrate the generation of needle-like beams from spontaneous parametric downconversion (SPDC) light using a compact inverse-designed multilevel diffractive lens (MDL). The nonclassical nature of the SPDC source is independently verified through a three-detector heralded Hanbury Brown-Twiss measurement performed before the MDL, yielding a zero-delay second-order correlation value of approximately 0.14. Spatial measurements using an intensified charge-coupled device reveal that the MDL maintains a tightly confined focal distribution over an axial distance of approximately 11 mm under collinear SPDC illumination, substantially reducing diffraction-induced broadening compared with a conventional plano-convex lens of the same nominal focal length. Under non-collinear SPDC illumination, two distinct regions of extended axial confinement are observed, demonstrating the dependence of the engineered focal distribution on the incident spatial field. These results establish a compact flat-optical approach for engineering extended-focus SPDC photon fields, with potential applications in structured quantum photonics.

items.title_en: eigenkit: A Provider-Neutral Quantum Computing Library
items.abstract_en: Quantum software ecosystems provide increasingly capable tools for simulation and hardware execution, but differences in programming models, supported features, and backend capabilities can make it difficult to move and systematically compare the same quantum algorithm across execution environments. We introduce eigenkit, a provider-neutral quantum computing library that separates algorithm definition from backend execution through a common circuit representation and provider interface. The library currently supports 12 execution providers spanning simulators and quantum hardware, provides backend-independent gradient computation, and integrates with standard scientific-computing and machine-learning workflows through NumPy, PyTorch, and scikit-learn interfaces. We evaluate the practical relevance of this abstraction across both simulation and quantum hardware. Simulator performance varies substantially with circuit size, structure, batching, and application workload, showing that no single backend is consistently preferable. On quantum hardware, experiments on IBM Heron and IQM Emerald show that which processor is better suited to a given algorithm depends not only on hardware constraints, but also on how well the topology of the quantum algorithm matches the physical connectivity of the processor. These results demonstrate that backend portability is not only a software-design convenience, but can be important for both computational efficiency and quantum execution quality.

items.title_en: Inducing cooperative dynamics in an inhomogeneous many-emitter ensemble with a pulse sequence
items.abstract_en: Driving a many-particle quantum system with an appropriately tuned external field can give rise to features in its nonequilibrium dynamics that are absent in the equilibrium counterpart. Cooperative dynamics in a dense ensemble of quantum emitters manifested through superradiance, a burst in the emission intensity as a function of time, is typically suppressed by spectral disparities among emitters in the ensemble. We demonstrate the enhancement of cooperative dynamics in a spectrally inhomogeneous ensemble of quantum emitters when it is driven by a periodic pulse sequence. Using both a semi-analytical mean-field solution and a digital quantum simulation, we examine the coherence of the pulse-driven ensemble and the intensity of the emitted radiation as a function of the spectral disparity in the ensemble, as a function of time, the number of atoms in the system, and as a function of the inter-pulse delay. We identify clear signatures of the enhanced cooperative dynamics for the pulse-driven inhomogeneous ensemble when dephasing in the dynamics of the ensemble is suppressed by a sufficient number of pulses during the individual emitter lifetime. These results demonstrate a post-fabrication tuning knob based on externally applied control fields for the dynamics of the many-emitter ensemble.

items.title_en: Towards Optimal Routing Strategies for qLDPC codes on Silicon Spin Qubits
items.abstract_en: One of the major challenges of implementing high-rate quantum error correction codes, like qLDPC codes, is realizing the required long-range interactions. Spin qubit platforms can provide this connectivity by shuttling qubits next to each other whenever they need to interact. When doing this, the performance of the code depends on the shuttling strategy. We study memory experiments of the [[144,12,12]] bivariate bicycle (Gross) code on two shuttling grids for future spin qubit devices: a square grid and a square grid with diagonals. We compare three shuttling strategies, structured and random initial layouts, and a range of shuttling noise models spanning best- and worst-case scenarios. The best strategy minimizes the longest distance travelled rather than the total distance. The initial layout has only a weak effect, whereas adding diagonals to the grid reduces the logical error rate by up to two orders of magnitude which may have implications for future hardware design.

items.title_en: Full-Rank Constructions of Explicit Lossless Expanders and Good Small-Set qLTCs
items.abstract_en: We construct explicit two-sided lossless expanders whose binary adjacency matrices have full rank, and use them to obtain explicit asymptotically good quantum LDPC codes whose specified X- and Z-check matrices have full row rank and satisfy small-set soundness, or confinement, on a linear range. Our lossless expanders are a variant of those of Hsieh, Lubotzky, Mohanty, Reiner, and Zhang, with a free action of a finite 2-group. Under such an action, injectivity and surjectivity of the adjacency matrix are detected on a fixed-size matrix indexed by vertex orbits. Adding a sparse factor to the gadget at the middle vertices of a single type then enforces full rank, with a controlled loss in expansion. To obtain the 2-group action, we observe that reducing the generators of the Lubotzky-Phillips-Sarnak Ramanujan graphs modulo powers of 2, instead of modulo an odd prime, gives Ramanujan Cayley graphs on finite 2-groups. This construction may be of independent interest. Plugging two such expanders into the balanced product of Lin and Hsieh gives the quantum codes, since full rank of the input graphs is inherited by the check matrices. Our construction supplies the code family sought by Hong, Guo, and Lucas. Applying their analysis, within their framework and under their dynamical assumptions, gives quantum memories whose free-energy density is analytic at every positive temperature and whose guaranteed lifetime is $exp(Ω(N))$ at sufficiently low fixed positive temperature, where N is the blocklength. This improves the previously guaranteed stretched-exponential timescale.

items.title_en: Frequency-domain spin-wave logic gate based on three-magnon confluence
items.title_zh: 基于三磁振子汇合的频域自旋波逻辑门
items.abstract_en: Spin-wave-based information processing provides a promising platform for low-power nanoscale computing by exploiting coherent magnon dynamics and intrinsic nonlinear interactions. A key advantage of wave-based processing for efficient miniaturization is the ability to perform operations in the frequency domain without requiring separate propagation paths for the input and output signals. Here, we demonstrate a frequency-domain spin-wave logic gate based on resonant, non-degenerate three-magnon confluence in an yttrium iron garnet nanowaveguide. Under resonant conditions, two input spin waves at different frequencies efficiently generate an output spin wave at the sum frequency, which occurs only when both input signals are present, thereby directly implementing an AND logic operation. We further show that the output intensity scales linearly with each input intensity and is therefore proportional to their product, enabling analog multiplication of two signals. These results demonstrate nonlinear magnon confluence as a versatile mechanism for frequency-domain spin-wave logic and analog signal processing.

items.title_en: FLAMIA: FLAsh MIcroscaling Attention for Fast and Causally Safe Training on Blackwell
items.title_zh: FLAMIA：面向 Blackwell 上快速且因果安全训练的 Flash 微缩放注意力
items.abstract_en: Attention remains a substantial computational cost in Transformer training, particularly at long context lengths. NVIDIA Blackwell GPUs provide high-throughput low-precision matrix multiplication, but exploiting it in attention requires addressing quantization overhead, causal information leakage through shared scales, and numerical inconsistencies between the forward and backward passes. We present FLAMIA, a family of attention kernels for Blackwell with MXFP8 and mixed NVFP4/FP8 training paths. Our design combines token-block scaling that reuses quantized operands across matrix orientations, targeted safeguards against scale-induced leakage, and consistent forward and backward computations. Fused quantization and architecture-specific kernel optimizations reduce overhead, while document-local scaling and workload-aware scheduling support variable-length documents directly in packed layouts without repacking. Across various causal packed-document workloads, the MXFP8 path accelerates the combined forward and backward attention call, including quantization, by factors of $1.10$--$1.40\times$ on B200 and $1.06$--$1.42\times$ on B300 relative to the fastest evaluated baseline for each workload. We validate training stability and quality preservation on pretraining Llama-style models. These results show how jointly designing quantization, training numerics, and document scheduling translates low-bit hardware throughput into practical attention acceleration.
items.abstract_zh: 注意力仍是 Transformer 训练中的主要开销，长上下文时尤为突出。NVIDIA Blackwell GPU 提供高吞吐的低精度矩阵乘法，但在注意力中利用它需应对量化开销、共享缩放导致的因果信息泄漏，以及前向与反向传播之间的数值不一致。我们提出 FLAMIA，一套面向 Blackwell 的注意力 kernel，支持 MXFP8 与混合 NVFP4/FP8 训练路径。其设计包括：跨矩阵取向复用已量化操作数的 token 块缩放、针对缩放泄漏的定向防护，以及前后向一致的数值计算；融合量化与架构特定优化降低开销，文档局部缩放与负载感知调度可直接在打包布局上处理变长文档而无需重打包。在多种因果打包文档负载上，MXFP8 路径将含量化的前向与反向注意力调用分别加速 1.10–1.40 倍（B200）与 1.06–1.42 倍（B300）。Llama 风格模型预训练验证了训练稳定性与质量保持。
items.highlight_zh: 低比特注意力 kernel 兼顾因果安全与前后向一致，最高提速 1.42 倍
items.digest_zh: ① 问题：Transformer 训练中注意力计算占比很高，上下文越长越明显。Blackwell 这类新 GPU 擅长低精度矩阵乘法，理论上能大幅提速注意力，但落地有三只拦路虎：量化本身的开销、因果掩码下共享缩放系数可能把未来 token 的信息「泄漏」给当前 token、以及前向与反向因量化方式不同而数值对不上，导致训练不稳。② 方法：FLAMIA 按 token 块统一缩放，让同一份量化数据能在 QK^T 与后续矩阵乘的不同取向上复用，减少重复量化；对共享缩放可能造成的因果泄漏做定向防护；并保证前向与反向使用一致的量化与累加方式，同时把量化与矩阵乘融合，针对 Blackwell 架构专门优化。③ 数据调度：训练时常把多篇文档打包进同一条序列，FLAMIA 采用「文档局部」缩放加负载感知调度，直接在打包布局上处理变长文档，不必反复重打包。④ 结果：在多种因果打包文档负载上，包含量化在内的「前向+反向」注意力整体调用，MXFP8 路径在 B200 上比各自最强基线快 1.10–1.40 倍，在 B300 上快 1.06–1.42 倍；作者还用 Llama 风格模型的预训练验证了训练稳定、质量未受损。⑤ 意义：说明低位硬件吞吐要变成真实的注意力加速，必须把量化方案、训练数值特性和数据调度放在一起设计，而不是单独优化某一块。

items.title_en: Library of Layers (LoL): Adaptively Ordering Transformer Layers at Runtime
items.title_zh: 层之库（LoL）：在运行时自适应排序 Transformer 层
items.abstract_en: Computer programmers chain together the same reusable computational primitives, for example, conditional statements or loops, but in different orders to implement different algorithms. In contrast, existing language model architectures always execute their layers in the same order. We introduce Library of Layers (LoL), an architecture that dynamically orders its layers during inference to solve the problem at hand. LoL has a single hyperparameter, the size of its global library of transformer blocks, that allows it to transition seamlessly between parameter reuse and sparsity, generalizing the parameter-efficiency and FLOPs-efficiency tradeoffs of dense, depth-recurrent, and mixture of experts architectures in one unified family. We show that LoL achieves competitive performance with all three above baselines when pretrained on text data. On synthetic sudoku and maze data, we observe that the model employs distinct layer orderings to implement different solution strategies, and we can intervene on routing to force a model to apply a specific solution strategy to a problem instance. In a multilingual natural language setting, we find that LoL chooses different layer order patterns based on language and script. Similarly, we train LoL on safety data and fit probes to its router outputs, finding that these probes distinguish safe from unsafe text with high AUROC. LoL provides a path toward a future in which models dynamically compose their own computational graph, enabling more efficient and controllable reasoning.
items.abstract_zh: 程序员会把相同的可复用计算原语（如条件语句、循环）以不同顺序串联来实现不同算法；而现有语言模型架构总是以固定顺序执行各层。我们提出 Library of Layers（LoL），一种在推理时动态排序各层以解决当前问题的架构。LoL 只有一个超参数——全局 Transformer 块库的大小，可在参数复用与稀疏性之间无缝切换，把稠密、深度循环与混合专家架构的参数效率和 FLOPs 效率权衡统一到同一家族中。在文本数据上预训练时，LoL 与这三类基线性能相当。在合成的数独与迷宫数据上，模型用不同的层顺序实现不同解题策略，且可通过干预路由强制模型对某实例采用特定策略。在多语言场景中，LoL 依语言与文字系统选择不同的层序模式。我们还对路由输出拟合探针，能以高 AUROC 区分安全与不安全文本。
items.highlight_zh: 模型推理时自行决定层序，统一参数复用与稀疏激活
items.digest_zh: ① 问题：今天的语言模型不管遇到什么问题，都按同一顺序把各层跑一遍；但人写程序时会把同样的语句和循环以不同顺序组合，实现不同算法。模型能否也这样？② 方法：作者提出 Library of Layers（LoL）：维护一个全局 Transformer 块「库」，推理时根据当前输入决定调用哪些块、以什么顺序调用。整个架构只有一个超参数——库的大小。这个旋钮很关键：库小就反复复用同样的块（省参数、多花算力，接近深度循环网络）；库大就更接近混合专家（MoE）式的稀疏激活。于是稠密模型、循环深度模型与 MoE 三种范式被统一到同一族里。③ 结果：在文本预训练上，LoL 与上述三类基线表现相当，说明这种自由度没有牺牲基本能力。在合成的数独和迷宫任务上，模型对不同题型采用不同的层顺序，相当于用不同「解题策略」；作者还能人为干预路由，强制模型对某实例使用指定策略，证明路由确实承载策略信息。在多语言场景中，它按语言与文字系统选择不同的层序模式。用安全数据训练后，对路由输出做探针，能以很高 AUROC 区分安全与不安全文本。④ 意义：这指向模型在推理时「自编计算图」的范式：计算路径不再固定，而随问题变化，既可能更省算力，也让内部决策更可观察、可干预，兼具可控性与可解释性。

items.title_en: WebHarbor: Docking Real Websites for Evolving GUI Agent Environments
items.title_zh: WebHarbor：为可演化的 GUI 智能体环境对接真实网站
items.abstract_en: GUI web agents require realistic and interactive environments that remain stable during both evaluation and training. Live website evaluation suffers from changing content, access restrictions, and limited coverage of authenticated workflows, while existing synthetic environments for training often lack functional depth and visual fidelity. We propose WebHarbor, a suite of 153 executable and dockerized website environments that faithfully reconstruct the visual interfaces, content, and functional workflows of real-world web services under deterministic control. We build WebHarbor through task-driven human-agent collaboration, where environments evolve as new tasks expand their functional scope, coding agents implement the required changes, and human contributors audit visual fidelity, functional correctness, and task validity. The resulting suite comprises 3,518 tasks spanning multi-step and post-authentication workflows, where existing works often fail to cover. Beyond reliable evaluation, WebHarbor provides high-fidelity synthetic web environments for cost-efficient reinforcement learning (RL). We demonstrate that a Qwen 4B-level GUI agent trained with RL in WebHarbor generalizes to unseen tasks and performs competitively with leading open-source GUI web agents across four benchmarks. The code and data are publicly available at https://github.com/aiming-lab/WebHarbor.
items.abstract_zh: GUI 网页智能体需要真实可交互、且在评估与训练中都保持稳定的环境。在线网站评估受内容变动、访问限制与认证流程覆盖不足之困，而现有合成训练环境常缺乏功能深度与视觉保真度。我们提出 WebHarbor，一套 153 个可执行、Docker 化的网站环境，在确定性控制下忠实重建真实网络服务的视觉界面、内容与功能流程。构建采用任务驱动的人机协作：新任务扩展功能范围，编码智能体实现所需改动，人类贡献者审核视觉保真度、功能正确性与任务有效性。该套件包含 3,518 个任务，涵盖多步骤与登录后流程，而这正是现有工作常覆盖不到之处。除可靠评估外，WebHarbor 还提供高保真合成环境用于低成本强化学习；在其中训练的 Qwen 4B 级 GUI 智能体可泛化到未见任务，在四个基准上与领先的开源 GUI 网页智能体表现相当。
items.highlight_zh: 153 个 Docker 化真实网站环境、3518 个任务，可评估亦可强化学习
items.digest_zh: ① 问题：训练和评测 GUI 网页智能体需要「像真网站一样」的环境。直接用线上真实网站评测，内容会变、有访问限制、登录后流程覆盖不全，结果不可复现；而现有合成环境往往只有空壳界面，功能深度和视觉真实度都不够，智能体学不到真本事。② 方法：作者构建 WebHarbor，包含 153 个可执行、Docker 容器化的网站环境，在确定性控制下重建真实服务的界面、内容和功能流程。构建方式是「任务驱动的人机协作」：先定任务，任务需要新功能时环境就扩展，由编码智能体写代码实现改动，人类贡献者再审核视觉保真度、功能正确性和任务有效性。于是环境随任务集合一起「生长」。③ 规模：最终形成 3,518 个任务，包含多步骤流程和需要登录认证之后的流程——这正是以往工作常覆盖不到的地方。④ 结果：除用作可复现的评测台，WebHarbor 还是高保真合成环境，可用于成本更低的强化学习。作者在其中用 RL 训练了一个 Qwen 4B 级别的 GUI 智能体，它能泛化到没见过的任务，并在四个基准上与领先的开源 GUI 网页智能体表现相当。⑤ 意义：它缓解了「评测不可复现」与「训练环境不够真」的两难，把真实网站的可控副本变成既可评测又可训练的基础设施，代码与数据已公开。

items.title_en: Pretraining Data Scale Reverses the Muon-AdamW Fine-Tuning Gap
items.title_zh: 预训练数据规模逆转Muon-AdamW微调差距
items.abstract_en: Muon has recently emerged as a promising optimizer for pretraining large language models, offering a speedup over AdamW in minimizing pretraining loss. However, it remains unclear whether Muon's advantage persists after fine-tuning. In this paper, we study the downstream behavior of Muon and AdamW and uncover a surprising trend: beyond a sufficiently large pretraining data budget, AdamW outperforms Muon after fine-tuning. Moreover, as model size increases, AdamW overtakes Muon at progressively smaller pretraining token-parameter ratios. To explain this reversal, we view fine-tuning as a perturbation of the outputs and introduce the margin-to-spread ratio, which measures how far the correct logit lies above the wrong ones relative to how widely the wrong logits are spread. In language models, Muon has the larger margin-to-spread ratio at small data budgets and AdamW at large ones, mirroring the fine-tuning trend. In a linear associative memory, we prove that after one update the margin-to-spread ratio of gradient descent gains on that of Muon as the data budget grows, and simulations show that this trend persists after extended training.

items.title_en: Not All Reasoning Generalizes: A Case Study on Learning Generalizable Reasoning Strategies in RLVR
items.title_zh: 并非所有推理都能泛化：RLVR中学习可泛化推理策略的案例研究
items.abstract_en: Reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) can enable generalizable improvement for large language model (LLM) reasoning. This paper studies how to incentivize such generalization via reasoning strategies. We study this question with a controllable equation-solving framework: finding multiple inputs x for equations f(x)=y, where f is a non-bijective string function. This setting makes reasoning strategies observable while supporting a clear definition of easy-to-hard out-of-distribution (OOD) shifts, e.g., more solutions, longer y, etc. We uncover a subtle RLVR failure: it teaches the model to solve in-distribution tasks with high accuracy and structured step-by-step derivation, yet under OOD shifts, the same model abandons derivation and collapses to ineffective brute-force enumeration, causing sharp accuracy drops. This observation reveals the deeper challenges of RLVR generalization as it is neither incapable base model nor reward hacking, since the model succeeds in-distribution with the correct reasoning strategy. The key to mitigating this failure is an indirect intervention that surprisingly helps: co-training with bijective inversion tasks. Although these bijective tasks are actually not uniformly harder and even further from the non-bijective OOD evaluation, they make derivation more certain and substantially restore the correct strategy and accuracy under OOD shifts. This effect further motivates our theoretical analysis: outcome-only RLVR can shape reasoning processes through implicitly crediting the effective reasoning strategies more, even without process supervision. To conclude, our analysis framework and findings systematically reveal the crucial role and incentivization of reasoning strategies in RLVR generalization under OOD shifts. Code is available at https://github.com/ziqipang/rl_meta_thinking.

items.title_en: FADE: Factored Ability--Difficulty Filtering for Online RLVR Scheduling
items.title_zh: FADE：面向在线RLVR调度的能力-难度分解过滤
items.abstract_en: Group-based reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) learns only from prompts whose sampled completions disagree: all-pass and all-fail groups produce zero relative advantage and burn generation budget without moving the policy. Adaptive schedulers try to steer rollouts toward informative prompts, yet they rely on per-prompt pass-rate trackers that entangle two quantities evolving at very different speeds---the policy's shifting competence across reasoning skills and each prompt's intrinsic difficulty. When a single exponential average or Beta counter tracks both at once, short memory scrambles the relative ordering of prompts whereas long memory reports stale pass rates. We introduce FADE (Factored Ability--Difficulty Estimation), a bilinear state-space filter that separates the two timescales. FADE represents each prompt's success logit as the inner product of a whitened $K$-dimensional skill loading with a fast-drifting policy ability vector, minus a slow-shrinking scalar item intercept. Using Pólya--Gamma augmentation, each minibatch of binary rollout outcomes updates the $K$-dimensional ability posterior in closed form via a rank-$K$ Woodbury step, instantly transferring competence shifts to all unobserved prompts that share those skills while leaving item intercepts stable. From the resulting posterior mean and variance we derive a closed-form utility for the probability of drawing a non-degenerate rollout group. Across five reasoning benchmarks, two base models, and four scheduling paradigms under a matched rollout budget, FADE consistently improves downstream accuracy and calibration while adding less than $0.6$\,ms per step.

items.title_en: Thought-deciphering via hierarchical EEG-to-text alignment
items.title_zh: 基于层级 EEG-文本对齐的思维解读
items.abstract_en: Communication is important for our well-being, but it can be impaired by disabilities, such as locked-in syndrome (LIS), cerebral palsy (CP), and dysarthria. Non-invasive brain-to-text brain-computer interfaces (BCIs) offer a promising solution by providing an alternative communication pathway for people with communication disabilities. However, most recent breakthroughs have relied on large, cumbersome, and costly neuroimaging modalities, such as functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) and magnetoencephalography (MEG). Numerous studies have attempted decoding using the lighter and cheaper electroencephalography (EEG), but the results remain inferior compared to the other modalities. More importantly, we do not understand how these modalities are related to text at the letter, word, sentence, and higher semantic levels.
