Inspired by computational mechanics, we adapt static Variational MultiScale (VMS) theory to dynamic optimization, treating low- and high-dimensional spaces as resolved coarse and unresolved fine scales. Through a multigrid-style V-cycle, ENGINE alternates between spaces, dynamically probing fine-grained information in the high-dimensional space and injecting it to correct the efficient low-dimensional sampling process. Under appropriate assumptions, statistical analysis characterizes variance reduction and correction of curvature-induced bias, and convergence analysis establishes a stationarity bound for the corrected coarse updates. Evaluations on standard LLM benchmarks show that ENGINE achieves higher accuracy and faster convergence than existing ZO methods, achieving up to a $2.61\times$ speed-up in forward passes with zero additional peak memory overhead. Code is available at https://github.com/AI4Science-WestlakeU/ENGINE.

items.title_en: Strictly proper scoring rules for node selection tasks on graphs
items.abstract_en: In node selection tasks, the goal is to identify a single unknown target node in a graph. We consider probabilistic supervised node selection, where the estimator outputs a probability distribution over the nodes of the graph and the ground-truth node is available for evaluation. Classical evaluation metrics for such tasks are either statistically ill-conceived or blind to the graph structure. To fill this gap, we introduce two strictly proper scoring rules that are explicitly graph-aware: the Resistance score, which is parameter-free, and the Diffusion score, which operates at an adjustable coarse-graining resolution. We show that the Diffusion score interpolates between the multi-category Brier score and a cluster-level weighted Brier score. The Resistance score generalises two classical scoring rules: the multi-category Brier score and the Ranked probability score. Applied to rooted trees, it also serves as the strictly proper version of the improper Hierarchical error distance used in hierarchical classification. In the same setting, we furthermore establish strict propriety of the Hierarchical cross-entropy family, a recently introduced separate class of hierarchy-aware scoring rules. Experiments on epidemic source detection and on ImageNet classification confirm that the proposed scores detect meaningful differences in estimation quality that classical metrics miss.

items.title_en: A Human-Verified AI Workflow for Annotating Environmental Sound Data
items.abstract_en: Large-scale annotation of environmental sound recordings presents significant challenges under time and resource constraints, particularly when sound categories are imbalanced and only part of a dataset has been labeled. This paper describes the development and evaluation of a human-AI workflow used during annotation of the Kenya Forest Sounds Dataset (KFSD), using a project-stage working collection of 7,531 audio recordings across 21 categories. We investigated zero-shot classification, a feature-based ensemble, and a fine-tuned Audio Spectrogram Transformer (AST). The fine-tuned AST achieved 89.36% accuracy, 85.98% precision, 89.24% recall, and 87.58% F1 on held-out test data for binary classification of Person talking. Because this result remained below the predefined 95% threshold for autonomous annotation, model predictions were used as suggestions and subjected to human verification. Of the 5,026 initially unlabeled recordings, 2,337 were routed to a speech-verification queue and 2,689 remained for ordinary manual annotation. The verifier reviewed all 2,337 machine-labeled files and detected zero false positives, yielding 100% verification accuracy. The observed average verification time was approximately 4.2 seconds per file. At an average rate of 35 seconds per file for manual annotation, the hybrid workflow reduced work on the remaining queue from approximately 48.9 to 28.9 person-hours, saving about 20.0 hours (41%). The study documents the model-selection process, provenance-aware file organization, verification procedure, observed errors, practical limitations, and opportunities for extending AI assistance beyond one category.

items.title_en: DeepWaveRL: Self-Supervised Full Waveform Inversion via Reinforcement Learning
items.abstract_en: Full Waveform Inversion (FWI) is a fundamental inverse problem in geophysics to estimate subsurface properties, such as velocity, from seismic measurements. Recently, self-supervised learning methods remove the need for ground-truth velocity maps during training by leveraging a forward operator to simulate seismic data from predictions and backpropagate the gradients of reconstruction loss through it. In this work, we consider a more challenging setting without accessing such gradients. To this end, we incorporate reinforcement learning into self-supervised FWI and propose a framework named DeepWaveRL. Specifically, we reformulate FWI as a policy learning problem, where the policy network predicts velocity maps as actions, and a forward operator is used solely for simulation. A global scalar reward is computed based on data misfit for each prediction and used to weight policy gradients. Thus, learning proceeds without accessing the gradients from the forward operator. Given the indirect and coarse supervision signals, we further identify key strategies to stabilize learning and mitigate the spatial credit assignment bottleneck. Experimental results show that, despite relying entirely on a single scalar reward, DeepWaveRL achieves competitive performance compared to supervised and self-supervised baselines. These findings suggest that our framework offers a flexible and complementary learning paradigm for the FWI research community.

items.title_en: PaddleMaterials: An End-to-End Deep Learning Toolkit for Materials Science
items.title_zh: PaddleMaterials：面向材料科学的端到端深度学习工具包
items.abstract_en: Machine learning supports materials design, atomistic simulation and experimental characterization, yet models and workflows remain fragmented. We present PaddleMaterials, an open-source framework integrating heterogeneous materials-learning tasks while preserving task-specific representations and scientific semantics. It unifies data processing, training, evaluation, pretrained-model management and workflows across six task classes: property prediction, structure generation, machine-learning interatomic potentials, electronic-structure fields, spectrum elucidation and microscopy image processing. Task interfaces record physical quantities, units, aggregation conventions and references, making cross-task composition verifiable. A shared compiler backend enables switching from dynamic-graph to compiled execution through one setting, using graph optimization, operator fusion and hardware-targeted code generation without changing model definitions. Across 65 model instances in 11 groups, compiled execution accelerated every instance in eight groups, with group median speedups of 11%-224% and group maximum speedups of 11%-336%. Case studies on LiMnO2 and toluene link structure generation or spectrum elucidation, interatomic-potential relaxation, property prediction and electron-density prediction, using same-geometry density functional theory (DFT) calculations as references. For LiMnO2, predicted formation energies for generated and relaxed structures differed from same-geometry PBE+U references by at most 7 meV per atom, while the computational cost of model steps was less than one-twentieth of a DFT single-point calculation. PaddleMaterials extends unified materials workflows beyond conventional property, potential and structure-generation tasks while supporting verifiable cross-task operations and compiled execution.

items.title_en: CoworkOS:Scaling Agent Coworkers for Real-world Automation
items.title_zh: CoworkOS：面向真实世界自动化的协作智能体规模化扩展
items.abstract_en: Rapid advances in cowork agents are shifting human-AI collaboration toward real-world automation, delivering software, designs, and other artifacts. However, such productivity work demands both high-quality delivery on complex productivity tasks and continued monitoring and decision-making over long horizons, a combination that remains an open challenge. We introduce CoworkOS, a general-purpose harness for long-horizon work that separates task strategy from execution management: the model decides actions, delegation, and acceptance, while the runtime maintains state and feedback. Its three-layer architecture enables direct execution or delegation to Subagents, synchronously or asynchronously, under stable responsibilities. Through a shared application layer, humans and agents inspect and revise the same evolving documents, presentations, CAD models, and Blender scenes, so human-in-the-loop participation can enter both through conversation and through direct modification of the work itself. To sustain continuity across agents and sessions, CoworkOS further introduces hierarchical workspaces and persistent semantic memory, so working files, key decisions, and long-running Job logs remain shareable, reusable, and resumable after interruption. Across 12 benchmarks and 6 categories of real-world applications, CoworkOS proves highly competitive with frontier agent applications such as Codex and DeepSeek Harness. As a sustained-work case study, CoworkOS uses GLM-5.3 as its backbone to conduct RSI-driven automated post-training on Qwen3.6-35B-A3B. Over five rounds, the model's average score across eight benchmarks rose from 33.19 to 42.95 (+9.76). Looking ahead, we believe CoworkOS opens a meaningful path toward general cowork-agent intelligence.
items.abstract_zh: 协作智能体正把人机协作推向真实世界自动化，但生产性工作既要高质量完成复杂任务，又需在长周期中持续监控与决策。本文提出 CoworkOS——一个面向长周期工作的通用框架，将任务策略与执行管理分离：模型负责决定动作、委派与验收，运行时维护状态与反馈。其三层次架构支持直接执行，或同步/异步委派给 Subagent；共享应用层让人与智能体共同查看、修改同一份不断演化的文档、演示、CAD 模型与 Blender 场景；分层工作空间与持久语义记忆保证工作跨智能体、跨会话可共享、可复用、可续做。在 12 个基准、6 类真实应用中，CoworkOS 与 Codex、DeepSeek Harness 等前沿智能体应用相比极具竞争力；以 GLM-5.3 为骨干对 Qwen3.6-35B-A3B 做五轮 RSI 驱动自动后训练，八个基准平均分从 33.19 升至 42.95（+9.76）。
items.highlight_zh: 分离策略与执行的长周期协作智能体框架，支持人机共编同一文件
items.digest_zh: 【研究了什么问题】现有“协作智能体”能替人写代码、做设计、出文档，但大多只擅长短任务。真实的生产性工作往往横跨数小时乃至数天，需要一边交付成果、一边持续监控和做决定。如何让智能体胜任这种长周期工作，仍是开放难题。【用了什么方法】作者构建 CoworkOS，核心思路是把“想干什么”（任务策略）与“怎么推进”（执行管理）拆开：模型只负责决策、委派与验收，运行时系统负责保存状态、汇总反馈。架构分三层，既能自己直接执行，也能把子任务派给 Subagent，同步或异步皆可。所有参与者共享同一个应用层，人类和智能体可以打开并修改同一份文档、演示幻灯片、CAD 模型或 Blender 场景，因此人既能“用对话介入”，也能“直接动手改作品”。为让工作不断线，系统还设计了分层工作空间与持久语义记忆，保存工作文件、关键决策与长任务日志，中断后可续做。【有什么结果】在 12 个基准、6 类真实应用场景中，CoworkOS 与 Codex、DeepSeek Harness 等前沿智能体应用表现相当乃至更具竞争力。在“长期持续工作”的案例中，它以 GLM-5.3 为骨干，对 Qwen3.6-35B-A3B 自动做 RSI 式后训练，五轮之后八个基准平均分从 33.19 升到 42.95，提升 9.76 分。【为何重要】它重新设计了“人的参与方式”：不是让人盯着 AI，而是让人随时在同一件工作物上接手；并用持久记忆解决长任务“断片”问题。若此类系统成熟，AI 有望从单次任务工具变成能长期共事的“同事”。

items.title_en: IdeaTaste: Do LLMs Share the Research Taste of Human Researchers?
items.title_zh: IdeaTaste：大模型是否拥有与人类研究者相同的科研品味？
items.abstract_en: Research taste, the judgment of what to read, which problems to pursue, and which methods to try, increasingly shapes the work of AI scientists, yet it remains far less understood than their ability to execute research. We introduce IdeaTaste, a benchmark that scores an LLM by how closely the research proposals it writes from a literature snapshot frozen at 2025 match the work the same communities published in 2026. Our experiments span six contemporary language models and four research areas from established to emerging fields, covering more than 90{,}000 proposals in total. LLM agents fall well short of human communities in both the literature they cite and the ideas they state, reaching about 26\% of the human level on citation matching and only 18\% on idea matching. Their populations can cite as diversely as a community and take up its tasks and methods, yet rarely arrive at the concrete approaches and research plans it pursues. Neither richer field context nor larger populations substantially close this gap. In blinded expert review, AI proposals trail the 2026 papers least in presentation and most in expected success, echoing their gap in concrete approaches, and those whose ideas no human paper shares fare worst, suggesting weaker directions rather than overlooked opportunities. These results indicate that the main bottleneck in AI research taste lies less in finding the directions a community works on than in turning them into the concrete approaches it goes on to pursue. We release IdeaTaste as an open, continuously updated leaderboard (https://cxcscmu.github.io/IdeaTaste) that benchmarks contemporary AI proposals against future publication cycles.
items.abstract_zh: 科研品味——决定读什么、追什么问题、试什么方法——日益塑造 AI 科学家的工作，但其受理解程度远不如执行能力。我们提出 IdeaTaste 基准：让 LLM 基于冻结在 2025 年的文献快照撰写研究提案，再以这些提案与同一社区 2026 年实际发表工作的吻合度打分。实验覆盖 6 个当代语言模型与 4 个研究领域（从成熟到新兴），共 9 万余份提案。LLM 智能体在引用文献与提出想法上均远逊于人类社区：引用匹配约为人类水平的 26%，想法匹配仅 18%。模型群体可以像社区一样广泛引用，也能采纳其任务与方法，却很少给出该社区真正采用的具体方案与研究计划；更丰富的领域上下文或更大规模群体都无法显著弥补差距。盲审显示，AI 提案在“表述”上差距最小、在“预期成功率”上差距最大，且其想法无任何人类论文共享的提案表现最差，说明方向更弱而非机会被忽视。可见 AI 科研品味的主要瓶颈不在发现方向，而在把方向转化为具体可推进的方案。
items.highlight_zh: LLM 提案与未来论文的想法匹配度仅达人类水平的 18%
items.digest_zh: 【研究了什么问题】AI 已能写研究提案、做实验，但“科研品味”——即判断该读什么、该做哪个问题、该试哪种方法——很少被检验。论文要问的是：大模型写出的研究想法，与人类学术社区真正会去做的工作有多接近？【用了什么方法】作者构建 IdeaTaste 基准，做法是把时间“冻结”：让模型只看 2025 年及以前的文献撰写提案，再把这些提案与同一社区 2026 年实际发表的论文比对，从引用匹配与想法匹配两个维度打分。实验覆盖 6 个当代大模型、4 个研究领域（从成熟到新兴），共 9 万多份提案，并辅以专家盲审。【有什么结果】差距非常明显：模型提案在“引用了哪些文献”上只达到人类水平的约 26%，在“提出了什么想法”上仅约 18%。值得注意的是，模型群体能达到与社区一样多样的引用分布，也能抓住社区关心的任务与方法，却很少收敛到社区真正采用的具体方案和技术路线；给更多领域上下文、或扩大模型群体规模，都补不上这个缺口。盲审中，AI 提案与 2026 年真实论文差距最小的是“写作表述”，差距最大的是“预期能成功”，与其缺乏具体方案相呼应；那些找不到任何人类论文共享想法的提案得分最差，说明它们是方向本身偏弱，而不是被埋没的好点子。【为何重要】结论指出，AI 科研品味的主要短板不在“选题方向”，而在“把方向变成可执行的具体方案”。这对 AI 科学家系统的设计有直接指导意义：与其喂更多背景知识，不如提升把模糊方向落实为技术路线的能力。作者还公开了一个持续更新的榜单，用未来论文不断检验当下的 AI 提案。

items.title_en: Avatar Intelligence: Amplifying Human Agency Through Persistent Personal Agents
items.title_zh: Avatar Intelligence：以持久个人智能体放大人的能动性
items.abstract_en: Personal AI agents are increasingly capable of handling long-horizon tasks across applications, yet users often need to invest substantial effort in specifying goals, resolving ambiguity, and verifying outcomes. We argue that progress should be measured by how effectively agents amplify human agency: enabling people to pursue their goals with less routine supervision while retaining control over consequential decisions. We advocate Avatar Intelligence, a paradigm of persistent personal agents that represent users' goals, values, and constraints through sustained decision delegation across contexts and time. We describe a maturity roadmap from human-directed execution to autonomous operation within delegated domains, and introduce the Agentic Oversight Index (AOI) as a framework for evaluating delivered value against agent-side operational cost and human oversight burden. We identify three core research challenges: identity-continuous personalization that carries user preferences across tasks, user-situated evolution through Rehearsal Engineering, and safety mechanisms that combine technical control with accountability and recourse. These directions define a research agenda for reliable decision delegation to personal agents across tasks and over time.
items.abstract_zh: 个人 AI 智能体已能跨应用处理长周期任务，但用户仍需投入大量精力去明确目标、澄清歧义并核验结果。我们认为，进展应以智能体在多大程度上放大人的能动性来衡量：让人减少例行监督，同时保留对重要决策的控制权。为此我们倡导 Avatar Intelligence（分身智能）——一种持久个人智能体范式，通过跨情境、跨时间的持续决策委派来表征用户的目标、价值观与约束。我们给出从“人指挥执行”到“在受委托领域内自主运行”的成熟度路线图，并提出 Agentic Oversight Index（AOI），用以权衡交付价值、智能体侧运行成本与人的监督负担。我们进而指出三项核心挑战：跨任务保持偏好一致的身份连续个人化、通过 Rehearsal Engineering 实现的用户情境化演化，以及结合技术控制与问责救济的安全机制。
items.highlight_zh: 提出以“放大人的能动性”衡量个人智能体，并给出 AOI 评估框架
items.digest_zh: 【研究了什么问题】个人 AI 智能体已能跨应用处理长任务，但用户往往要花大量精力去说清目标、澄清歧义、核对结果。论文主张，衡量智能体进步的真正标准应是“它多大程度上放大了人的能动性”——让人少做例行监督，同时保留对重要决策的控制权。【提出了什么】作者提出“Avatar Intelligence（分身智能）”范式：持久的个人智能体长期代表用户的目标、价值观与约束，在不同场景与时间中持续承担决策委派；并给出一条成熟度路线图，从“人指挥执行”逐步走向“在受委托的领域内自主运行”。换言之，评估重点不是智能体能做多少事，而是它能不能替人扛下例行的判断负担。【如何评估】论文提出 Agentic Oversight Index（AOI，智能体监督指数），把“交付的价值”与“智能体侧运行成本＋人的监督负担”放在一起权衡，而不是只看任务完成率。这一视角提醒：一个频繁需要人纠偏的智能体，即使完成任务，也未必真正减轻了人的负担。【三大研究挑战】一是身份连续的个人化，让用户偏好跨任务迁移而不走样；二是用户情境化的演化，作者称之为“Rehearsal Engineering（预演工程）”，让智能体在贴近用户的模拟情境中成长；三是安全机制，既要技术层面的控制，也要有责任归属与申诉救济渠道。【为何重要】这是一篇立场与议程型论文，价值在于把讨论焦点从“智能体能做多少任务”转向“人是否更省心且仍掌控关键决定”，并为个人智能体的评测与设计提供了可操作的坐标系（AOI）与明确的研究路线。

items.title_en: Strategist: Evolving Reasoning with Agents
items.title_zh: Strategist：用智能体演进推理
items.abstract_en: A model is only half of an AI agent system. The other half is the inference strategy: the reasoning procedure that turns model calls into a response. Today that second half is written by hand, and the experience of building one strategy never carries to the next. We introduce Strategist, a meta-agent that evolves inference strategies across tasks. Each strategy is written as a blueprint,executable code that other strategies can reuse, and together the blueprints form a library. Given a task and a small development set, Strategist retrieves related blueprints, writes candidate strategies, tests them on real samples, and revises them from the results. Every candidate then enters the library, so later tasks build on earlier discoveries. On 30 benchmarks, Strategist beats the strongest baseline on 24 and matches its average accuracy (74.7% vs.74.0%) at 39% lower inference cost. Its strategies also transfer to unseen tasks and other models without further search. The part of an AI system that is not improved on its own now does.

items.title_en: Tracing the Scientific Discovery Capacity of LLMs to Their Training Data
items.title_zh: 追踪LLMs的科学发现能力至其训练数据
items.abstract_en: Large language models (LLMs) show growing promise for scientific discovery, yet basic questions remain about what enables reliable discovery. How can we trace the scientific discovery capacity of LLMs to their training data? We study this question as one of missing probability mass and develop a theoretical account in which monofacts-the facts observed once during training-set the discovery capacity. In materials science and regulatory genomics, we directly manipulate monofact rates in training sets and find that more monofacts consistently yield more discoveries across two open-weight model families, sampling strategies, and reasoning budgets. Further experiments show the relationship cannot be explained by training-set diversity alone and can transfer across scientific domains when paired with in-domain data. Together, our results identify monofact rate in training data as a key factor governing discoveries in language models.

items.title_en: ufakzeka-kulak: Building and Evaluating a 31.6M-Parameter Turkish Speech Recognizer from Scratch
items.title_zh: ufakzeka-kulak：从零构建并评估一个31.6M参数的土耳其语语音识别器
items.abstract_en: ufakzeka-kulak is an open Turkish speech-to-text model of 31.6M parameters, a FastConformer encoder with a token-and-duration transducer (TDT) and a CTC head, trained from scratch and released under Apache-2.0. It writes cased, punctuated Turkish with numbers as words. Its 4,977 training hours come from sources whose licences allow commercial use; 281 hours are human-transcribed, and for the other 4,696 the training text is an uploader subtitle or a machine transcript, kept only where a second, independent reading of the audio agrees with it. The recipe, checkpoint, labelling and export choices were made on development data, and the test sets were scored once, in a release gate fixed before training. With greedy TDT decoding the normalised word error rate (WER) is 0.0921 (95 percent interval 0.0792 to 0.1055) on FLEURS Turkish test and 0.0916 (0.0873 to 0.0958) on Common Voice 27.0 Turkish test, lower than Whisper base and Whisper small on both sets with paired intervals wholly below zero; Whisper large-v3 (greedy) scores 0.0604 and 0.0767. On conversational speech the WER is 0.3807. We also report punctuation and casing, degraded audio, and how closely each shipped export reproduces the trained model.

items.title_en: DiabAgent: Toward Agentic Physiological Control
items.title_zh: DiabAgent：迈向智能体化的生理控制
items.abstract_en: As pretraining scales, medical language models have advanced rapidly in clinical question answering. Their ability to achieve effective physiological control through sustained intervention still lacks systematic quantitative evaluation. Type 1 diabetes provides a concrete setting: impaired insulin secretion creates dependence on exogenous insulin, with dosing continually adjusted using information about meals, exercise, illness, and glucose measurements. We introduce DiabAgent, a research suite for agentic physiological control comprising the Agentic Physiological Control (APC) framework, the DiabetSim simulator, and the SweetBench benchmark. APC controls glucose through medical-device tools, using ongoing observations to infer individual states, accumulate personal experience, and choose treatment actions. We build DiabetSim to simulate different patients, events, and device conditions for scalable virtual testing and training. Using DiabetSim, we construct SweetBench by instantiating 32 scenario designs as 212 glucose-control tasks. With Claude Opus 5.5 and a fixed decision interval of one hour, APC achieves a COGI of 73.5, compared with 71.2 for the open-source closed-loop baseline OpenAPS. Ablations further show that individual adaptation and contextual information improve glucose control. Combining high-frequency rule-based control with lower-frequency agent decisions shows potential for balancing control performance and computational cost. Our work provides a framework, simulator, and evaluation foundation for agents to participate in human physiological control.
items.abstract_zh: 随着预训练规模扩大，医学语言模型在临床问答上进步迅速，但其通过持续干预实现有效生理控制的能力仍缺乏系统的量化评估。1 型糖尿病提供了具体场景：胰岛素分泌受损使患者依赖外源胰岛素，剂量需依据进餐、运动、疾病与血糖测量不断调整。我们提出 DiabAgent 研究套件，包含智能体化生理控制（APC）框架、DiabetSim 模拟器与 SweetBench 基准。APC 通过医疗设备工具控制血糖，利用持续观测推断个体状态、积累个人经验并选择治疗动作；DiabetSim 可模拟不同患者、事件与设备条件，用于可扩展的虚拟测试与训练，并据此把 32 个场景设计实例化为 212 个血糖控制任务。在 Claude Opus 5.5、固定 1 小时决策间隔下，APC 的 COGI 为 73.5，高于开源闭环基线 OpenAPS 的 71.2。消融显示个体自适应与上下文信息可改善控制，高频规则控制结合低频智能体决策有望平衡性能与计算成本。
items.highlight_zh: 智能体闭环控糖 COGI 73.5，超过 OpenAPS 的 71.2
items.digest_zh: 【研究了什么问题】医学大模型在临床问答上越来越强，但它们能否像医生一样通过“持续干预”把生理指标真正控制住，一直缺少系统的量化评估。作者选择 1 型糖尿病作为试验场：患者胰岛素分泌受损，必须依赖外源胰岛素，而剂量要根据进餐、运动、生病、血糖测量不断调整——这正是典型的长期闭环控制问题。【用了什么方法】作者构建 DiabAgent 研究套件，含三部分：（1）APC（智能体化生理控制）框架，智能体通过医疗设备工具操作，持续读取观测、推断个体状态、积累个人经验并选择治疗动作；（2）DiabetSim 模拟器，可模拟不同患者、不同事件与设备状况，用于可扩展的虚拟测试与训练；（3）SweetBench 基准，把 32 个场景设计实例化为 212 个血糖控制任务。【有什么结果】在 Claude Opus 5.5、决策间隔固定为 1 小时的设置下，APC 的血糖控制指标 COGI 达到 73.5，高于开源闭环基线 OpenAPS 的 71.2。消融实验表明，个体自适应与上下文信息确实能改善控制效果。作者还发现，把高频的规则控制与低频的智能体决策结合，有望在控制性能与计算开销之间取得平衡。【为何重要】这项工作提供了一套“框架＋模拟器＋基准”的基础设施，让智能体参与人类生理控制这类高风险任务可以被安全、可重复地研究：先在虚拟病人身上大规模试错，再谈真实应用。这对糖尿病管理乃至更广泛的慢病闭环治疗都有借鉴意义，也为“智能体能否真正参与人的生理调控”提供了可比较的评测起点。

items.title_en: NitiBench+: A Temporal Thai Legal Question Answering Benchmark Across 17 Domains
items.title_zh: NitiBench+：跨17个领域的时间感知泰语法律问答基准
items.abstract_en: Law changes over time. A court decides a case under the law in force on that day, and legal QA benchmarks grade answers against today's law. We checked 156,650 decisions of four Thai courts. Up to 67% of them cite law that has since been amended or repealed. We introduce NitiBench+, the sequel of our NitiBench, a Thai legal QA benchmark with 1,670 items across 17 domains, built from decisions of three courts. For each cited section it holds both the text in force on the decision date and the current text, and its retrieval corpus holds every dated version of every Thai statute section. Answers are graded on the Thai Bar Council rubric, the Bar-standard score, and on the overlap between the cited sections and the court's. The report has two parts. Part I measures the cost of the wrong text on 13 open-weight models. Reading the current text of amended law drops the Bar-standard score by 0.25 and missing repealed law drops it by 0.79. The penalty comes from rule changes, 0.45 on the 428 rule-changed items and none on the 331 wording-only items, and Citation F1 does not see it. The text in force is the fair setting. Part II benchmarks today's models on that setting. A public leaderboard ranks 26 models on a held-out test split of 500 items stratified by domain, with a validation split of the same shape released for public use, from memory alone, with the court's sections provided, and as a retrieval agent over the law in force, with the cost per item and the hallucinated citations. The best model scores 7.78 out of 10 and the best open-weight model 6.39. Without a search tool only five open-weight models recall any Thai law, and with it twenty of the 26 models gain and six lose. Leaderboard will take new models as they are released. Legal benchmarks must track dates, and on the right text today's models still leave a wide gap on Thai law.

items.title_en: VeriHarm-Bench: Measuring Harmful Success in LLM Coding Agents Verifiably
items.title_zh: VeriHarm-Bench：可验证地度量LLM编码智能体中的有害成功
items.abstract_en: Large language model (LLM) coding agents increasingly operate with shell access, allowing them to write scripts, move files, alter permissions, and modify system configurations. However, an agent may achieve a user's goal while causing unintended harm, such as deleting unrelated files, weakening access controls, or corrupting data, in response to benign inputs without explicit jailbreaking. This failure mode is particularly important because apparent task success may reassure users that an agent behaved correctly, causing harmful side effects to go unnoticed. We call this harmful success: the agent successfully completes the intended benign task while simultaneously causing unintended harm. Despite its importance, harmful success is difficult to measure because conventional task-success metrics overlook harmful behaviors, while existing safety evaluations are often designed solely to assess harmful outcomes. We introduce VeriHarm, an automatic framework for constructing programmatically verifiable benchmarks that directly measure harmful success. VeriHarm minimally perturbs coding tasks to elicit unintended harmful behavior while maintaining the benignity of the task and preserving the original task objective. It then synthesizes executable harm tests that, together with the original task-correctness tests, evaluate both task accuracy and harmful outcomes. Frontier agents, including GPT-5.6-Sol and Claude-Opus-5, achieve an average task accuracy of 95% on our curated VeriHarm-Bench, yet still struggle to complete tasks safely: their safe success rate, the fraction of tasks completed successfully without triggering the designated harm, averages only 37%. These results suggest that successful task completion can frequently coexist with unintended harm, and that task-success metrics alone may substantially understate the potential safety risks of coding agents.

items.title_en: Can LLM Agents Be Forward-Deployed Engineers? Requirement Discovery and Delivery for Enterprise Text-to-SQL
items.title_zh: LLM智能体能否成为前沿部署工程师？面向企业Text-to-SQL的需求发现与交付
items.abstract_en: LLM coding agents can increasingly automate model post-training, but whether they can act as forward-deployed engineer (FDE) agents, discovering customer requirements and turning them into deployment decisions, remains unclear. We study this on a real enterprise text-to-SQL engagement: a simulated customer, grounded in the real use case's requirements, starts with an ambiguous request. An agent must discover acceptance criteria, data permissions, and hardware constraints in the discovery phase, then plan and execute a post-training recipe in the delivery phase. Across 15 models, the strongest discover over 80% of withheld requirements and open-weight models discover 40-50%; in the delivery phase, only 25% of runs across eight coding-agent configurations pass all acceptance criteria. We identify four bottlenecks in this engagement: (1) incomplete discovery, with 40% of withheld requirements missing or misrepresented; (2) unreliable execution; (3) underused compute budgets and a lack of systematic comparisons across base models and post-training methods; and (4) benchmark accuracy does not guarantee production readiness. We suggest human review of discovered requirements, monitoring of the agent's plan during execution, and an explicit experiment-environment specification covering hardware, budget scope, and production checks.

items.title_en: Online Label-Free Gradient Matching for Continual Language Model Training
items.title_zh: 面向持续语言模型训练的在线无标签梯度匹配
items.abstract_en: Language models in customer-facing products must be continually updated, since the data they serve shifts over time. As retraining on the full accumulated data is impractical, each update should instead run on a small set of examples carrying the training signal of all data seen so far. The strongest current methods build this set by gradient matching, which synthesizes examples whose training gradients match those of the full data. However, they require ground-truth labels, run once on a fixed snapshot rather than on a growing stream, and are slow on large data. We introduce \textbf{OLGA}, which lifts these limitations. It distills unlabeled data by drawing the gradient matching targets from the model's own next-token predictions. Across five text classification benchmarks with phi-1.5, it improves accuracy by 10 percentage points over the strongest selection baseline using as few as five examples. OLGA also distills online data streams by keeping a running rehearsal memory of synthetic examples, which is re-distilled together with each new batch as it arrives. In the online setting, it outperforms the strongest selection-based continual baseline by 6.6 stream-AUC percentage points. Finally, our method scales to large data by pairing distillation with selection in a hybrid pipeline, letting selection handle the mild stage of compression and distillation the extreme one. It cuts runtime by 30\% versus distillation alone at similar accuracy, and beats the best selection-only pipeline by up to 12.6 percentage points.

items.title_en: Optimize the Harness, Not the Model: Fitting a Minimal Agent to a Self-Hostable LLM for Investigative Analysis
items.title_zh: 优化执行框架而非模型：将最小智能体适配到可自托管LLM以开展调查分析
items.abstract_en: Government intelligence teams need LLM agents that can analyze large, messy evidence collections, but security and cost constraints often rule out hosted frontier models and broad, hard-to-audit tool surfaces. We report CLEO: Constrained Loop for Environment Optimization, a method for fitting a minimal agent harness to a fixed, self-hostable LLM. Given an expert-validated dataset, CLEO admits only the tools, guardrails, memory policies, and loop components that improve accuracy while remaining general and auditable. On our held-out dataset, the CLEO harness reaches an 83.8% pass rate, within 1.2 points of the strongest out-of-the-box Claude Code SDK baseline, while being two orders of magnitude smaller.

items.title_en: Steering with Multilingual Lexicons for Sentiment Control in Low-Resource Languages
items.title_zh: 借助多语言词典引导低资源语言的情感控制
items.abstract_en: Activation steering offers a lightweight mechanism for controlling model behavior, but existing methods depend on sentence-level contrastive data that is unavailable for most of the world's languages. We show that multilingual sentiment lexicons are a viable substitute across three model families: aggregated multilingual lexicons outperform English-derived steering vectors for mid- and low-resource languages, while monolingual lexicons remain stronger for languages a model has specialized in during pre-training. The steering efficacy is mechanistically dictated by both representational density and pre-training priors. Large-magnitude English vectors overwhelm the compact representations of low-resource languages, causing "linguistic collapse." This fragility is mitigated by the norm-dampening of multilingual aggregation. Architectural biases, including bilingual specialization penalty and latent numerical rigidity, also heavily constrain cross-lingual steering responsiveness. Ultimately, our work establishes lexicons as a practical steering signal and offers a comprehensive mechanistic account of cross-lingual steering dynamics.

items.title_en: MultiInpaintCOCO: Fine-Grained Visual Understanding in Multiple Languages
items.title_zh: MultiInpaintCOCO：多语言下的细粒度视觉理解
items.abstract_en: Previous research shows that vision-language (VL) models struggle to understand fine-grained image details and tend to focus on the overall layout. Moreover, any weakness in English tends to be further amplified in the multilingual setting. To study that, we extend InpaintCOCO, an English dataset focused on fine-grained visual details, to 13 typologically diverse languages across five language families, creating MultiInpaintCOCO - a new multilingual benchmark of 953 minimal-pair examples. We further test several state-of-the-art models in multilingual multimodal retrieval, considering both light VL CLIP-like encoders and large language models. Our results show that performance degrades substantially for lower-resource languages, with the strongest predictor being the data resources available for the languages rather than typological similarity to English. In cross-lingual retrieval, most models exhibit a systematic bias toward English: when given a correct caption in a non-English language and an incorrect one in English, models preferentially select the English caption. This bias varies considerably across architectures. Among the tested models, Gemma 3 shows the strongest English preference while Qwen 3 is the least biased, despite both reaching similar monolingual accuracy across languages. The code is available at https://github.com/ufal/multi-inpaint-coco.

items.title_en: Specificity Bias and the Wikipedia Paradox: An xAI Analysis of AI Text Detectors under Domain Shift
items.title_zh: 特异性偏差与维基百科悖论：域偏移下AI文本检测器的xAI分析
items.abstract_en: The widespread adoption of Large Language Models (LLMs) demands reliable detection of human-authored versus synthetic text. However, current Transformer-based detectors often experience severe performance degradation during domain shifts and operate as opaque classifiers. This paper investigates the robustness and interpretability of fine-tuned Transformer models (DistilBERT, RoBERTa) by evaluating them against a custom out-of-distribution (OOD) dataset of hyper-local news synthesized via open-source LLMs (Llama 3, Mistral, Gemma). To analyze model decision boundaries, we apply a tripartite Explainable AI (xAI) framework using SHAP. Our analysis reveals three key phenomena: First, detectors often rely on a "Call-to-Action" syndrome inherent to instruction-tuned LLMs rather than generic machine text. Second, we observe a "Specificity Bias," where LLMs successfully bypass detection by hallucinating specific named entities and mimicking conversational imperfection. Finally, we illustrate the "Wikipedia Paradox," wherein formal, objective human writing is frequently misclassified as AI due to its low statistical burstiness. These findings demonstrate that purely statistical detection paradigms face systematic limitations in highly structured human domains, emphasizing the critical need for semantically-aware, interpretable detection architectures.

items.title_en: Do Agents Still Follow the Rules? Benchmarking Rule Compliance under Agent Context Compaction
items.title_zh: 智能体还遵守规则吗？智能体上下文压缩下的规则遵循基准测试
items.abstract_en: LLM agents compact long histories to fit their context windows, but the compacted context must still carry the operating rules that govern later actions. Prior work shows that violations rise after compaction, but measures compliance outside a complete agent harness and does not identify where each violation comes from. We introduce ARCBench(Agent Rule Compliance Benchmark), a configurable benchmark built on the open-source pi agent harness. Its tool-calling agent loop lets us measure rule compliance from actions taken during execution, bringing the evaluation closer to deployed agent workflows. Using ARCBench, we examine where violations after compaction come from, and how different compaction configurations and adversarial settings change their sources. We find that compaction rarely deletes the rule: most violations after compaction occur while the rule is still in the compacted history, with the agent treating a later request as permission, ignoring the rule, and proceeding anyway. Where violations come from depends on the configuration: how the rule is delivered decides whether the agent would break it even without compaction, while the compaction strategy and budget decide whether the rule survives. The strongest compactor-targeted attack more than doubles violations by corrupting the rule in the summary and changing how the agents behave, whereas the strongest defense restores the rule in most summary but still violates. Finally, retaining a rule does not guarantee compliance: compacted runs that retain the rule violate more than twice as often as runs with the full history.

items.title_en: Written Once, Read Differently How Language Models Own Answers Steer Their Next Ones
items.title_zh: 一次书写，不同解读：语言模型自身的答案如何引导其后续答案
items.abstract_en: When a language model answers a yes/no question, that answer changes how it answers a different question about the same entity. We study this \emph{self-commitment} in 22 open-weight models from four families (0.5B--72B parameters), fixing the model's first answer and measuring the shift in its second across 3,600 question pairs about 120 entities. Each answer writes a \emph{commitment direction} into the residual stream. The similarity of two questions' directions predicts their coupling on held-out entities ($ρ= 0.43$--$0.85$), and ablating a single direction shared across topics leaves at most 17\% of the effect in every model. How this direction is read is far less stable: the reading circuit spreads across more attention heads as models grow, instruction tuning makes more questions read it in the opposite sense, and in one model changing only the system prompt reverses the circuit's sign. Ablating the direction while sparing the attention sink removes most of the coupling at under 1.3\% perplexity cost in 18 of 19 instruction-tuned models, though it shifts standalone answers in two. Without the sink spared, the direction's alignment with the leading principal component of ordinary text predicts which models pay a high cost. Written once, the commitment is read differently across scale, training and prompt.

items.title_en: Dhārā Bench: An Evidence-Oriented Retrieval Benchmark for Indian Knowledge Systems
items.title_zh: Dhārā Bench：面向印度知识体系的证据导向检索基准
items.abstract_en: Dhārā Bench is a retrieval benchmark for Indian Knowledge Systems (IKS), with 325 questions in 12 categories and 60,121 text chunks from 15 source groups. The categories were developed based on 4,500 questions submitted to the Dhārā application; the evaluation set combines corpus-aligned application queries with expert-contributed questions. The annotations comprise 7,578 question-chunk relevance links involving 6,847 distinct corpus chunks. For 34 composite and multi-hop questions, 401 conjugate groups specify alternative sets of passages that jointly support each question. Chunk identifiers and hierarchical references connect the judgments to their source texts. The paper describes corpus preparation, annotation, and validation, and reports a fixed BM25 baseline implemented with Pyserini with $k_1=0.9$ and $b=0.4$. Across all questions, BM25 achieves MRR@20 of 0.315, Recall@10 of 0.182, and nDCG@10 of 0.205. On the group-annotated subset, complete-evidence scores are CE_Recall@20 = 0.294 and CE_MRR@20 = 0.141. The category results expose particularly weak verse retrieval, while group scores reveal gaps between finding individual passages and completing their support. The corpus and evaluation code are available at https://github.com/Avinash2236/Dhara-Bench.

items.title_en: ACTOR: Action-Centered Temporal Organization for Literary Role-Playing Agents
items.title_zh: ACTOR：面向文学角色扮演智能体的以行动为中心的时间组织
items.abstract_en: Large language agents for literary role-playing are typically modeled around dialogue generation, leaving characters' non-dialogue behaviors and their dynamic evolution over story time underrepresented. In this paper, we propose ACTOR (Action-Centered Temporal Organization for Literary Role-Playing Agents), an automated framework for constructing such behavior trajectories from raw novel texts. ACTOR extracts dialogue and persona-relevant non-dialogue behaviors, represents each behavior using a Thought-Action-Observation structure, and organizes behavior trajectories according to the internal temporal order of the story. We build a behavior dataset from 143 diverse literary works. For each source behavior, we generate counterfactual behaviors that are contextually plausible yet inconsistent with the character's persona. We find that existing models struggle to reliably infer character-consistent actions from historical behaviors and evolving character states. Using these behavior pairs, we train models with Regularized Preference Optimization (RPO), which augments DPO with a negative log-likelihood loss on the source behavior to jointly optimize behavior preference and generation. We further design a four-way next-behavior selection task to evaluate the model's ability to faithfully mimic character actions. Across 17,560 evaluation instances, the model trained on ACTOR's preference pairs achieves substantially improved accuracy. This result demonstrates that structured, temporally organized supervision enables models to leverage character profiles and prior behaviors to infer subsequent actions, greatly advancing literary role-playing beyond mere dialogue imitation. Code and data are available at https://github.com/SilentStar233/ACTOR.

items.title_en: Every Clause Counts: Instruction-Following Reranking by Multiplying Small, Answerable Questions
items.abstract_en: People often attach instructions to their search queries, asking for pages written for beginners, documents in a certain language or official sources only. Most rerankers were trained to judge topical relevance and treat such instructions as a few extra words. On the InfoSearch benchmark, even GPT-4o used as a list-wise reranker reaches an average WISE (Weighted Instruction Sensitivity Evaluation) of only 33.5. We present DMReranker (Decision-Model Reranker), a zero-shot reranker that splits an instructed query into a topic and a short list of typed clauses. A small judge model answers one narrow question per clause, and the answer probabilities are multiplied into a single score. Nothing is trained, and the configuration was frozen before the test runs. Reranking the same top-100 candidates as the published baselines, DMReranker reaches a macro WISE of 50.9 over all six InfoSearch dimensions while keeping original-mode nDCG@10 at 82.9. It trails GPT-4o on the stricter SICR (Strict Instruction Compliance Ratio) metric, 19.2 against 32.1. We show that this gap follows from how a product of probabilities behaves when SICR compares raw scores across runs. Computed from ranks, our SICR is 67.0. On the same judge, splitting the instruction raises WISE from 32.9 to 47.6 over a single combined question, while raw-score SICR falls. Scoring all six dimensions cost about $10 at list price.

items.title_en: DepthGraft: Structural Regularization through Hierarchical Cross-Layer KV Reconstruction
items.abstract_en: Scaling depth is a key route to stronger large language models, but Pre-LN architectures often suffer from depth-wise information dilution, limiting the effective use of deep layers. While cross-layer connectivity has proven effective at mitigating this problem, existing designs usually introduce additional computation or memory access. We revisit cross-layer KV sharing as an efficient form of such connectivity. Beyond cache compression, each KV reuse edge creates a direct gradient path from deep layers to source KV projections, turning KV sharing into an implicit structural regularizer for KV representation geometry. We provide a systematic analysis of this mechanism, showing that proper sharing topologies sharpen key retrieval directions while enriching the value content subspace, whereas existing adjacent or global-anchor designs do not fully exploit this effect. Motivated by this, we propose DepthGraft, a hierarchical KV-sharing architecture that reconstructs deep-layer KV from stride-aligned shallow-middle source pairs. DepthGraft distributes non-local gradient flow across source layers, while preserving prefill early completion and reducing KV cache by roughly one third. Experiments on dense and MoE models from 0.5B to 16B parameters show consistent downstream improvements under both GQA and MLA. Notably, on the 16B MoE model, DepthGraft achieves a 7.0% absolute improvement on MMLU-Pro, along with gains of 6.6% on CMMLU and 6.4% on C3. These results validate the potential of DepthGraft as a scalable design for large-scale pretraining. The project page is available at https://github.com/jianke0604/DepthGraft.

items.title_en: Meet Students Where They Are: Student-Prefix Teacher Adaptation for On-Policy Distillation
items.abstract_en: On-policy distillation (OPD) mitigates the student's exposure bias by optimizing on student-generated trajectories. However, student-generated prefixes may contain reasoning errors or follow patterns unfamiliar to the teacher, undermining the reliability of its token-level supervision. This degradation becomes more pronounced as prefixes grow longer. To address this teacher-side distribution mismatch, we propose Student-Prefix Teacher Adaptation (SPTA), which adapts the teacher to the states on which it is queried during distillation. Specifically, before OPD starts, we collect student rollout prefixes with random lengths and continually train the teacher to continue from the prefixes using reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR). By treating each prefix as context and rewarding correct final answers, the teacher learns to recover from student-induced states rather than imitate the student's reasoning. Then, the adapted teacher is used for standard OPD, with no changes to the distillation objective. Experiments on mathematical reasoning benchmarks show that our SPTA improves average student performance over standard OPD and OPD with task-level RLVR-adapted teachers. These results highlight the importance of adapting teachers not only to solve problems independently, but also to provide reliable guidance on the states their students actually visit.

items.title_en: SAGE (Subjectivity-Aware Generation Estimator): A Linguistic Framework for AI-Generated Review Detection *
items.abstract_en: We propose a simple, linguistically motivated approach to detecting AI-generated peer reviews based on the inherently human trait of subjectivity. We capture subjectivity at two levels: the semantic level of evaluative language and modality and the pragmatic level of speech acts. Using features derived from speech act annotations and model-predicted subjectivity scores, we train a lightweight classifier that achieves an AUROC of 0.9566 with only these linguistic features. Combining its output with the state-of-the-art detector Sem-Detect raises the TPR at 1% FPR of Sem-Detect on the APRDB benchmark from 0.874 to 0.985, outperforming the current state of the art. Our results show that linguistic features of subjectivity provide an explainable source of information for detecting AI-generated peer reviews and can be readily integrated into existing detection methods. The code and models are publicly available on GitHub (https://github.com/Arys02/generated\_ text\_detection\_hub) and Hugging Face (https://huggingface.co/Arys02), respectively.

items.title_en: Unlocking Criminal Court Decisions: Flexible Information Extraction for Empirical Legal Research
items.abstract_en: Criminal verdicts contain descriptions of criminal behavior that can support quantitative legal research, but structuring them requires attributes and extraction rules that cannot always be fully specified in advance. We present an LLM-based pipeline that builds a structured dataset through attribute exploration, text span extraction, and value normalization, guided by annotation instructions that legal experts can refine. We evaluate it on two traffic offenses: driving under the influence (DUI) and driving despite a ban (DDB). For DUI, revising the instructions was associated with higher extraction accuracy (from 52% to 70% of correctly extracted values) and higher agreement between human annotators. Repeated runs of the same model agreed with each other more than with the gold annotations, showing that consistent output is not necessarily correct, while disagreement between annotators and between models helped reveal unclear instructions. For DDB, where the instructions defined fixed categories and output formats, agreement was high for most attributes.

items.title_en: Finding Errors Is Not Enough: Selective Model Escalation for Entity-Targeted Sentiment Analysis
items.abstract_en: Improving a sentiment classifier with limited resources involves more than simply deciding how much data to collect or which model to train. A labelled collection may lack examples of an important class. Once trained, a classifier may benefit from another model even when that model is weaker on its own. We study these decisions in document-level Entity-Level Sentiment Analysis (ELSA), primarily using South Slavic news. We first compare acquisition orders as collections grow. We then use uncertainty to choose which predictions to revisit, how many to process, and whether an alternative encoder or local LLM can correct them. Finally, we select complete routing policies on development data for held-out evaluation. Minority-prioritised acquisition helps at some very small training sizes, but not consistently thereafter. On SentiCoref, an oracle correcting all errors in the least-confident 10% without harming correct predictions would add 9.14 Macro-F1 points; however the best evaluated action gains only 0.90. Encoder averaging helps on AspectBench and NewsMTSC but harms SentiCoref, where selective LLM assistance is more promising. Both development-selected policies route 30% of records to the encoder-assisted LLM, yielding observed gains of 1.02 points on SentiCoref (interval includes zero) and 1.71 on NewsMTSC, at substantially different inference costs.

items.title_en: Distilling Literary Sentiment from LLM Annotations into an Ordinal BERT Model
items.abstract_en: The scarcity of human-annotated literary corpora limits the development of domain-specific sentiment analysis models. This study investigates whether LLM-generated annotations can supervise smaller models for literary sentiment analysis. We fine-tune five BERT models using ordinal regression on 10,889 literary sentences annotated by Gemma 4 31B on a ten-point sentiment scale. The models are evaluated against 1,923 human-annotated sentences from Hemingway's "The Old Man and the Sea", alongside the teacher model and conventional baselines. BERT-large achieves a Kendall's $τ$ of 0.589, approaching the teacher's 0.604. Although a constant-neutral predictor achieves the lowest overall mean absolute error (MAE), BERT-base outperforms the teacher on non-neutral sentences, achieving an MAE of 0.726 versus 1.116. These findings demonstrate the potential of LLM-generated supervision for developing smaller literary sentiment models, while highlighting the limitations of aggregate error metrics on predominantly neutral datasets.

items.title_en: TAMPAgent: Agentic Belief-Space Planning for Mobile Manipulation
items.title_zh: TAMPAgent：面向移动操作的智能体化信念空间规划
items.abstract_en: Open-world robotic mobile manipulation requires acting in physical environments with only partial information. While recent Large Vision-Language Model (LVLM) agents show strong open-world reasoning capabilities, existing architectures that rely on direct tool calling struggle with geometric uncertainty and thus are limited to fully-observable tabletop environments. In contrast, Task and Motion Planning (TAMP) systems can solve long-horizon tasks under partial observability but incur high computational costs and require closed worlds. We propose \textbf{TAMPAgent}, an agentic planning framework that unifies the reasoning of LVLMs with the structured constraint satisfaction of TAMP systems. We endow an LVLM agent with a belief-space planning model operating over an extensible API of perception, planning, and control tools. The agent formulates a partial task plan composed of parameterized observation and execution actions, which is subsequently completed using classical search algorithms. After extracting the plan's geometric constraints, the agent leverages its tool API to bind valid parameter values, satisfying feasibility requirements and producing an executable motion plan. Upon execution, the agent continuously updates its belief history and repeats this closed-loop process by interleaving observation and manipulation actions. Evaluated across complex household mobile manipulation tasks on Rainbow Y1 and Unitree G1 platforms, TAMPAgent significantly outperforms direct tool-calling agentic baselines, demonstrating that integrating TAMP constraint satisfaction into agentic planning loops is essential for unstructured, partially observable environments.
items.abstract_zh: 开放世界移动操作需要在信息不完整的物理环境中行动。现有大型视觉语言模型（LVLM）智能体虽具备很强的开放世界推理能力，但依赖直接调用工具，难以处理几何不确定性，只能用于完全可观测的桌面场景；任务与运动规划（TAMP）可求解部分可观测下的长时程任务，却计算代价高且要求封闭世界。本文提出 TAMPAgent，把 LVLM 的推理与 TAMP 的结构化约束满足结合起来：LVLM 智能体在可扩展的感知、规划与控制工具 API 上构建由参数化观察和执行动作组成的部分计划，再由经典搜索算法补全，并借助工具 API 绑定满足几何约束的参数值，生成可执行运动计划；执行过程中持续更新信念历史，交替观察与操作形成闭环。在 Rainbow Y1 与 Unitree G1 平台上的复杂家庭移动操作任务中，该方法显著优于直接调用工具的智能体基线，表明将 TAMP 约束满足融入智能体规划循环，对非结构化、部分可观测环境至关重要。
items.highlight_zh: 以信念空间规划统一 LVLM 推理与 TAMP 约束满足
items.digest_zh:
1. 问题：让机器人在家里做移动抓取这类任务时，它的视野和知识都不完整（比如抽屉里有什么并不知道）。现有两类办法各有短板：大型视觉语言模型（LVLM）智能体推理能力强，却只会直接调用工具，处理不了空间几何上的不确定性，基本只能在“桌上东西全看得见”的场景里用；任务与运动规划（TAMP）能在信息不全时求解长时程任务，但计算慢，还要求环境封闭已知。
2. 方法：TAMPAgent 把两者结合起来。LVLM 智能体维护一个“信念空间”，也就是对世界可能状态的估计，并可调用一整套感知、规划、控制工具（可扩展 API）。它先给出“半成品”任务计划，只写要观察什么、要执行什么（参数留空），再用经典搜索算法补全；接着从计划中抽出几何约束，用工具 API 绑定满足约束的参数值，得到真正可执行的运动方案。
3. 闭环：执行时机器人不断把观察结果写入信念历史，交替“看一眼—动一下”，反复重规划。
4. 结果：在 Rainbow Y1 和 Unitree G1 两个平台上完成复杂家庭移动操作，明显超过直接调用工具的智能体基线。
5. 意义：说明在非结构化、看不全的真实环境中，把 TAMP 式约束满足引入智能体的规划循环是必要的，而非可有可无的工程细节。

items.title_en: Seeing Through the Illusion: Test-Time Scaling for World Action Models
items.title_zh: 穿透幻象：面向世界动作模型的测试时扩展
items.abstract_en: World action models (WAMs) jointly generate actions and imagined futures, but a plausible prediction need not be realized by its co-generated action. We introduce WISE (\emph{World Action Inference Scaling through Evaluation}), a pre-execution selector that scores each sampled rollout on action validity and temporal regularity, inverse-dynamics consistency between the proposed action and the imagined motion, and instruction-conditioned task progress, and executes the highest-scoring candidate while keeping the WAM frozen. With four candidates per decision, WISE raises closed-loop success from 6.0\% to 24.0\% on RoboLab with Cosmos~3 Edge and from 75.1\% to 78.3\% mean success on LIBERO with DreamZero, and exceeds the best existing selector in aggregate by 4.0 and 0.9 points. Component ablations and agreement analyses show that the three scores rank candidates differently and that task progress carries the largest weight in the fused decision.
items.abstract_zh: 世界动作模型（WAM）同时生成动作与想象的未来，但一个看似合理的预测未必能由与其共同生成的动作真正实现。我们提出 WISE（World Action Inference Scaling through Evaluation），一种执行前选择器：它对每个采样得到的推演轨迹在三个方面打分——动作有效性与时间规律性、所提动作与想象运动之间的逆动力学一致性、以及以指令为条件的任务进展；在保持 WAM 冻结的前提下执行得分最高的候选。每次决策只采四个候选，WISE 便在 RoboLab（Cosmos 3 Edge）上把闭环成功率从 6.0% 提升到 24.0%，在 LIBERO（DreamZero）上把平均成功率从 75.1% 提升到 78.3%，总体比现有最佳选择器分别高出 4.0 和 0.9 个百分点。组件消融与一致性分析表明，三个分数对候选的排序各不相同，且任务进展在融合决策中权重最大。
items.highlight_zh: 执行前给候选轨迹打分筛选，成功率 6.0% 升至 24.0%
items.digest_zh:
1. 问题：世界动作模型（WAM）会一边输出动作，一边“想象”未来画面。但预测看起来合理，不等于配套动作真能做到：模型可能编出一个漂亮却执行不了的结果，闭环执行时就失败。
2. 方法：作者提出 WISE，一个在执行前筛选候选的选择器，WAM 本体完全冻结、不做改动。对同一个决策采样若干条候选轨迹，按三个维度打分：（a）动作本身是否合法、时间上是否平滑规律；（b）所提动作与想象出的运动是否自洽，用逆动力学来检验；（c）任务按指令推进了多少。执行得分最高的那一条。
3. 结果：每次决策只用 4 个候选，RoboLab + Cosmos 3 Edge 上闭环成功率从 6.0% 提升到 24.0%；LIBERO + DreamZero 上平均成功率从 75.1% 提升到 78.3%；总体比现有最好的选择器分别高 4.0 和 0.9 个百分点。
4. 分析：消融和一致性分析显示，三个分数给出的候选排序并不相同，说明它们互相补充；融合时“任务进展”这一项权重最大。
5. 意义：不重训模型，只加一层成本很低的执行前检验，就能显著提升可靠性。这说明“想象的未来”必须被检验，而“多采样 + 打分”这种测试时扩展思路在机器人策略上同样奏效。

items.title_en: Mediating Human-Swarm Interactions Through a Robot Helper: A Shepherding-Inspired Approach
items.title_zh: 通过机器人助手中介人-集群交互：一种牧羊式方法
items.abstract_en: This work investigates human-swarm interaction (HSI) for steering large collectives through an intermediary robot helper. While prior robot-swarm control and HSI techniques commonly assume swarm members are addressable, these assumptions often fail for ``ungovernable'' swarms such as wildlife flocks and schools of fish. Motivated by pastoral shepherding, we compare low-level teleoperation to a higher-autonomy motion-primitives interface in a virtual reality (VR) shepherding task under varied swarm cohesion dynamics. Results indicate that motion primitives that operate on collective shape (e.g., boundary-based control) improve task performance and reduce perceived workload.
items.abstract_zh: 本文研究如何通过一个中介机器人助手来引导大规模集群，即人-集群交互（HSI）。以往机器人-集群控制与 HSI 技术通常假设集群成员可被单独寻址控制，但对野生动物鸟群、鱼群这类“不可治理”的集群往往失效。受牧羊启发，我们在虚拟现实（VR）牧羊任务中比较了底层遥操作与自主性更高的运动基元接口，并考察不同集群内聚动态的影响。结果表明，作用于集体形状的运动基元（如基于边界的控制）能够提升任务表现并降低主观工作负荷。
items.highlight_zh: 用机器人助手中介牧羊式集群控制，形状级接口更具优势
items.digest_zh:
1. 问题：想让一个人同时指挥一大群个体（比如一群鸟、一群鱼或一群机器人）。以往的人-集群交互（HSI）方法通常假设每个成员都能被单独点名控制，但野生动物群这类“不可治理”的集群根本不接受指令，这一假设直接失效。
2. 思路：借鉴牧羊——牧羊人不去指挥每一只羊，而是通过自己的位置和动作把整群“推”向想要的方向。论文让一个机器人充当这种“牧羊犬”式中介，人只操纵这个助手来间接影响集群。
3. 方法：在虚拟现实（VR）中搭建牧羊任务，对比两种人机接口：一种是底层遥操作，人直接精细控制助手的运动；另一种是自主性更高的运动基元接口，人只下达边界、形状等高层指令，由助手自己落实。实验还改变了集群的内聚程度等动态特性。
4. 结果：以集体形状为操作对象（例如基于边界的控制）的运动基元接口，任务完成得更好，人也觉得更省力、负担更小。
5. 意义：说明当人管不过来一大群个体时，把人从底层操控中解放出来、让人只表达“想要什么形状或态势”，是更有效的交互设计方向，对野生动物管理和集群机器人都有参考价值。

items.title_en: When Robots Outweigh Objects: How Inertia Mismatch Shapes Robot Policy Learning
items.title_zh: 当机器人比物体更重：惯性失配如何塑造机器人策略学习
items.abstract_en: Conventional robot arms can be extremely heavy compared with the everyday objects they manipulate, creating a significant inertia mismatch at contact. Even a small accidental bump from a heavy arm can knock a light object out of place. Modern learning methods have nevertheless demonstrated a wide range of successful manipulation behaviors on these platforms, suggesting that even extreme inertia mismatch can be overcome with sufficient data. However, it remains unclear whether high inertia imposes a hidden cost on learning, potentially worsening scaling with data or lowering the performance ceiling of modern robot learning methods. We investigate this question through controlled simulation experiments that vary robot and object masses. We find that reinforcement learning succeeds across a broad range of mass combinations, while behavior cloning learns more reliable policies when a lighter robot manipulates a heavier object, and more data narrows the resulting gap without closing it. Behavior cloning likewise degrades on a simulated robot arm as its motors reflect more inertia through their gearing, even though its weight stays the same. Finally, because new hardware is rarely an option, we explore ways to lower contact inertia on the arm one already has, either by choosing a lower-inertia workspace before collecting data or by steering the demonstrator toward lower-inertia solutions of the task. In both simulated cases, the lower-inertia demonstrations are imitated more reliably. Project website: https://younghyopark.me/inertia-mismatch/

items.title_en: SNAP: Semantic Navigation Among Pedestrians
items.title_zh: SNAP：行人间的语义导航
items.abstract_en: Navigating crowded urban environments requires robots to avoid pedestrians while adhering to social norms such as remaining on sidewalks. Existing approaches typically address either crowd avoidance or semantic path planning in isolation. We propose a reinforcement learning (RL) navigation policy that jointly reasons about semantic terrain and dynamic obstacles from a single semantically annotated bird's-eye-view (BEV) map, without relying on explicit human-state estimation. Our policy outperforms established crowd-navigation and semantic-aware baselines and transfers zero-shot to a legged robot, demonstrating socially compliant navigation in highly dynamic real-world scenarios.

items.title_en: Delay-Certified Readiness Barriers for Overactuated Multirotor Allocation Without Lipschitz Constants
items.title_zh: 无需Lipschitz常数的过驱动多旋翼分配延迟认证就绪屏障
items.abstract_en: Overactuated multirotors can produce the same wrench with many rotor-speed combinations, some of which leave the vehicle unable to change its wrench quickly, e.g., to reject a gust. Readiness barriers keep this ability, the readiness, above a floor, but only in continuous time; with sampled commands and varying speed-controller delays, the available robustness bound covers less than one millisecond. We remove this limit by exploiting the structure of the problem: each rotor responds monotonically and in closed form to its own torque, so the speeds reachable under uncertain switching times lie in a cheaply computed box, and the lowest readiness over that box sits at a corner known in advance. This yields a Lipschitz-free test that a command keeps the readiness above its floor until the next sample, plus a fallback torque that keeps the vehicle on a certified plan. In hexarotor simulations with 2--40~ms delays and $\pm2$~ms jitter, the filter never violated the floor. At $10\pm2$~ms, it matched a delay-compensating predictor within the design envelope and cost 2--30\% more tracking error beyond it, where the predictor alone violated the floor in 2 to 16 of 16 missions.

items.title_en: Exploring Proximity and Tactile Sensing for Robotic Manipulation
items.title_zh: 探索用于机器人操作的接近觉与触觉传感
items.abstract_en: Pre-touch sensing, or sensing information about an object before contact, is an attractive modality for robot hands as it can allow a robot to anticipate and respond to a contact before it happens. In this work, we introduce ToFTouch, a multimodal tactile sensor combining three multizone (4$\times$4 resolution) time-of-flight sensors with an optics-based pressure sensing array. We mount this sensor on a parallel jaw gripper and demonstrate its utility on three distinct tasks: (i) pre-grasp adjustment, (ii) item extraction from clutter, and (iii) item insertion into tight spaces. For pre-grasp adjustment, ToF feedback reduced cycle time by 7.4$\%$ by enabling anticipatory gripper closure during approach. For extraction, ToF sensing enabled successful retrieval across all tested depth offsets ($\pm$2 cm) deviating from the nominal pick point, including conditions where baseline approaches failed, with standard deviations below 0.4 cm. For insertion into dense clutter, we explore the proximity and tactile information provided from ToFTouch during an insertion trajectory. The results demonstrate the utility of multizone ToF sensing in a manipulation environment.

items.title_en: Clinician-AI Collaboration in Endovascular Neurointerventions: In-Vitro User Study of Copilot Assistance Modes for Robotic Navigation Across the Autonomy Spectrum
items.title_zh: 血管内神经介入中的临床医生—AI协作：跨自主谱系的机器人导航Copilot辅助模式体外用户研究
items.abstract_en: Mechanical thrombectomy (MT) is an effective treatment for acute ischemic stroke, yet access remains limited by the availability of neurointerventional expertise. Telerobotic and AI-assisted systems may help address this challenge, but it remains unclear how clinicians interact with different levels of autonomy and how autonomous navigation systems perform in realistic environments. This work introduces Copilot Assistance Modes (CAMs), a framework for clinician-AI collaboration in robotic endovascular navigation spanning the autonomy spectrum from manual operation to full autonomy. In the first in-vitro user study comparing clinician-AI collaboration strategies, 11 experts and two students evaluated six navigation modes in a patient-specific vascular phantom. Objective performance metrics were combined with subjective assessments, including workload and usability. Autonomous performance was additionally evaluated both in silico and in vitro to investigate sim-to-real transfer. Hands-on manual navigation achieved the strongest overall performance (100% success). While fully autonomous navigation achieved 81% success in simulation, performance dropped to 23% in vitro. In contrast, several clinician-AI shared-autonomy modes achieved success rates of 92-97%, approximately four times higher than full autonomy and comparable to direct robotic control (95%), demonstrating mitigation of sim-to-real domain shift through clinician-AI collaboration. Among the evaluated AI-driven approaches, user-directed task delegation and rotational shared control demonstrated the most favorable balance between performance and clinician acceptance. These findings suggest that effective clinician-AI collaboration and allocation of control authority may currently be more important for reliable robotic neurointerventional navigation than increasing autonomy alone.

items.title_en: Toward Uncertainty-Aware, Physics-Grounded Human World Models
items.title_zh: 迈向不确定性感知且基于物理的人类世界模型
items.abstract_en: A robot that acts around people needs a world model of the human: a belief over the person's body state and a dynamics model that predicts where that state goes next. This abstract argues that two published components form exactly these two halves, and specifies how to couple them. KNOWN [1] reconstructs the 3D human body while estimating both aleatoric and epistemic uncertainty in real time (11.6 ms per frame); its aleatoric term identifies unreliable observations, its epistemic term identifies inputs from low-density regions of the training data, and refinement driven by the epistemic term reduces the error on such inputs from 81.3 to 70.3 mm. PhysMoP [2] predicts future body configuration by solving the Euler-Lagrange equations of the body with learned dynamics terms, reducing the 80 ms prediction error from 9.6 to 2.1 mm on Human3.6M and from 12.1 to 0.7 mm on 3DPW. We define the interface between the two, propose three mechanisms by which KNOWN's uncertainty enters PhysMoP, and specify an evaluation protocol on in-the-wild video. No new experimental results are reported here.

items.title_en: Myoelectric Control for Upper-Limb Exoskeletons: A Decoder-Shaper-Controller Framework, Design Guidelines, and Future Directions
items.title_zh: 上肢外骨骼的肌电控制：解码器—整形器—控制器框架、设计指南与未来方向
items.abstract_en: Myoelectric Control Systems (MCSs) enable voluntary control of wearable robots through muscle activity. However, intention decoding, assistance shaping, and low-level actuator control are often not explicitly distinguished, making their contributions difficult to evaluate and compare. This review introduces a functional decoder-shaper-controller framework for continuous myoelectric control of upper-limb exoskeletons. The decoder estimates an intention-related variable from surface electromyography (sEMG), the shaper maps it to a control reference according to an assistance policy, and the controller realizes that reference through actuator control. This decomposition separates intention estimation from assistance-policy design and enables comparison of heterogeneous architectures. Representative approaches are critically examined in terms of module design, calibration, and evaluation. The analysis highlights that the shaper, despite determining the magnitude and shape of assistance, lacks established design and tuning methodologies and is often embedded within the decoder or controller. Key open issues include inconsistent reporting of assistance levels, limited use of interaction-aware stability and passivity tools, and insufficient validation across degrees of freedom, users, and tasks. Building on these findings, this review provides design guidelines for systematic module-wise tuning and identifies future research priorities to bridge the gap between accurate intention decoding and safe, effective, and generalizable assistance under real-world operating conditions.

items.title_en: OpenZilo: An Open Smart-Ring Platform for Human-Centric Sensing and Interaction with Robots
items.title_zh: OpenZilo：面向以人为中心的传感与机器人交互的开放智能戒指平台
items.abstract_en: Wearable robot interfaces must connect user input to timely physical action. We present the proposed platform, an open smart-ring platform for studying this connection across task stages. The ring integrates a microphone, an inertial measurement unit, photoplethysmography, and skin-temperature sensing. Its software architecture separates acquisition, event interpretation, interaction policy, and robot execution. We characterize seven operating modes and evaluate speech and gesture control with 10 participants. Across five commands and 250 trials per modality, speech and gestures achieved task success rates of 90.4% and 88.8%, respectively. Recognition accuracy exceeded task success for both modalities. Gaussian hidden Markov models achieved higher accuracy than a support vector machine across three vocabulary sizes, with longer scoring times. Following a shared spoken task start, gesture-based adjustments had shorter median response times than speech. Whole-task success was 70.0% with gestures and 64.0% with speech. We further examine physiological-event-triggered robot interaction using simulated event notifications. Mean notification-receipt-to-arrival times were 11.71 s for the robot and 9.20 s for an on-site person. These descriptive findings support evaluating wearable robot interfaces through both recognition and physical outcomes, with timing measures appropriate to each task stage.

items.title_en: Safe-Ballbot: Tilt-Consistent MPC with Control Barrier Functions for Ballbot Navigation
items.title_zh: Safe-Ballbot：面向Ballbot导航的基于控制屏障函数的倾角一致性MPC
items.abstract_en: Ball-balancing robots (ballbots) must lean to accelerate, and the lean is limited by the wheel torques and by safety. Planners that use the full robot model are expensive, while planners that ignore the balance dynamics produce references that cannot be followed. This paper presents a two-layer navigation scheme for a three-omni-wheel ballbot. The upper layer is a model predictive controller on a \emph{jerk model} of the ball position, with discrete-time control barrier functions for static, moving, rotating and concave obstacles. The lower layer is a hierarchical sliding mode controller with an extended state observer and a robust exponential control barrier function on the tilt (HSMC-ESO-ECBF). The layers are linked by an acceleration bound derived in closed form from the largest steady tilt that the barrier function admits, so that the plan never asks for a lean the tracker refuses. For obstacles whose motion is only predicted, the obstacles are inflated by conformal prediction radii that bound the prediction error with a prescribed probability. In MuJoCo, with omni-wheel roller contacts and torque saturation, the scheme keeps at least $10$\,cm of clearance, tracks the plan within $2$\,cm RMS, keeps the tilt below the limit and plans in $9$--$12$\,ms, $10$--$15$ times faster than a full-model nonlinear MPC that enters the inflated obstacles; with predicted obstacles, the conformal inflation removes the collisions of a constant-velocity predictor in $30$ random crossing scenarios and reduces them in an endless run on a closed path.The source code and video illustrations are available at https://safe-ballbot.github.io

items.title_en: ForceLDM: A Force-aware Latent Dynamics Model for Contact-Rich Manipulation
items.title_zh: ForceLDM：面向接触丰富操作的力感知潜在动力学模型
items.abstract_en: Contact-rich manipulation requires fine-grained control and complex physical interactions with the environment, posing significant challenges for robot policy learning. Vision-only policies struggle with such tasks, as contact states and interaction forces are difficult to infer from visual observations alone. Existing methods mitigate this issue by incorporating force or tactile sensing. However, they often treat these signals as auxiliary observations without fully exploiting their role in modeling future interaction dynamics. To address this, we propose ForceLDM, a force-aware latent dynamics model that learns future contact and motion dynamics to guide action generation. Rather than directly predicting future observations, which can entangle task-relevant dynamics with irrelevant sensory details, ForceLDM learns a compact representation of future dynamics through knowledge distillation. Specifically, a teacher network with privileged future force/torque and optical flow signals extracts future dynamic features, which are then distilled into a student network trained only on current observations. This enables the student model to reason about upcoming contacts and physical dynamics without relying on future sensory inputs at deployment. To improve robustness and generalization, we further introduce a curriculum-based progressive noise injection strategy to mitigate over-reliance on future features. Experiments on five real-world contact-rich manipulation tasks demonstrate that ForceLDM outperforms state-of-the-art baselines, generalizes effectively to novel objects, and remains robust to environmental perturbations. Project page and code are available at https://tpy001.github.io/ForceLDM/.

items.title_en: VerifLM: Physically Verified Image-Edit-Guided Goal Pose Generation for Robotic Manipulation
items.title_zh: VerifLM：面向机器人操作的物理验证图像编辑引导目标位姿生成
items.abstract_en: Many manipulation goals are easier to visualize than to specify numerically through explicit geometric constraints. We present VerifLM, a framework that converts image-edited goal configurations into physically verified 6-DoF object poses for planning. Using an edited image, VerifLM recovers an initial relative pose between an active object and a passive object, then prompts a vision-language model to generate axis-wise sampling constraints and a task-specific validation program. Candidate poses are evaluated in a physics simulator, and the VLM selects the most task-consistent retained candidate. To operate without predefined object meshes or physical parameters, VerifLM reconstructs metric object geometry from RGB-D observations and constructs multiple hypothetical simulations with varying physics and geometry. Parallel-world validation evaluates candidates across geometry--physics variations and ranks them by the number of worlds in which they satisfy the validation program. We evaluate VerifLM on nine manipulation tasks. VerifLM achieves the highest task success on eight of nine tasks, with the largest performance gain on goals requiring precise orientation and contact relationships.

items.title_en: TRAILS: Trajectory Generation for Automated Indoor Locomotion Studies
items.title_zh: TRAILS：面向自动化室内移动研究的轨迹生成
items.abstract_en: Virtual reality experiments involving navigation and simulated robot motion often require large, realistic environments and numerous distinct trajectories to avoid repetitive navigation while providing sufficient variation for controlled experiments. Designing such scenarios manually is labor-intensive, particularly when trajectories must satisfy predefined geometric and kinematic constraints while remaining diverse and comparable across experimental conditions. This paper presents TRAILS, an automated framework for generating complete virtual navigation scenarios consisting of an environment layout, a path, and a time-parameterized motion profile. The framework combines a constraint-based procedural environment generator inspired by Wave Function Collapse, trajectory generation using optimized cubic Bézier curves, and speed-profile generation subject to kinematic constraints. The generated scenarios provide diverse indoor environments with corridors, open spaces, and obstacles, together with trajectories of identical duration that vary in path geometry, wall proximity, and velocity profiles while minimizing systematic dependencies between these characteristics. The framework is designed as an easy-to-use tool requiring only a small number of intuitive user-defined parameters to automatically generate large sets of distinct navigation scenarios satisfying prescribed geometric and kinematic constraints. By relying on explicit, seed-controlled algorithmic procedures rather than data-driven models, the generated scenarios remain transparent, reproducible, and configurable, making the framework well suited for telepresence and human-subject experiments. The code is available at https://github.com/JucciK/Trails .

items.title_en: Towards end-to-end co-design for one-shot printable task-specific soft robots
items.title_zh: 面向单次可打印的任务专用软机器人的端到端协同设计
items.abstract_en: Soft robot co-design methods can jointly optimise morphology and control, but the resulting designs are often difficult to manufacture, while manufacturable approaches typically restrict actuator placement or require manual assembly. We present a simulation-based co-design framework that jointly optimises material distribution, pneumatic actuator placement and orientation, and control, while producing designs that can be fabricated monolithically using fused deposition modelling. The framework uses a differentiable 2D plane-stress Material Point Method simulator, incorporating an experimentally validated material model and an empirically derived surrogate model of a 3D-printed inflatable actuator. We demonstrate gradient-based optimisation soft robotic arms for prescribed tip trajectories. Optimised designs are transferred directly from simulation to one-shot monolithic FDM fabrication, with integrated actuators and no post-assembly. Physical experiments demonstrate that the resulting arms reproduce the behaviour predicted in simulation. This framework provides a path from task-level objectives to physically realisable soft robots while retaining substantial freedom over both morphology and actuation.

items.title_en: Rollout then Recycle: 3,718 Labelled Real-Robot Episodes from Benchmarking 7 Policies on 12 Tasks
items.title_zh: Rollout then Recycle：在12项任务上基准测试7种策略所获的3,718条带标注真实机器人回合
items.abstract_en: We release all 3,718 episodes from the ArmnetBench v0.1 evaluation (arXiv:2607.24481), which contains 600 teleoperated demonstrations and 3,118 rollouts of seven imitation-learning and vision-language-action policies on 12 tabletop tasks, recorded on low-cost SO-101 arms; 73% of the rollouts are failures. Every policy for a task was trained or fine-tuned on the same 50 demonstrations and rolled out on the same cell, so the corpus contains many policies' failures on shared tasks. An operator labelled every rollout successful, suboptimal or failure. Each episode has three camera views, joint states and actions and is available on the Hugging Face Hub in LeRobot v3.0 and a reward-model format. This note documents how the episodes were collected and the limitations that could affect their use.

items.title_en: FineCraft: Enhancing VLA Models for Fine-Grained Manipulation
items.title_zh: FineCraft：面向细粒度操作增强VLA模型
